# Polaris — Architecture Reference

Deep reference material extracted from CLAUDE.md. This file is **not** auto-loaded into Claude Code sessions — read it on demand when a task touches one of the areas below.

For the always-loaded project memory (conventions, business rules, env vars, deployment, RBAC overview, getting started, common tasks, out of scope, cross-cutting rules), see [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md). For relationship/dependency lookups across services, see [TOUCHES.md](TOUCHES.md). For canonical implementation references when building a new instance of an existing pattern, see [TEMPLATES.md](TEMPLATES.md).

## Architecture

```
polaris/
├── CLAUDE.md
├── TOUCHES.md                       # Lookup index: per-service writers/readers/invariants + 6 cross-cutting concerns. Reviewed alongside CLAUDE.md on every commit per "Before any commit, review CLAUDE.md, TOUCHES.md, and TEMPLATES.md for updates" — keeps regression-prone relationships visible without rereading every consumer.
├── TEMPLATES.md                     # Canonical-implementation index: when there are multiple ways to build the same thing (chart, modal, slide-over, sortable table, …), this names the reference implementation new work should match. Reviewed alongside CLAUDE.md and TOUCHES.md on every commit so canonicals don't go stale.
├── README.md
├── .env.example
├── package.json
├── tsconfig.json
├── prisma.config.ts                 # Prisma 7 config (datasource URL, seed command)
├── prisma/
│   ├── schema.prisma                # Database schema
│   └── seed.ts
├── docs/
│   ├── INSTALL.md                   # Fresh-install guide (RHEL/Rocky/AlmaLinux 9, Ubuntu/Debian, Windows Server). Includes disk-sizing requirements per volume (DB ≥50 GB, app/state ≥5 GB, /var/log ≥5 GB on STIG layouts) and recovery steps for the "/var is full and Postgres is crash-looping" case. Don't follow this for upgrades — those use the in-app updater under Server Settings → Maintenance → Updates.
│   └── fmg-discovery.md             # FortiManager discovery decision tree (operator-facing): transport mode (proxy vs direct), roster filtering, per-class stamping for FortiGates / FortiSwitches / FortiAPs, push toggles, projection apply. Companion to the phase-by-phase narrative in CLAUDE.md's "FMG Discovery Workflow" section.
├── scripts/
│   ├── test-fmg.mjs                 # FortiManager integration test harness
│   ├── audit-multi-mac-assets.ts    # One-off: unstitch assets cross-stapled by old IP-fallback bug
│   ├── check-fmg-tokens.ts          # One-off: print stored FMG/FortiGate token length/prefix to diagnose token corruption
│   ├── fetch-std-mibs.mjs           # Repopulate src/services/stdMibs/<MODULE>.txt by fetching the eleven canonical standard MIBs (SNMPv2-MIB / IF-MIB / HOST-RESOURCES-MIB / ENTITY-MIB / ENTITY-SENSOR-MIB / LLDP-MIB / POWER-ETHERNET-MIB / BRIDGE-MIB / Q-BRIDGE-MIB / RSTP-MIB). Per-module `mirror` field selects the source: pysnmp.com for the original seven, the netdisco-mibs `rfc/` tree for the four switch physical-layer modules (pysnmp was returning HTTP 522 when they were added; each was verified against its published RFC and by canonical-OID resolution). Writes SHA-256 + the actual source URL into SOURCES.md alongside the files. Run when refreshing the bundle; existing files are overwritten in place.
│   ├── copy-build-assets.mjs        # BUILD STEP (not ad-hoc): second half of `npm run build` (tsc && node scripts/copy-build-assets.mjs). Mirrors non-.ts runtime assets that tsc won't emit — today the stdMibs/*.txt files — into dist/services/stdMibs/. Without it, every std SNMP-walk (LLDP-MIB etc.) on a built install fails with "Standard MIB ... is not installed on the server", because stdMibLibrary.ts reads the files relative to its compiled location (dist/). Fails the build if it copies 0 files. Every build site invokes `npm run build` so the copy is guaranteed; see cross-cutting/deployment in TOUCHES.md.
│   └── smoke-std-mibs.ts            # Spot-check that each bundled std MIB parses + resolves to its canonical OIDs (sysDescr=1.3.6.1.2.1.1.1, lldpRemTable=1.0.8802.1.1.2.1.4.1, etc.). Backstop for the resolver + parser; vitest unit tests in tests/unit/stdMibLibrary.test.ts cover the same ground formally.
├── public/                          # Vanilla JS frontend (served statically)
│   ├── index.html                   # Dashboard — operator-customizable widget canvas (SolarWinds-style column layout). Read-only by default; a "Customize Page" button (top-right) enters EDIT MODE ("Add Widgets" + "Done Editing"). The dashboard is an ordered list of COLUMNS (each a 12-grid width 3/4/6/12) holding a vertical stack of widgets (height step 1–3 → 280/576/872px). In edit mode: "Add Widgets" opens the full picker (translucent overlay with the dashboard dimmed behind it, a Group-By category list, search, name sort, and a ★ favorite toggle per widget — favorites in localStorage via favorites.js); drag a widget (from the picker or an existing one) → a green "+" insertion placeholder marks the slot and a trailing "+ New block" target accepts drops into a fresh column; the dragged widget lifts with a shadow. Per-column width selector (¼/⅓/½/Full) + remove-column ×; per-widget a ⠿ drag handle (moves the widget to any column), a 1×/2×/3× height cycle, gear config (besides per-widget options, every NOC widget carries a **Regions** scope — All regions / My regions / Selected regions…, narrowing to the caller's effective `regionTags` or to a per-widget checkbox pick of the created region names (list fed by `/dashboard/filter-options` via the memoized `PolarisWidgets.getRegionOptions()`); newly-added widgets default to **My regions** (an unrestricted caller with no effective regions still sees everything), and the unauthenticated /dash wallboard hides **My regions** — no viewer identity to resolve it against — leaving All / Selected regions — and every NOC widget except the Status Map carries an **Asset types** toggle grid over the eight built-in types, default all on; both rendered by the shared `PolarisWidgets.renderNocFilterConfig`, threaded to the server as `?assetTypes=&regionTags=` so the payload is memoized per filter; every severity-bearing widget (Down Assets, Down Interfaces, Storage Forecast, the six top-N widgets, Active Alerts) additionally carries a **Minimum severity** select — All rows (default) / Notice / Informational / Warning / Serious and up / Critical only, the same ladder the ⤓ CSV export tiers use — that narrows the widget to rows whose device carries an active alert at or above that severity, filtered client-side before the row limit / header count / export (any tier past "All rows" therefore hides un-alerted rows, which the popover hint states); when the asset-type filter selects a strict subset, the chosen types appear in the widget's header title in parens, e.g. "Highest Avg CPU (Server, Switch)"), and remove ×. The page top bar is frozen (sticky `.page-header-sticky`) so Add Widgets / Done Editing / search stay reachable while the widgets scroll. The dashboard supports **multiple named dashboards as tabs** (layout schema v3: `{version:3, dashboards:[{id,name,columns}], activeId}`, max 24; v1/v2 layouts migrate client-side into a single "Dashboard 1" tab on load) — a "Create New Dashboard" button (right of "Customize Page") adds a tab, click a tab to switch, click the active tab's name to rename it inline, and remove via its × in edit mode. Layouts persist server-side per user (PUT /me/dashboard, debounced 800ms; "Done Editing" forces a save). Widget catalog: Recently Reserved, Assets by Type, Block Utilization (each fetches only its own /dashboard/summary section — `?sections=` — via the 15s-memoized `PolarisWidgets.getSummary({sections,...})`); the SolarWinds-style NOC set — Status Summary, Down Assets, Highest Avg CPU, Highest Avg Memory, Slowest Response, Packet Loss, Highest Disk Usage, Highest Temperature, Stale Polls, Recent Reboots, Active Alerts, Sites with Issues, Status Map (each fetches only its own /dashboard/noc-summary feed — `?feeds=` — via the 15s-memoized `PolarisWidgets.getNocSummary(opts, feeds)`, so a widget renders as soon as ITS query returns instead of gating on the slowest feed; Status Map uses /map/sites); plus role-gated Stale Reservations / Capacity Health / Discovery Activity / Conflict Queue. Each widget module under `public/js/widgets/` self-registers with `PolarisWidgets.register()` and exposes a `renderPreview` (mock-data mini for the library), `renderInstance` (full canvas render), and optional `renderConfig` (gear popover contents).
│   ├── login.html
│   ├── setup.html                   # First-run wizard
│   ├── ipam.html                    # IPAM tabbed surface — folds the legacy /blocks.html + /subnets.html pages into one sidebar entry. Tabs: IP Blocks | Networks. Hash-routed (`#tab=blocks|networks`, `#tab=networks&block=<id>`, `#tab=networks&subnet=<id>[&focusReservation=<id>]`). Each tab's markup lives in a `<template>` element; the orchestrator (`public/js/ipam.js`) clones one template into `#ipam-mount` at a time because the two tab markups share several DOM IDs (filter-pagesize, pagination, pagination-top). `public/js/blocks.js` and `public/js/subnets.js` are loaded once but expose `window.PolarisBlocks.init()` / `window.PolarisSubnets.init()` and suppress their own DOMContentLoaded auto-run when `window.__polarisIpamTabs=true` is set (ipam.html sets it before they load). Legacy /blocks.html and /subnets.html URLs are redirected client-side via tiny HTML stubs served by Express (`legacyIpamRedirect` in src/app.ts) so existing fragments (`#ip=<sid>@<ip>`, `#view=…`) are preserved across the hop.
│   ├── blocks.html                  # Legacy — bookmarked URLs hit a server-side stub that redirects to /ipam.html#tab=blocks while preserving the original fragment. The file itself is still here so any tooling that fetches it for content keeps working; the runtime path is the stub.
│   ├── subnets.html                 # Legacy — same redirect treatment as blocks.html; targets /ipam.html#tab=networks.
│   ├── assets.html
│   ├── integrations.html
│   ├── events.html
│   ├── users.html
│   ├── server-settings.html
│   ├── (logo.png)                   # RETIRED 2026-08 — replaced by the themed marks below. Every favicon is now a two-link `prefers-color-scheme` pair (browser chrome follows the OS, not Polaris's data-theme), the PWA icon source is `img/brand/polaris-symbol-dark.png` (light ink, because every opaque icon variant paints ICON_BG and iOS composites onto black), and `BRANDING_DEFAULTS.logoUrl` points at that same file. `/logo.png` is still recognised by `isDefaultLogoUrl` because installs seeded before the cutover store it in their branding row — see brandingService.DEFAULT_LOGO_URLS.
│   ├── img/brand/                   # Polaris brand art, one file per (orientation, theme): `polaris-horiz-{dark,light}.png` (login card) + `polaris-vert-{dark,light}.png` (sidebar) + `polaris-symbol-{dark,light}.png` (the star alone — the accent overlay brandLogoService composites onto an operator's logo). "dark"/"light" name the BACKGROUND the file is for, not its ink: the dark-theme wordmark is light blue, the light-theme one near-black, so painting the wrong variant makes the logo vanish. The symbol pair splits the same way for a different reason — the dark variant's wedges are WHITE and the light variant's are NAVY, so on the wrong background half the mark disappears and the star reads as four disconnected arms. Chosen by public/js/brand-logo.js off `data-theme`. Downscaled from the source art (900×180 horiz / 600×512 vert / 512² symbol) — the originals are ~6000px and 120–400 KB each, which is a real cost on the pre-auth login page. **Also NORMALIZED across the pair, which the source exports were not:** the vertical light file's star was ~39% larger relative to its wordmark than the dark file's, with a 2px star/wordmark gap against the dark's 20px, so simply scaling each to a common width still rendered two visibly different logos. Both variants are now laid out to one geometry — star scaled to 371px high at y≈3, wordmark to 116px high at y=396, each centered — so swapping them on a theme flip moves nothing. Re-exported art must be re-normalized the same way (measure the alpha bounding box of each band, don't trust the export's packing); when doing it by compositing bands out of one source image, clip each band's layer to its OWN target rect — a clip with slack lets the other band show through at the wrong scale, which renders a small ghost wordmark above the real one.
│   ├── map.html                     # Device Map page (Leaflet basemap + Cytoscape topology modal)
│   ├── mobile.html                  # Phone-targeted SPA (Material 3). Single document, hash-routed, reuses /api/v1 + session auth from the desktop app. Phone-class user-agents hitting `/` or `/index.html` are auto-redirected here by the UA middleware in `src/app.ts`; the `?desktop=1` query param is the escape hatch the More tab's "Desktop view" link uses to bypass the redirect.
│   ├── dash.html                    # Dash wallboard — the UNAUTHENTICATED read-only duplicate of index.html's dashboard, served at /dash by the dash process (src/dash/dashServer.ts). Same widget canvas/picker markup + full widget script list (keep in lockstep with index.html — both files carry a comment); loads js/dash-mode.js FIRST (page flags: POLARIS_DASH_LOCAL, __polarisApiBase=/dash/api/v1, __polarisOn401 no-op) and js/dash-boot.js INSTEAD of app.js (slim boot: theme, synthetic /auth/me identity globals, permAtLeast, showToast/timeAgo copies, branding incl. title + favicon swap to branding.logoUrl, mirroring app.js applyBranding). No sidebar, no asset slide-over chain (table-sf/integrations/assets/jspdf/html-to-image dropped — widget click-throughs no-op via the POLARIS_DASH_LOCAL guard in widgets/index.js openAssetDetail). Layout persists per-browser in localStorage `polaris-dash-layout` (dashboard.js branches on POLARIS_DASH_LOCAL instead of /me/dashboard). Widgets the readonly role can't read (Discovery Activity / Conflict Queue / Capacity Health) hide via getAllowed().
│   ├── css/
│   │   ├── styles.css
│   │   ├── map.css                  # Device Map styles (marker icons, topology modal grid)
│   │   ├── mobile.css               # Material 3 component library for mobile.html. Defines both dark (`:root`) and light (`[data-theme="light"]`) MD3 token blocks — every component rule reads `var(--md-...)` so a theme flip swaps surfaces, primaries, and outlines without per-component branching. Status colors (monitor health pills, topology node hues defined in topology-render.js) deliberately stay literal — they need the same hue on both backgrounds for at-a-glance recognition. The GPS pin stroke flips per theme via `--user-pin-stroke` (near-white on dark, near-black on light) so the stick figure stays legible against either basemap. Also carries: `.user-pin` styles + walking keyframes for the Map tab's GPS pin (CSS keyframes alternate left/right limb rotations + a body-bob; honors `prefers-reduced-motion`); `.topo-screen` / `.topo-bar` / `.topo-search` / `.topo-graph` / `.topo-section` styles for the mobile topology surface; `.app[data-tab="__fullbleed"]` rule that hides the topbar slot + bottom navbar so the topology graph owns the whole viewport; landscape-orientation lockout (`@media (orientation: landscape) and (max-height: 480px)`) that replaces the UI with a "Rotate to portrait" overlay — universal fallback for iOS Safari which silently rejects `screen.orientation.lock()` outside an installed PWA. Also carries the `.app.kb-open` rules the auth screens' keyboard fit toggles — the `justify-content: flex-start` flip there is load-bearing, since overflow above a centered flex item is unreachable.
│   │   └── vendor/leaflet/          # Leaflet + markercluster + leaflet-draw 1.0.4 CSS + marker PNGs + draw spritesheet (bundled; CSP blocks external CDN)
│   └── js/
│       ├── api.js                   # HTTP client with auth/error handling. 401 redirect goes to /login.html unless `window.__polarisOn401` is set (mobile app sets this to route back to its in-app login).
│       ├── app.js                   # Navigation, layout, theme switching
│       ├── brand-logo.js            # `window.PolarisBrandLogo` — which mark a surface paints, in one place, because the desktop login, the mobile login and the sidebar all have to agree. `resolve(branding, "login"|"sidebar")` → `{src, custom, showName, showSubtitle}`: the shipped art picked per `data-theme` (horizontal for the login card, vertical for the sidebar), an operator's logo when `customLogo` and that surface's `logoOnLogin`/`logoOnSidebar` flag is on (pointing at the server-composited `logo-accent.png` when `logoAccent`), and `showName` FALSE for the Polaris art — the wordmark is in the picture, so a caption would repeat it. `applyTo(img, …, {bust})` also tags the element `.brand-mark` so CSS can size fixed-aspect art differently from an arbitrary upload; `bust` is how the Customization tab forces a re-fetch of an accent URL whose bytes changed but whose path didn't. `onThemeChange` observes the `data-theme` attribute rather than hooking each surface's toggle, and the module registers the `prefers-color-scheme` listener that keeps a user who has never picked a theme tracking their OS. Loaded before app.js on every page, plus login.html and mobile.html.
│       ├── dashboard.js              # Dashboard orchestrator (column layout v2). Owns `state.layout = {version:2, columns:[{id,width,widgets:[{id,type,height,config}]}]}` + `state.editing`, loads from `GET /me/dashboard`, migrates a legacy v1 (`{widgets:[{col,row,...}]}`) layout to columns on load (`migrateV1ToV2`: bucket by col-start, order by row), and renders each column as a CSS-grid item (`grid-column: span width`) holding a flex stack. Edit mode (`enterEditMode`/`exitEditMode`) toggles `.is-editing` + re-renders so drag handles / controls / the "+ New block" target appear. Drag (picker card OR existing widget) computes a `{columnIndex, insertionIndex}` or `{newColumn}` target via `dropTargetFromCursor` (column + card-midpoint geometry), moves a single green "+" `.dashboard-drop-placeholder` into the target stack, and lifts the source with `.lifted`. Mutations (`addWidgetAt`/`moveWidgetTo`/`removeWidget`/`removeColumn`/`setColumnWidth`/`setWidgetHeight`) rewrite `columns[]`, drop emptied columns, re-render, and debounce a `PUT /me/dashboard` (800ms; "Done Editing" forces the save). `renderWidget` (per-widget mount: `fetchData`→`renderInstance`→`ctx.onUnmount`) is unchanged from v1, and additionally attaches `startAutoScroll` (read-only mode only) — a NOC-style slow auto-scroll (`noc.rogersgroupinc.com`: ~3s top pause, 1px/80ms creep, ~3s bottom dwell, glide-home loop) that activates only when a widget's content overflows and pauses while the operator hovers it. Widgets own their data fetches (`fetchData(config)`) — there is no orchestrator-prefetched shared payload; the per-feed/per-section memoized accessors in `widgets/index.js` (`getNocSummary` / `getSummary`) dedupe same-key fetches across widgets. Also owns the **first-run welcome modal** (`maybeShowWelcomeModal`): after `userReady`, admins landing on the dashboard of a not-yet-set-up instance (zero IP blocks OR zero integrations) get a getting-started `openModal` (add a block → carve networks → connect an integration, with done-state checkmarks and a context-sensitive CTA to IPAM or Integrations); shows once per user per browser via `localStorage` `polaris.welcome.dismissed.<username>`, stamped at show time so any close path counts as seen.
│       ├── widget-library.js         # "Add Widgets" picker (SolarWinds-style). `WidgetLibrary.open/close/isOpen`. A translucent full-height overlay (`.widget-picker-overlay`, dashboard dimmed behind) docks a panel with a Group-By list (`All` / `★ Favorites` / each widget `category` with counts), a search box, a name sort, and the available-widgets list. Cards keep `.widget-library-card` + `data-type` + `draggable` + live `renderPreview` so the orchestrator's drag/drop + click-to-add are unchanged; each card adds a `.widget-fav-star` (favorites via favorites.js entity `"widgetlib"`, localStorage per-user). Filter = category ∩ search; favorites pinned to top. Permission-filtered via `PolarisWidgets.getAllowed()`.
│       ├── widgets/                  # Per-widget modules. `index.js` is the registry + shared helpers (`PolarisWidgets.register`, `getAll`, `getAllowed`, `uuid`, `durationSince`, `ASSET_TYPE_LABELS/COLORS`, `BUILTIN_ASSET_TYPES` (the eight built-ins, display order), `getNocSummary(opts, feeds)` — 15s-memoized `/dashboard/noc-summary` accessor **keyed by (feeds, per-widget filter)** (asset types + region scope + the widget's `?feeds=` subset), so two widgets sharing a feed + filter make one fetch while each widget pulls only the feed(s) it renders (renders as soon as its own query returns); `getSummary({sections, sourceTypes, recentLimit})` — the same memo pattern over `/dashboard/summary?sections=` for the IP-space widgets; `nocFilterOpts(config)` (pulls `{assetTypes, regionScope, regions, fortigateScope, fortigates, sampleCount}` off a widget config — `sampleCount` is sent as `?samples=` only when it deviates from the server default of 10, so default-config widgets share one cached payload; `fortigates` is sent as `?fortigates=` only when fortigateScope="custom" and the pick is non-empty), `myRegionNames()` (the caller's effective region names), `regionNamesForConfig(config)` (resolves a widget's region scope — custom pick / mine / null=unfiltered — for the map widgets' direct `/map/sites` fetches), `getRegionOptions()` / `getFortigateOptions()` (created-region names / live-gate `{name, regions}` entries off one shared memoized `/dashboard/filter-options` fetch), `renderNocFilterConfig(el, config, onChange, includeAssetTypes)` — appends the shared **Regions** scope select (+ the Selected-regions checkbox list) and, when includeAssetTypes, a **FortiGates** scope select (All / Selected FortiGates checkbox list — narrows to assets behind the picked gates for one-site dashboards, with a "(No FortiGate)" entry = the `__none__` sentinel for gate-less devices; the offered gate list itself narrows LIVE to the popover's current region selection via each gate's own region tags, repainting on region changes and pruning picks the re-filtered list no longer shows; rendered single-column + scroll-capped (`.widget-config-fglist`) since device hostnames overflow the two-column grid; skipped for the map widgets, which fetch `/map/sites` and don't ride the noc-summary filter) + the **Asset types** toggle grid into a gear popover — `setHeaderExport(el, {columns, rows, filename?, severityOf?})` — stamps a ⤓ CSV-export button on the widget header whose menu exports the widget's FULL pre-clip listing filtered by severity tier (All rows / Critical only / Serious and up / Warning and up, live per-tier counts, empty tiers disabled): rows filter on each row's active-alert severity via `PolarisWidgets.ALERT_SEVERITY_RANK` (client mirror of nocDashboardService's ladder, audit-Event levels folded in at error=critical / info=informational), a trailing Severity column is appended, the filename defaults from the widget's `data-type` (`polaris-top-cpu-critical-<date>.csv`), and the download uses app.js `downloadCsv` with a local fallback for the Dash wallboard; wired on Active Alerts / Down Assets / Down Interfaces / Storage Forecast + all six top-N widgets (once, inside `_topnBar.renderRows`); the outside-click/Escape/page-scroll dismiss deliberately ignores scrolls inside `.dashboard-widget-body` so the NOC auto-scroll can't close an open menu — the **minimum-severity display filter** helpers `SEVERITY_TIERS` (the one operator-facing tier ladder over `ALERT_SEVERITY_RANK`, least→most severe: All rows / Notice / Informational / Warning / Serious and up / Critical only — the export menu's four tiers are taken off this same list so the two can't drift), `minSeverityRank(config)`, `filterByMinSeverity(rows, config[, severityOf])` (rows at/above `config.minSeverity`; defaults to `row.alertSeverity`, Active Alerts passes its own alert severity), `severityTierForRank(rank)` (the inverse — folds a pre-control config's rank floor back to a tier), `minSeverityEmptyText(config)` (tier-named empty state so a filtered-empty widget doesn't read as "nothing is wrong"; null at tier "all"), `minSeverityOptionsHTML(current)` and `renderMinSeverityConfig(el, config, onChange, hint?)` (appends the **Minimum severity** select + its caveat hint `.widget-config-hint` to a gear popover, called between the widget's own controls and `renderNocFilterConfig`) — and `openAssetDetail(id)` — opens the canonical asset slide-in in place via the global `openViewModal` (from assets.js, which `index.html` now loads alongside its deps — jspdf / html-to-image / table-sf / integrations — mirroring `map.html`), falling back to `/assets.html#view=asset:` navigation when unavailable). `_topnBar.js` is a non-registering shared renderer (`window.PolarisTopN`) for the four metric widgets; its `renderRows` takes an optional `fillTo` = red-guarantee mode (CPU/Memory/Disk/Response): the operator's **Row limit governs how many rows show** (top-N by value, default 20), except every **red** row — at/above the top color threshold, ≥90% or ≥500 ms — always shows even past the limit, so an alert can't be clipped away; `fillTo` is the fallback count when the config has no usable rowLimit. The ellipsizing name cell carries a native `title` tooltip with the full hostname (+ mount detail on Disk Usage). There is no per-widget numeric "hide below" floor on any of them — the gear's Minimum severity control is the display filter, and the red guarantee supersedes a floor anyway (the plumbing was removed 2026-08; a stored `threshold` is ignored); Packet Loss omits `fillTo`, so its rowLimit is a plain cap. All six top-N widgets share a gear **Group by** control (None default / Site): grouping happens AFTER ranking + row-limit + red-guarantee (presentation only — never changes which rows qualify), buckets under the same group-header markup Down Assets uses (neutral count pill — rankings, not alarms), groups ordered by their hottest row; the per-row `site` label is hydrated server-side in `nocDashboardService` (`TopNRow.site`, same location > learnedLocation > snmpLocation coalesce as Down Assets) so buckets match across widgets. IPAM/system widgets each fetch their own /dashboard/summary section via `PolarisWidgets.getSummary({sections})`: `recentReservations.js` (sections=recent + its source-type/limit params), `assetTypes.js` (sections=assetTypes), `blockUtilization.js` (sections=blocks). NOC widgets (`assets:read`, `events:read` for recentReboots, `alerts:read` for activeAlerts): `statusSummary.js` (status tiles + uptime% + alert count), `downNodes.js` (**Down Assets** — the registered type stays `downNodes`, which is what saved layouts key on; down assets grouped by site/division, dependency-suppressed assets excluded unless the gear's **Include dependency-down assets** toggle is on — which sends `?includeDependencyDown=1` and badges each suppressed row "Dep. Down" so the two kinds stay tellable apart, overall TRUE down count from `downNodesTotal` stamped as a header count pill via the shared `PolarisWidgets.setHeaderPills(el, pills)` family: `setHeaderCount(el, count[, severity])` renders a single total — the optional `severity` (from `PolarisWidgets.maxAlertSeverity(rows)`, the set's most severe active alert) colors the pill off the same `ALERT_SEV_PILL` palette the per-row severity pills use, so a group of `serious` rows reads orange instead of critical-red, and the per-group count pills take the same color via `PolarisWidgets.countPillClass(rows)` — both fall back to red when no row carries an alert; `setHeaderSeverityCounts(el, rows[, {unalerted, severityOf}])` renders the per-severity BREAKDOWN instead — one pill per active-alert severity in the set (counted by `alertSeverityCounts`), most severe first, each colored to its own severity, and is **universal since 2026-08** across every widget whose rows carry a severity: the six `_topnBar` top-N widgets + Storage Forecast, Down Assets, Down Interfaces, Recent Reboots, Sites with Issues and Active Alerts. **Each caller passes the rows it is about to RENDER** — post minimum-severity filter, post row limit / horizon / red guarantee — so the pills count what's on screen (a 10-row panel over a 40-node outage reads 10); the ⤓ export provider deliberately stays on the full matched set, so its tier counts and the header pills can legitimately differ. `unalerted:"neutral"` (Down Assets / Down Interfaces — a trailing grey pill counts the rendered non-alerting rows so the pills sum to the visible list, and a set with no alerting row at all falls back to the plain red total) vs `unalerted:"omit"` (the ranked top-N family + Sites with Issues + Recent Reboots + Active Alerts, whose row count is the operator's Row limit rather than a fleet total, so a grey bucket would be noise). Down Assets' header no longer shows the server's uncapped `downNodesTotal` (the payload still carries it); Sites with Issues counts SITES at a severity, not nodes; Active Alerts passes `severityOf` for the raising automation's severity and stamps from its 25-row display slice. `setHeaderTierCounts(el, rows, {keyOf, order, classOf, noun})` is the same breakdown for a widget with its OWN severity vocabulary — **Capacity health** over its ok/watch/amber/red reasons, kept generic rather than teaching `ALERT_SEVERITY_RANK` a second ladder that would then rank against automation severities in the min-severity filter and export tiers. **Stale Polls** has no pills by design: its feed passes `{kind:"none"}` relevance server-side (no automation matches "overdue for a poll"), so its rows carry no severity at all; clicking a node opens its asset details slide-in **in place** over the dashboard via `PolarisWidgets.openAssetDetail`, ctrl/meta/middle-click still opens the Assets page in a new tab), `topCpu.js` / `topMemory.js` / `slowestResponse.js` / `packetLoss.js` / `diskUsage.js` / `temperature.js` (top-N bar lists via `_topnBar`; `diskUsage.js` is **per-volume** — one row per (asset, mountPath) with the mount shown as the row's muted `detail`; `temperature.js` ("Highest Temperature") is **per-sensor** — one row per (asset, sensorName) from the temperature-class hardware sensors, sensor name as the `detail`, °C values, red guarantee at ≥80 °C), `stalePolls.js`, `recentReboots.js`, `activeAlerts.js` (one row per uncleared Notification, severity-first then newest: the automation's name titles the row with the device beside it and the alert message below, an acknowledged alert stays listed but dims and wears an "ack" pill since it is still active, and the pill/bar palette is the automation ladder's own — serious is orange, distinct from critical red), `sitesWithIssues.js` (expandable), `siteMap.js` (labeled "Status Map"; The status-pill popover paints synchronously, so `assets.js` warms the same cache at `DOMContentLoaded`. │       ├── topology-render.js        # Shared Cytoscape element + stylesheet builders consumed by both desktop map.js and mobile topology-tab.js. Exposes `buildTopologyElements(data)`, `topologyStylesheet(theme, opts)`, `topologyLegendSpec()`, `computeTopologyColumns(elements)`, and `computeGroupedLayout(elements)` (quotient two-level layout for location-coded sites: per-group rank-compressed interiors + height-budgeted shelf packing of group boxes; returns the same {depth,lane} contract or null on untagged sites) so node colors per monitor health, edge styles for controller / interface-inferred / LLDP / mesh edges, ghost LLDP nodes, cross-site remote assets, and operator-uploaded icons stay consistent across surfaces. FG→switch controller edges are labeled with the real port pair (`srcIf.name ↔ tgtIf.name`, post trunk→member swap) when the edge is `verifiedUplink` AND the server attached interface details on both ends; otherwise they fall back to the logical `fortilink` label (dashed gray when unverified). **`computeTopologyColumns` is the deterministic layout solver** (replaces dagre auto-ranking): a node-weighted Dijkstra from the FortiGate (firewall 1 / switch 2 / AP 3 / endpoint 4) places **column anchors** on **even** columns by weighted depth (distinct depths compacted to contiguous columns), **leaves** on the **odd** column right of their parent, FortiLink-fallback switches (no interface/LLDP-verified path to the FortiGate) in **negative** columns (-2, their endpoints -3). An anchor is infra (FortiGate / switch / AP) that isn't a *terminal* AP — `isLeafAp` classifies a FortiAP hanging off a switch port with no wireless mesh/bridge children of its own as a **leaf** (placed in the parent switch's leaf column, NOT its own anchor column), so a FortiGate's switch chain stays in tight consecutive columns with each switch's APs hung directly off it instead of every AP's weighted depth fanning the switches across the canvas; mesh-root and bridged-switch-parent APs stay anchors. Rows come in **two passes**: (a) a **nearest-free-slot packing** pass over **anchors only** (a node's first anchor child in a different column continues the parent's row so chains stay flat; every other anchor scans downward from just below its parent's row for the first lane where its whole footprint fits — its own cell, the spine chain that will inherit its lane into later columns, and each chain member's planned leaf block one column right, that block starting one row below a member whose chain continues since the continuing spine edge occupies the member's own row — so rows pack tight near the spine and drift down only where subtrees congest, instead of every subtree pre-claiming a globally disjoint row band that pushed a left-column switch's later children below everything placed before them) and (b) a leaf pass that slides each parent's leaves as one **contiguous window** (grouped by parent, blocks ordered by parent row) starting at the parent's row, slid down as a whole to dodge occupied lanes or a drawn edge passing through the column (per-leaf dodging would fragment a block around another chain's spine running through it) — so each switch's AP stack lines up just below it, grouped together, never staircased rightward or split apart/interleaved by another switch's APs even when the `/topology` payload lists APs in interleaved order; orphans stack below everything. Mesh leaves (AP-as-station-on-AP, `isMesh`) and LLDP wireless-bridge switches (`bridgeEdges` → `isBridge`) stay anchors and route through their AP. Wired AP↔switch links (a managed AP's switch uplink or a bridged switch behind an AP) carry `isApLink` and render solid blue (#3b82f6) with a directional arrow — distinct from the dashed violet wireless mesh backhaul and the gray controller edges. `markPhysicalLoops` (exported; runs at the end of `buildTopologyElements`) stamps `inLoop: 1` on every wired edge lying on a cycle — Tarjan bridge-finding over the simple graph of interface/LLDP/AP-link/verified-uplink edges **plus MCLAG ICLs** (an ICL is a real cabled link, so when it closes a cycle — the usual MCLAG shape where both peers uplink to a common parent — it's part of a physical loop and gets haloed; an isolated ICL that's the only path between its peers is a bridge/cut-edge and stays unflagged; wireless and unverified controller edges are excluded; parallel cables between one pair collapse to one adjacency so a trunk pair isn't flagged) — and the stylesheet halos those edges yellow (`line-outline-color` #eab308) around their own line color, with a matching legend row. `fortinetNodeColor` renders dependency-suppressed ("Dep. Down") nodes gray. `topologyLegendSpec()` is the single source of truth for the desktop Legend overlay — node + monitor-health + edge (incl. Mesh/bridge) swatches with descriptions, mirroring the constants the stylesheet uses. Desktop opts in to the endpoint-overlay styles (synthetic round-rectangle endpoint node + .dimmed off-path styles) used by its connection-path overlay; mobile opts out.

Collapsed row: IP headline + `MAC · hostname` subtitle (MAC first, then hostname; falls back to subnet label when both empty). Tap the row to expand inline (one row at a time) showing hostname/owner/network/source/notes/expires plus role-gated action buttons: **Reserve** on `sourceType="dhcp_lease"` rows for any create-capable role — calls `window.PolarisReserveSheet.open()` (exposed by subnet-detail.js) with the lease prefilled and `existingLeaseId` so the lease is released atomically before the manual reservation is created (which then pushes to the FortiGate when the integration's `pushReservations` toggle is on); the button is blue by default (`btn-filled`, tooltip `Reserve in Polaris`) and flips green (`btn-success`, tooltip `Reserve on Gate`) when the row's `pushEligible` flag is set so the operator sees at a glance that confirming will also write to the FortiGate; **Edit** opens an inline PUT sheet (hostname/owner/MAC/notes/expires), labels MAC as required on push-eligible subnets to match the backend's reject-on-clear rule; **Release/Revoke** is a confirm + `api.reservations.release()` — labelled "Revoke" with tooltip `Revoke Lease` on `dhcp_lease` rows (FortiOS forgets the current lease; client can re-acquire) and "Release" with tooltip `Release Reservation` on every other source. Edit/Release mirror backend role gates — admin/networkadmin always pass; user/assetsadmin only when `r.createdBy === user.username`. **Open network** text button preserves the original tap-to-subnet navigation. The Edit / Free / Reserve-from-lease flows are also exposed as `window.PolarisReservationActions.{edit, free, reserveFromLease, canCreate, canModify}` so the Networks page (subnet-detail.js IP list) can drive the same tap-to-expand pattern with shared modal markup. Replaced the prior Alerts tab in the bottom nav), tabs.js (per-tab registry + Search results renderer + shared snackbar helper). The Search input itself lives in the shell-owned `#search-slot` (rendered once by app.js `renderShell` and persistent across navigation so the typed query survives tab/route changes); tabs.js exposes `window.PolarisSearch.{runSearch, debounce, setOriginRoute}` that the shell's input handler calls. Typing on any page replace-navigates to `/search` so results land in the body. The Search tab's own `renderTopbar` returns `''` (no duplicate bar); its `render()` re-runs the current persistent-input value so coming back to the tab shows the same results. **Page-aware ordering**: `setOriginRoute` is called by app.js `routeChanged` on every non-search route, so the result renderer hoists the matching section to the top (Reservations tab → reservations first; subnet detail → subnets first; assets tab / asset detail → assets first; map / site / topology → sites first; block detail / More→Blocks → blocks first; More→Subnets → subnets first). Mirrors the desktop search dropdown's page-aware section ordering., details.js (detail-route renderers — asset / subnet / block / site / topology; site delegates to map-tab, topology delegates to topology-tab), asset-detail.js (Asset detail **slide-up bottom sheet**, opened by `PolarisAssetDetail.open(id)` — a pure overlay with no route/hash change; the `asset/<id>` route survives only as a deep-link shim that paints the assets list as a backdrop then calls `open()`. All entry points call `open(id)` directly — assets-tab card tap, map site sheet, more-tab, subnet detail, both topology pivots, the search-hit consumer in tabs.js, and the LLDP-neighbor pivot (which replaces the sheet content in place) — each with a `PolarisRouter.go("asset/"+id)` fallback if the module isn't loaded; a `_openId` guard in `open()` and every loader bails a superseded asset's late fetch. `screenshotSheet` in asset-detail.js); a Hero with the status pill + identity bits (the name is NOT repeated here — it lives in the header); **Response Time** (collapsed by default — header subtitle shows the loaded avg / max / packet-loss summary at a glance, expand for the full response-time chart with 1h/12h/24h/7d/30d range buttons); **CPU + Memory** (collapsed by default — header subtitle shows the loaded `cpu avg N% · max N% · mem avg N% · max N%` summary with color spans matching the chart series, expand for the full chart; "Not collected for this monitor type" rendered in the subtitle when the asset's monitor type doesn't deliver telemetry); both charts render missed polls the way the desktop charts do — the line dives to the baseline in red with a gradient transition instead of bridging the hole, driven by explicit `ok:false` points for response time (mirroring desktop's `ptHasResponse`/`ptIsFailure`, so partial-loss rollup buckets still plot their average) and by inferred cadence gaps for CPU/memory, which carries no per-sample success flag (`charts.js` → TEMPLATES.md "Failure-aware line rendering"); General (IP / MAC / type / model / OS / location / last seen); **Temperatures** — per-sensor list driven by `api.assets.systemInfo` for the current reading and a single unfiltered `api.assets.temperatureHistory(id, {range:"1h"})` call whose samples are grouped by `sensorName` client-side for per-sensor min/avg/max so each row shows `1h · min N° · avg N° · max N°`; **Interfaces** — filtered to `operStatus==="up"` (down hidden), sorted by `alias || ifName`, each row shows the operator-set alias as the primary label with the real ifName as the secondary line (or the interface's IP when alias and ifName collapse to the same value) and the resolved link speed via a local `formatBps()` helper; tap a row opens a `.scrim` + `.sheet` bottom sheet reusing the map-tab.js pattern with status (`oper X · admin Y`), speed, type/VLAN, IP, MAC, cumulative inErrors / outErrors plus an LLDP **Neighbor** card list filtered from the cached `lldpNeighbors[]` payload to `localIfName === iface.ifName` (peer-inferred entries are surfaced server-side so they appear here too — rendered with an italic "inferred" tag) — each neighbor card carries a **View asset** button when `matchedAsset.id` resolves, replacing the sheet content in place with the matched asset via `open(id)`. The two system-info-derived sections share one `api.assets.systemInfo` round-trip cached in module-level `_systemInfoCache` keyed by asset id so the sheet renders without a re-fetch; the Refresh action re-issues system-info alongside the chart pulls so a manual probe-now refreshes the new sections too. Three discovery-provenance sections follow: **Discovery sources** (`api.assets.getSources` → `GET /assets/:id/sources`, per-source list with the `SOURCE_LABELS` humanized sourceKind + integration name + lastSeen + externalId, mirrors desktop `_assetSourceLabels`; expanded by default), **Firewall sightings** (`api.assets.getSightings` → `GET /assets/:id/sightings`, fortigateDevice + ip + subnet/VLAN + source + lastSeen — endpoint needs `assetsQuarantine read`, so lower-privilege roles get a muted error note), and **IP history** (`api.assets.getIpHistory` → `GET /assets/:id/ip-history`); all three endpoints return bare arrays (the loaders read `Array.isArray(resp)`, not `resp.history`) and each header subtitle shows a count. The Hero also carries a **Quarantine** / **Release Quarantine** button (`quarantineButtonHtml` / `wireQuarantineButton`), gated on `assetsQuarantine:write` (read from `PolarisMobile.user().permissions`) and mirroring the desktop quarantine tab's eligibility — **Quarantine** (`btn-error`) for non-infra assets carrying a MAC, **Release Quarantine** (`btn-tonal`) for already-quarantined assets, nothing otherwise; it prompts for an optional reason (quarantine) or confirms (release) via `window.prompt`/`window.confirm`, then `refreshAfterQuarantine` re-fetches the asset to update the hero pill / header dot / button in place. The Hero also carries a **View SD-WAN** button (`btn-tonal`) for FortiManager/FortiGate-discovered firewalls — `loadSdwanGate` fetches `sdwan-members` / `sdwan-rules` / `perf-sla-links` (mirroring the desktop SD-WAN tab's prefetch-then-conditional gate) and reveals the button only when the device actually reported data, caching the payload in `_sdwanCache`. Tapping it opens a second stacked `.sheet`/`.scrim` bottom sheet (`openSdwanSheet`, same pattern as the interface sheet) with **Members** (status dot + member/zone + IP/link/speed + per-health-check latency chips), **Rules** (rule name/id + destination/criteria + member pills with the selected member highlighted + enabled state), and a **Performance SLA** section — a health-check `<select>` + 1h/12h/24h/7d/30d range segmented control driving three `PolarisCharts.lineChart` panels (latency / jitter / packet-loss) that overlay every member of the selected health-check (one color per member via a shared `sdwanColor` palette matching desktop), with a member legend, cross-member average stats line, and the SLA thresholds. Out of scope on mobile: per-interface throughput + errors charts, interface comment editor, IPsec tunnels, SNMP walk, per-source observed blob view.), more-tab.js (More tab — sub-page registry for Blocks / Subnets / Events plus the root menu with `Appearance → Theme` toggle row that flips dark↔light via `window.PolarisTheme.set` — sun/moon icon swap matches desktop's idiom, supporting label updates inline without re-rendering the tab), app.js (orchestrator: bootstraps auth, mounts the tab shell, dispatches tab and detail routes; detail specs may carry a `parentTab` to keep the corresponding navbar item highlighted; an early IIFE reads `localStorage["polaris-theme"]` (default `"dark"`, same key as desktop so a preference set on either surface flows to the other) and stamps `data-theme` on `<html>` *before* the orchestrator runs so the first paint never flashes the wrong theme; exposes `window.PolarisTheme.get()` / `.set()` for map-tab and more-tab to read/write without duplicating the localStorage key; bootstraps a best-effort `screen.orientation.lock("portrait")` — Android Chrome / installed PWAs honor it, iOS Safari rejects silently and the CSS landscape lockout in mobile.css picks up the slack).

│   ├── utils/portVlans.ts         # Pure Q-BRIDGE-MIB (RFC 4363) per-port VLAN decoding: `decodePortList` (PortList OCTET STRING → dot1dBasePort numbers; octet 0's MOST-significant bit is port 1) and `derivePortVlans` (dot1qPvid + the per-VLAN egress/untagged bitmaps → per-port {nativeVlan, taggedVlans}). The decision worth isolating: `dot1qVlanStaticUntaggedPorts` is often a verbatim COPY of the egress column (observed on FortiSwitch, 2026-08), and the RFC subtraction against a copy leaves EVERY port with an empty tagged set — a working trunk silently reported as carrying nothing. The untagged column is therefore believed only when it is a STRICT SUBSET of egress; otherwise the port's own PVID does that job. A port's native VLAN is never listed among its tagged VLANs either way

Both accept a subset param so each widget fetches only what it renders (`?sections=blocks|recent|assetTypes|monitorAlerts` on summary, `?feeds=<feed,...>` on noc-summary; absent = full legacy shape), and both serve every section/feed through a short server-side TTL cache (`utils/ttlCache.ts`, 10s = `NOC_FEED_CACHE_TTL_MS`) so concurrent widgets/tabs/kiosks share one computation. `summary` sections: blockUtilization from utilizationService.getGlobalUtilization, recentReservations from utilizationService.getRecentManualReservations (sourceType=manual only by default; cache key carries the recentLimit/sourceTypes params), assetTypeCounts via prisma.asset.groupBy (excluding decommissioned/disabled), and monitorAlerts via prisma.asset.findMany filtered to monitored + status in (warning, down), ordered by monitorStatusChangedAt desc nulls-last, capped at 50. `noc-summary` delegates to `nocDashboardService.getNocSummaryPayload` (feed registry + per-feed cache + `resolveFilteredAssetIds`); the route only parses params (`?assetTypes=server,switch,…` = the ENABLED built-in types, `?regionTags=East,West` = region names from the widget's Regions scope ("My regions" or a Selected-regions pick), `?fortigates=SITE-FG1,…` = FortiGate device names from the widget's FortiGates scope (assets behind any named gate; `__none__` = the "(No FortiGate)" gate-less entry), `?limit=` row cap, `?feeds=`) and resolves permissions. Reads gated by `assets=read`; writes by `assets=write` (admin + assetsadmin). Eight built-ins seeded by migration are `isProtected=true` and reject rename/delete. Rename is transactional — every Asset row holding the old name is rewritten in the same `$transaction` as the registry update.
│   │       ├── mibs.ts              # MIB Database CRUD + Browse + MIB-aware Walk. Mounted at `/server-settings/mibs` BEFORE the rest of /server-settings so its per-route guards (admin OR assets-admin on reads, admin-only on writes) take precedence over the blanket `requireAdmin` on the rest of /server-settings. Carries the `/structure` (parsed object tree) and `/walk` (decoded MIB-aware SNMP walk) endpoints alongside the existing list/get/upload/delete/profile-status/facets routes that moved here from serverSettings.ts.
│   │       └── serverSettings.ts    # HTTPS, branding, backup/restore
│   ├── services/
│   │   ├── brandLogoService.ts      # The operator's logo with the Polaris symbol composited onto its bottom-right corner (`branding.logoAccent`), rendered server-side via @resvg/resvg-js so login / sidebar / mobile can't each drift on the geometry. `accentGeometry` is the pure placement math (`ACCENT_FRACTION` = 0.5 of the logo's LONGEST side, clamped to half its shortest so a wide banner can't be swallowed; the canvas caps at MAX_RENDER_PX). Renders PER THEME (`renderAccentedLogo(theme)`, `?theme=dark|light` on the route, narrowed by `normalizeBrandTheme` since the value picks a filesystem path on an unauthenticated route) because the symbol art is theme-paired; the theme is part of the cache key and therefore of the ETag, so the two variants can't revalidate into each other. In-memory cache (≤4 entries) keyed on the logo + symbol mtimes + theme (the upload route writes a FIXED filename). Never throws — accent off / default logo / missing file / WebP / resvg failure all return null and the caller serves the plain logo. Served at the PUBLIC `GET /server-settings/branding/logo-accent.png` (declared in api/router.ts, above requireAuth, because the login page renders it pre-session).
│   │   ├── brandingService.ts       # The `branding` Setting row (appName / subtitle / logoUrl / logoAccent / logoOnLogin / logoOnSidebar / temperatureUnit — the DISPLAY-ONLY °C/°F preference for hardware sensors, normalized by `normalizeTemperatureUnit`; samples stay Celsius, see TOUCHES.md) + BRANDING_DEFAULTS. Extracted from routes/serverSettings.ts (which re-exports getBranding for its own routes + the public /branding alias) so appIconService and routes/pwa.ts can read branding without importing a route module. **`appName` may be EMPTY** — an operator whose uploaded logo carries their own wordmark blanks it, and the value is no longer snapped back to "Polaris" on read or write; surfaces that must print a name (page titles, the PWA manifest `name`, the acknowledge page) go through `displayAppName`. `logoAccent` / `logoOnLogin` / `logoOnSidebar` are read through `normalizeBrandingFlag` (only `undefined`/`null` take the default, so a stored `false` survives) and are inert without a custom logo; `hasCustomLogo` is the one definition of "custom", surfaced to the frontends as the derived `customLogo` field so they never compare paths.
│   │   ├── appIconService.ts        # PWA home-screen icons rasterized from the branding logo via @resvg/resvg-js (SVG canvas embedding the source as a data: URI). ICON_SPECS is the route's allowlist (192/512 any + maskable, 180 apple). On-demand + in-memory cache keyed on logo mtime (the upload route writes a FIXED filename, so mtime is the only invalidation signal). Never throws: unresolvable/traversal/missing/WebP/resvg-failure all degrade to the shipped public/img/brand/polaris-symbol-dark.png.
│   │   ├── certInfo.ts              # Leaf-cert fingerprint/SANs/expiry — dual-mode (reads disk in proxy mode, in-memory PEM in Node-HTTPS mode); layered cache with last-known-good fallback for cert-rotation atomic-rename windows
│   │   ├── ipService.ts             # Core IP math & validation
│   │   ├── blockService.ts          # Block business logic
│   │   ├── subnetService.ts         # Subnet allocation logic
│   │   ├── reservationService.ts    # Reservation business logic
│   │   ├── reservationPushService.ts # Push manual DHCP reservations to FortiGate via an FMG integration (proxy or direct realtime, with read-back verify); used by reservationService on create + release. Also exports `buildTransportForIntegration` / `findScopeIdForCidr` / `listReservedAddresses` / `callFortiOs` so subnetRefreshService can reuse the same FMG-proxy/direct-FortiGate transport for read-only single-scope reconciliation. **Exports `classifyPushError(err) → "permanent" | "transient"`** — single source of truth for whether a push failure is operator-action-required (4xx, 502 with "verify mismatch" / "not visible on read-back" / "Authentication failed") or retry-eligible (everything else; defaults to retry-eligible). Consumed by `reservationService.createReservation` (transient → keep row + queue; permanent → rollback) and `retryPendingReservations` (transient → leave pending; permanent → flip to `failed_permanent`).
│   │   ├── infraReservationPushService.ts # OPT-IN post-sync discovery pass: turns a managed FortiSwitch/FortiAP's dynamic lease into a real MAC→IP `reserved-address` entry on its own gate. Double-gated (`config.pushReservations` + `config.autoReserveFortinetInfra`, both default off, both Fortinet integration types). Pins an address the device ALREADY holds, so pool occupancy is unchanged. The only scheduled DHCP write in Polaris, hence: bounded per cycle (RUN_CEILING 25), concurrency 2, MAC taken only from the gate's lease table, read-back-verified by `pushReservation`, and never re-attempted once the row carries push state — a permanent refusal stamps `pushStatus="failed_permanent"` + `pushError` so it drops out of the candidate set and shows the device's message in the IP panel. Eligibility is the pure `isInfraPushCandidate`. Stamps the push pointers the lifecycle release's pinned-unpush branch needs, so decommissioning the device removes the entry.
│   │   ├── placeholderMacAdoptionService.ts # Discovery Phase 7.7: replaces a reservation's PLACEHOLDER MAC with the real device's MAC once the gate reports one at that reserved IP, and re-pushes the corrected binding. Double-gated (`config.pushReservations` + `config.adoptDiscoveredMac`, both default off, both Fortinet integration types). Evidence is the ARP table + device inventory ONLY, keyed `(fortigateDevice, ip)` like Phase 7.6 (`buildMacEvidenceIndex` — ARP beats inventory, online beats offline, two disagreeing ARP rows drop the address). Eligibility is the pure `isAdoptionCandidate`: only a MAC matching the configured placeholder prefix is ever overwritten, the observed MAC must not itself be a placeholder, and a MAC already held by another active reservation in the same subnet is skipped (FortiOS would refuse it permanently). Device write goes through `updatePushedReservation` BEFORE the Polaris write so the two views can't diverge; a `pending` row skips device contact. Bounded per RUN, not per call (`AdoptionBudget`, 50) because FMG mode syncs once per gate. See business rule 26.
│   │   ├── reservationMacService.ts # The install-wide placeholder-MAC prefix Setting (`reservationMacPlaceholder`, default `02:0F:5E`). createSettingStore + pure normalizer + AppError-throwing save, the assetSourcePriorityService shape. Read self-heals a bad stored row to the default (an unparseable prefix would make `isPlaceholderMac` answer false for everything and silently disable adoption); save rejects, because an operator typing a vendor OUI needs to hear why.
│   │   ├── fortinetManagementAccessService.ts # Reads management-access (`allowaccess`) config for Fortinet devices during FMG/FortiGate discovery and summarizes it into `Asset.managementAccess`. `collectManagementAccess(integration, groups, opts)` builds one transport per controller FortiGate (via `buildTransportForIntegration` + `callFortiOs`, so FMG-proxy / FMG-direct / standalone all work) and reads: firewall `/api/v2/cmdb/system/interface` (the `config.mgmtInterface` interface's allowaccess), FortiAP `/api/v2/cmdb/wireless-controller/{wtp-profile,wtp}` (serial→profile→allowaccess), and FortiSwitch `/api/v2/cmdb/switch-controller/managed-switch` (best-effort interface allowaccess — `protocols: null` when unreadable). Returns `Map<serial, ManagementAccessSummary>`. Pure parsers (`parseAllowaccess` / `findInterfaceRow` / `buildFirewallSummary` / `parseWtpProfiles` / `parseWtpToProfile` / `buildApSummary` / `buildSwitchSummary`) are exported + unit-tested; never throw on malformed payloads. Per-device failures are swallowed (logged) so one unreachable FortiGate never aborts the pass. Read-only — never writes the device. Hooked into `syncDhcpSubnets` Phase 13.6 (gated `full|finalize`).
│   │   ├── fortigateLocationService.ts # Discovery-time `fetchFortigateSysLocation()`: REST `GET /api/v2/cmdb/system.snmp/sysinfo` against a FortiGate via the existing FMG-proxy / standalone transport (reuses `callFortiOs` + `buildTransportForIntegration` from reservationPushService). Returns the trimmed sysLocation string or null. Chosen over an SNMP get to avoid a separate credential resolver / net-snmp session and to work in FMG proxy mode where Polaris can't reach the FortiGate's management IP directly. Never throws — REST failures come back as null so the discovery sync continues with no location update.
│   │   ├── geocoderService.ts         # Address-string → lat/lng geocoder backed by OpenStreetMap Nominatim. `geocode(query)` normalizes the input (trim + collapse-whitespace + lowercase), consults `GeocodeCache` (90-day TTL; positive AND negative results cached), and on cache-miss hits Nominatim through a process-global 1 req/sec rate limiter (module-level chained Promise enforces the gap). User-Agent identifies Polaris per Nominatim's usage policy. Transport failures (timeout / non-2xx / parse error) do NOT poison the cache; only successful responses (including empty result arrays — the negative-cache signal) write rows. Never throws. Used by the FortiGate coord-resolution chain in `syncDhcpSubnets` Phase 3.
│   │   ├── fortigateCoordPushService.ts # `pushCoordsToFortigate()` — write-back orchestrator for geocoded coords. FMG mode writes to BOTH per-device metavars `Latitude` / `Longitude` (native FMG `update` on `/dvmdb/adom/<adom>/device/<n>` with `{"meta fields": {...}}`) AND CMDB `gui-device-latitude` / `gui-device-longitude` (native FMG `update` on `/pm/config/device/<n>/global/system/global`). Standalone FortiGate writes only CMDB via direct REST PUT on `/api/v2/cmdb/system/global`. Best-effort: per-target failures are logged and reflected in the returned `{ok, targets[], error?}` shape but never throw. FMG-mode CMDB writes land in FMG's CMDB but require an operator Install Device Configuration in FMG to reach the live FortiGate — Polaris explicitly does not trigger installs.
│   │   ├── subnetRefreshService.ts   # Per-subnet "refresh from device" action (Refresh button in the IP panel slide-in). Queries the originating FortiGate for ONE DHCP scope (CMDB reservations + live leases) via the same transport reservationPushService uses, reconciles against Polaris's `dhcp_reservation` + `dhcp_lease` rows on this subnet (manual / VIP rows untouched), and bumps `Subnet.lastDiscoveredAt`. Narrower than `discoverDhcpSubnets` — doesn't recompute asset sightings / decommissions / map regions / etc.; those reconcile on the next full integration cycle. Writes one `subnet.refresh` Event.
│   │   ├── reservationStaleService.ts # Stale-reservation detection: settings (staleAfterDays), alert lister (active|ignored), snooze/ignore mutators, and the job entry point that emits reservation.stale Events. The freshest-signal core (`effectiveLastSignalMs`) folds THREE real presence signals — `lastSeenLeased` (DHCP lease), `lastSeenArp` (FortiGate ARP table binding the reserved IP to the reserved MAC — stamped by sync Phase 7.6), and Asset.lastSeen (correlated by MAC then IP) — so statically-addressed / ICMP-silent devices that never lease aren't flagged. Excludes reservations on deprecated subnets (decommissioned-firewall networks) from the active list/count
│   │   ├── arpPrimeService.ts        # ARP-priming presence sweep: fire-and-forget UDP datagrams (port 33434, 1-byte payload) at a list of reserved IPs so the FortiGate is forced to ARP-resolve each target right before discovery reads its ARP table — any live IP stack answers ARP even when it firewalls ICMP. `planSweepBatches` (pure: dedupe / IPv4-validate / cap 4096 / chunk 256) + `primeArpCache` (single udp4 socket, paced batches, per-datagram errors swallowed, never throws) + `ARP_SETTLE_MS` (2s sweep→read gap; FortiOS GCs unreferenced neighbor-cache entries in ~60-90s so callers must read promptly). Opt-in per integration via `config.arpPresenceSweep` (default off — the sweep is IDS-visible); called per-gate from fortimanagerService Step 3d.54 (proxy mode) and fortigateService Step 3e.54 (standalone + FMG-direct)
│   │   ├── dnsResolvedReservationService.ts # Auto-creates Reservation rows with `sourceType="dns_resolved"` for every Asset with an `ipAddress` that falls inside a non-deprecated Subnet and has no authoritative (manual / dhcp_reservation / dhcp_lease / interface_ip / vip / fortiswitch / fortinap / fortimanager / fortigate) reservation already there. Carries the asset's hostname (`hostname || dnsName`) and `macAddress` when known; `createdBy="system:dns-resolved"`. Exports `reconcileDnsResolvedForAsset(assetId)` (the per-asset path called from the Prisma extension hook in `src/db.ts` post-write + from the periodic job per-row), `reconcileDnsResolvedForAllAssets()` (the periodic sweep — batches of 25 via Promise.all), `releaseDnsResolvedForAsset(assetId)` (asset-delete hook), and `releaseDnsResolvedAt(subnetId, ipAddress)` (the discovery hand-off used by `syncDhcpSubnets` and `reservationService.createReservation` right before creating an authoritative row at the same target). Eligible asset statuses: active / maintenance / storage / quarantined. IPv4 only. Defers silently to authoritative entries — never raises Conflict rows, never pushes to FortiGates.
│   │   ├── utilizationService.ts    # Utilization reporting. `getGlobalUtilization` backs the legacy `/utilization` route and is also reused by the new Dashboard summary. `getRecentManualReservations` is the new helper that powers the Dashboard's "Recently Reserved" card — same `findMany` shape as `recentReservations` but filtered to `sourceType="manual"` so DHCP discoveries / leases / VIP echoes don't crowd it out, with `{id,cidr,name,vlan}` hydrated on the subnet relation so the card renders without a second fetch.
│   │   ├── nocDashboardService.ts   # Fleet-wide aggregates behind `/dashboard/noc-summary` (SolarWinds-style NOC widgets). getStatusSummary (groupBy monitorStatus + infra-subset uptime% + active-alert count), getDownNodes, getHighestCpu/getHighestMemory (avg of each asset's most-recent N telemetry samples — N = the caller's `sampleCount` from the widgets' "Average over" gear control, default `DEFAULT_TOPN_SAMPLE_COUNT` = 10, ceiling `MAX_TOPN_SAMPLE_COUNT` = 100, 1 = rank on the latest sample only — via a windowed `row_number()` over asset_telemetry_samples; the window scales at 6 min/sample (1h at the default) so it always holds N samples while staying chunk-excluded — hydrated in one findMany; replaced the prior DISTINCT-ON latest-value ranking), getSlowestResponse (averages each asset's most-recent 10 response times via a windowed `row_number()` over asset_monitor_samples — 6h window keeps the hypertable scan chunk-excluded — then hydrates names; replaced the prior instantaneous Asset.lastResponseTimeMs ranking), getPacketLoss (failed-probe ratio groupBy over asset_monitor_samples — no schema change), getHighestDiskUsage (per-volume used % — DISTINCT-ON latest per (assetId, mountPath) over asset_storage_samples, 48h window for the slow storage cadence, hydrated in one findMany with the mount as `detail`), getStalePolls (indexed candidate findMany + cached resolveMonitorSettings per candidate), getRecentReboots (an Event read), getRecentAlerts (the UNCLEARED Notification rows — an ALERT read, not an Event one: it listed every warning/error Event until 2026-08, which surfaced automation-less discovery/sync failures as permanent alerts nothing could clear and showed `Event.level`, whose critical/serious collapse displayed a `serious` automation as "error"), getSitesWithIssues (raw COALESCE groupBy + one bounded node findMany), and resolveFilteredAssetIds (turns the optional per-widget `{assetTypes, regionNames, fortigateNames}` filter into a constraining assetId set — `assetType notIn <hidden built-ins>` + `tags hasSome region:<name>` + behind-any-named-gate (`learnedLocation` equals-insensitive OR sighting rows; `FORTIGATE_NONE_SENTINEL` = gate-less assets) — or null when nothing narrows; every feed takes an `assetIds` arg). `getStorageForecast` (days-until-full per growing filesystem via `storageForecastService`, severity-first then soonest-full). **Severity-first ordering:** every asset-sourced feed decorates rows with the owning asset's highest ACTIVE automation alert (`activeAlertSeverityByAsset` over uncleared Notification rows, `ALERT_SEVERITY_RANK` incl. legacy info/error) and STABLE-sorts alerted rows first — each feed's own order (value desc / youngest outage / most overdue / soonest-full) holds within a severity band; `getRecentAlerts` is itself alert-sourced — it sorts the uncleared set by `ALERT_SEVERITY_RANK` desc then triggeredAt desc in memory, since severity is a string rather than a rank column, and slices to the row cap AFTER sorting so a limit can't drop a critical; `getSitesWithIssues` takes the max rank across a site's affected nodes. `getNocSummaryPayload({feeds, canAssets, canEvents, canAlerts, assetTypes, regionNames, capLimit, sampleCount})` is the route's entry point: a `NOC_FEEDS` registry maps each of the 15 feed names (`NOC_FEED_NAMES`) to its permission gate (`assets` / `events` / `alerts` — the last only activeAlerts), empty value, runner, and response-key flattening (`status` fans out to statusCounts/uptimePercent/activeAlertCount; `downNodes` unwraps `.nodes`); unknown feed names drop silently; every (feed, filter, cap[, samples]) computation — and the filter→assetIds resolution — goes through a shared 10s `createTtlCache` (only the `usesDepDown` feed — downNodes — keys on `?includeDependencyDown`, and only the `usesSamples` feeds — topCpu/topMemory — key on the samples count) (`NOC_FEED_CACHE_TTL_MS`, `clearNocFeedCache()` test hook) so N widgets/browsers recompute nothing. Read-only; every query scale-checked flat to 2000 assets.
│   │   ├── probeLossQuery.ts        # The ONE windowed failed-probe-ratio query over asset_monitor_samples, shared by the notification engine probeLossPct trigger (every asset with >=1 successful probe, incl. 0% rows for hysteresis recovery) and the NOC Packet Loss widget (onlyLossy mode: >=1 failure too, lossiest-first, capped; plus `includeFullyDown`, which reports an asset with NO success in the window as 100% instead of letting the anchor drop it - DISPLAY ONLY, since a 100% reading reaching the engine would double-alert an outage asset-down already owns). Counts EVERY `probeKind`, one of only two all-kinds readers of that table (with alertChartService's loss chart) - that is what the ICMP loss sampler exists to feed. 2026-08 dedup -- the drifted HAVING clauses turned out to be a real semantic difference, so it is a parameter. The ratio is measured from each asset's FIRST SUCCESSFUL probe in the window (partitioned `min("timestamp") FILTER (WHERE "success")`, everything older trimmed), not from the window's leading edge: a device that was unreachable for part of the window had no probes to lose, so a device recovering from a 55-minute outage reads 0% on its first clean probe instead of ~92% loss for a full window's worth of ticks. See business rule 29.
│   │   ├── storageForecastService.ts # Per-filesystem "days until full" forecasting — the shared computation behind the Storage Forecast dashboard widget (nocDashboardService `storageForecast` feed) and the `storageDaysUntilFull` automation metric (notificationEngine resolver). ONE regr_slope aggregate over a UNION of day-bucketed storage DETAIL samples (7d retention — covers every storage-scraped asset incl. the slow 24h cadence) and the DAILY rollups (365d, but cadence='fast' pinned assets only — see sampleRollupService), deduped per (asset, mount, day); 30-day lookback (`FORECAST_LOOKBACK_DAYS`), ≥7 distinct daily points (`FORECAST_MIN_POINTS`), growing mounts only, forecasts beyond 365 days dropped (`FORECAST_MAX_DAYS`). JS side only does the remaining/slope division via utils/linearTrend. Read-only; flat at 2000 assets.
│   │   ├── fortimanagerService.ts   # FMG JSON-RPC client & discovery orchestration. All FMG-bound calls (rpc, fmgProxyRest, resolveDeviceMgmtIp, ...) accept an optional `integrationId` and route through `getFmgWorker(integrationId)` so cross-feature traffic (discovery + reservation push + quarantine push + manual proxy + connection test) stays serial against FMG's "one-request-at-a-time" constraint.
│   │   ├── fortigateService.ts      # Standalone FortiGate REST API client & discovery. **Per-device REST queries fan out across 6 independent chains via Promise.all** so per-FortiGate wall-clock is `max(longest chain)` instead of `sum(all 12 steps)`. Chains (after Steps 1 + 2): A) DHCP CMDB → Promise.all(DHCP monitor + interface IPs); B) device inventory; C) managed switches → managed APs → AP-port mapping (serial intra-chain — 3e.5 needs both 3d and 3e); D) ARP table; E) geo coordinates; F) firewall VIPs. Peak intra-device REST concurrency is ~6 simultaneous calls; small-branch FortiGates (60F/61F class) handle this fine, and each step keeps its own try/catch so a slow individual query doesn't tank the whole device. Used by the standalone FortiGate integration directly AND by `fortimanagerService` in direct mode (`useProxy=false`) which delegates per-device work to `fortigateService.discoverDhcpSubnets`.
│   │   ├── fmgActivityService.ts    # DB-backed heartbeat of every `FmgWorker`'s lane state. The role that owns FMG traffic (discovery in split-role prod, the single process in "all" mode) snapshots all `getAllFmgWorkers()` to the `fmgActivitySnapshot` Setting row every 2 s; the web role reads it back via `getFmgActivityForIntegration(integrationId)` to power the "Active FMG Calls" row on the integrations page. Snapshots stamp `updatedAt + role`; `STALENESS_MS=10_000` is the freshness threshold the API + UI use to flag a dead heartbeat (e.g. polaris-discovery down). One write per 2 s per FMG-running process; reads are key-equality on `Setting.key`.
│   │   ├── fmgWorker.ts             # Per-integration FortiManager worker with two lanes. Module-level `Map<integrationId, FmgWorker>`, lazily created on first submit. The FMG concurrency constraint is specifically about `/sys/proxy/json` (the passthrough that forwards calls through to managed FortiGates) — FMG drops parallel proxy connections past 1-2 for the same API user. Native endpoints (`/pm/config/...`, `/dvmdb/...`, auth) hit FMG's own DB and don't share that constraint. Lanes: **proxy lane** is strict single-consumer FIFO (concurrency=1) and carries every `/sys/proxy/json` call; **native lane** is unbounded and just tracks inflight count for observability. Dispatch happens inside `rpc()` (fortimanagerService) by inspecting the JSON-RPC payload's first param URL; callers use `submitProxy` / `submitNative` explicitly. Cross-feature serialization still holds for proxy calls (discovery per-device monitor scrapes, proxy-mode reservation push, proxy-mode quarantine push, manual `/sys/proxy/json` proxy endpoint all share one slot); native calls (mgmt-IP resolves, CMDB scrapes, the device roster) parallelize freely. Exports `polaris_fmg_worker_queue_depth{integrationId}` + `polaris_fmg_worker_inflight{integrationId}` (proxy lane) and `polaris_fmg_worker_native_inflight{integrationId}` (native lane) so operators can see which lane is the bottleneck.
│   │   ├── windowsServerService.ts  # Windows Server WinRM DHCP discovery
│   │   ├── entraIdService.ts        # Microsoft Entra ID + Intune device discovery via Graph
│   │   ├── activeDirectoryService.ts # On-premise Active Directory computer discovery via LDAP/LDAPS
│   │   ├── azureArcService.ts       # Azure Arc (Arc-enabled servers) discovery client. OAuth2 client-credentials against **Azure Resource Manager** — reuses src/utils/entraClientCredentials.ts at scope https://management.azure.com/.default, so no Azure SDK and no Microsoft Graph permission. Two interchangeable read paths normalizing through the same normalizeArcMachine: Azure Resource Graph (default — ONE POST across every readable subscription, with server-side projection) and a per-subscription paged Microsoft.HybridCompute/machines list used when ARG is off or unavailable (transparent fallback, logged once). ARM specifics the Graph client doesn't have: nextLink paging (not @odata.nextLink), ARG's skipToken body paging, and mandatory 429 backoff honouring Retry-After / x-ms-user-quota-resets-after. Pure exported helpers are unit-tested: normalizeVmUuid (rejects the all-zero GUID), swapVmUuidEndianness (the SMBIOS little-endian disagreement between Windows / dmidecode / VMware — both variants are indexed at match time or every Arc-on-VMware machine duplicates), parseArmResourceId, inferArcAssetType, filterArcMachines, matchesTagFilter, arcHostnameCandidates, buildArcObservedBlob, throttleDelayMs, describeAadTokenError. Also backs testConnection (token → per-subscription read → bounded machine list, so a missing Reader role can't report a false success) and the Query API modal's proxyQuery (host-pinned to management.azure.com, api-version required, POST allowed only to the Resource Graph endpoint).
│   │   ├── vcenterService.ts        # VMware vCenter discovery + telemetry client. vSphere Automation REST (session auth, per-host VM listing pins VM→host placement + sidesteps the 4000-item list cap, VMware Tools guest identity/networking/filesystems per VM at bounded concurrency) + two narrow SOAP property-collector calls against /sdk (WinRM-Identify hand-rolled-envelope precedent, no XML dep): batched VM quickStats (CPU MHz + RAM usage for EVERY VM in one call — feeds the discovery usage snapshot AND monitoringService's per-tick telemetry warm cache) and datastore facts (summary capacity/free/uncommitted → provisioned, host mount list, VMFS extent NAA ids → array vendor via the exported `vendorFromNaa` prefix map, NFS remote host). Every SOAP surface degrades to nulls independently; datastores fall back to the REST list when /sdk is unreachable. Pure exported helpers (pickVmExternalId — instanceUuid with integration-scoped moref fallback; buildVcenterDependencyEdges — vMotion-safe cluster multi-parent; filterVms; SOAP parsers) are unit-tested. Also backs testConnection + the Query API modal's proxyQuery (REST surface only).
│   │   ├── searchService.ts         # Global typeahead search (classifies IP/CIDR/MAC/text; parallel entity queries). MAC lookups are range-aware: a full typed MAC also matches an AssetMacAddress range row containing it (lexicographic containment over canonical colon-uppercase bounds), and a partial hex term is additionally tried as a MAC prefix interval against ranges (`macPrefixBounds`)
│   │   ├── allocationTemplateService.ts # Saved multi-subnet allocation templates (Setting-backed)
│   │   ├── autoMonitorInterfacesService.ts # "Auto-Monitor Interfaces" feature: pure resolver over a multi-block union (byNames / byPatterns / byTypes / byLldp) + DB-bound aggregate/preview/apply for the FMG/FortiGate Monitoring tab. By LLDP pins any interface whose neighbor — direct `AssetLldpNeighbor.matchedAssetId` OR peer-inferred edge from `Asset.fortinetTopology` — resolves to a monitored asset of one of the selected types. The peer-inferred half (`loadInferredLldpByAsset` — class-aware raw SQL over `fortinetTopology->>'controllerFortigate'` / `parentSwitch` / etc.) covers managed FortiAPs whose FortiSwitch silently consumes LLDP without re-publishing via SNMP LLDP-MIB; same data source as the inferred Neighbor column on the System tab (see `peerInferredLldpService`). For the `fortiap` class, a post-load step (`normalizeFortiapInferredLldp`) rewrites synthesized `localIfName` from FortiAP-CLI naming (`lan1`) to SNMP-canonical (`eth0`) when the AP's interface table actually exposes the eth* form — without this, the resolver would pin a name that doesn't match any ifIndex on the fast-cadence scrape. UI label reads **By LLDP (includes inferred interfaces)** so operators see at a glance that the match set isn't LLDP-protocol-only. `compilePattern` dispatches wildcards vs raw regex per block. `coerceLegacySelection` rewrites the older single-mode discriminated-union shape (`{mode, ...}`) on read so the Zod parser + apply route + frontend renderer all keep working until the one-shot migration sweeps stored configs. Strictly additive to Asset.monitoredInterfaces.
```
