```
                                -- (nobody could ever see them again); public rows survive with ownerId NULL.
  ownerName     String          -- username snapshot so a surviving public preset still renders an author
  visibility    String          -- "private" (owner only) | "public" (anyone who can read the scope)
  state         Json            -- TableSF getPrefs shape: { sfFilters, sortKey, sortDir }. Validated by
                                -- sanitizeFilterState on every write — this blob is replayed into OTHER
                                -- operators' browsers when a public preset loads. Column widths / hidden
                                -- columns deliberately stay per-browser in localStorage (applyTableLayout):
                                -- they describe the operator's screen, not the query.
  createdAt     DateTime
  updatedAt     DateTime
                                -- @@unique([scope, ownerId, name]) (NULL owners compare distinct, so orphaned
                                -- presets never block a live user from reusing a name), @@index([scope, visibility])

ApplicationMapLayout            -- SHARED Application Map node positions — the appmap.html counterpart of
                                -- TopologyLayout, minus the per-site FK (the Application Map is one global
                                -- graph, not rooted on a firewall Asset).
  id            UUID PK
  view          String @unique @default("global") -- one global map today; the column future-proofs sub-views
  positions     Json            -- { [nodeId]: { x, y } } keyed on applicationMapService's deterministic
                                -- node ids (asset:<id>, proc:<assetId>:<b64url(name)>, ip:<ip>,
                                -- ipgroup:<cidr>) so saved layouts survive refresh. Validated by the
                                -- shared topologyLayoutService.sanitizePositions.
  updatedBy     String?
  createdAt     DateTime
  updatedAt     DateTime
                                -- Written via PUT /application-map/layout (applicationMap=write, audited);
                                -- read by everyone via the savedLayout embed on GET /application-map.
                                -- localStorage ("polaris.appmap.positions") is the per-browser fallback for
                                -- readers. Single writer: applicationMapService.

TopologyLayout                  -- SHARED Device Map topology node positions (the per-resource variant of
                                -- the UserDashboard JSON-layout pattern)
  id            UUID PK
  siteId        String FK → Asset (cascade delete) -- the FortiGate the topology graph is rooted on
  view          String @default("flat")            -- "flat" | computeFloorViews key ("b|<area>|<bldg>" / "f|<area>|<bldg>|<floor>").
                                -- Renaming a:/b:/f: codes changes view keys and orphans that view's row (harmless).
  positions     Json            -- { [nodeId]: { x, y } } pixel model coords — the exact shape map.js
                                -- saves/loads (and previously kept only in localStorage). Full-replace per
                                -- save; stale nodeIds are ignored at render and dropped on the next save.
                                -- Last-write-wins between concurrent editors (updatedBy/updatedAt enable a
                                -- future conditional write). Validated by topologyLayoutService
                                -- (sanitizePositions: finite coords, ≤3000 nodes) on top of the route Zod.
  updatedBy     String?
  createdAt     DateTime
  updatedAt     DateTime
  @@unique([siteId, view])
                                -- Written via PUT /map/sites/:id/topology/layout (deviceMap=write, audited);
                                -- read by everyone via the savedLayouts embed on GET /map/sites/:id/topology.
                                -- Server layout wins client-side; localStorage remains the per-browser
                                -- fallback (non-writer drags, pre-server installs). Mobile deliberately does
                                -- NOT apply it (transposed axes). Single writer: topologyLayoutService.

Event                           -- Audit log, 7-day rolling retention
  id            UUID PK
  timestamp     DateTime
  level         String          -- "info" | "warning" | "error" (display source of truth)
  levelRank     Int @default(0) -- Numeric severity stamped at write time by logEvent from `level`:
                                -- 0=info, 1=warning, 2=error (room for -1=debug / 3=critical
                                -- later). The Events list endpoint's sortBy=level dispatches
                                -- to orderBy: { levelRank } so severity sort matches operator
                                -- expectations (info < warning < error) instead of the
                                -- alphabetical accident (error < info < warning). Backed by
                                -- the (levelRank, timestamp) composite index for "severity
                                -- within the 7-day window" Index Scan plans.
  action        String          -- e.g. "block.created", "integration.discover.started"
  resourceType  String?
  resourceId    String?
  resourceName  String?
  actor         String?         -- username that triggered the event
  message       String
  details       Json?
  -- Indexed on: timestamp, action, resourceType, level, (levelRank,timestamp),
  -- (actor,timestamp), (resourceName,timestamp). The trailing-timestamp
  -- composite indexes back the per-column sort UX added when the Events page
  -- adopted the server-side TableSF pattern.

Conflict                        -- Discovery conflict resolution (two variants)
  id                UUID PK
  entityType        String         -- "reservation" | "asset"
  reservationId     UUID? FK → Reservation (cascade delete; null for asset conflicts)
  assetId           UUID? FK → Asset (cascade delete; null for reservation conflicts)
  integrationId     UUID?
  -- Reservation-conflict proposed values (null for asset conflicts):
  proposedHostname  String?
  proposedOwner     String?
  proposedProjectRef String?
  proposedNotes     String?
  proposedSourceType String?       -- Required for reservations, null for assets
  -- Asset-conflict proposed values (null for reservation conflicts):
  proposedDeviceId  String?        -- Entra deviceId (dedupe key across discovery runs)
  proposedAssetFields Json?        -- Full snapshot: hostname, serial, mac, model, manufacturer, os, osVersion, assignedTo, chassisType, complianceState, trustType
  existingAssetSnapshot Json?      -- Asset-conflict only. Snapshot of the collision-target asset's displayed fields (hostname, serial, mac, ip, manufacturer, model, os, osVersion, assignedTo) frozen at raise time, refreshed on each discovery run while pending, frozen at resolution. The Conflict Review card's "Existing Asset" column reads this so a resolved card shows conflict-time state, not the post-merge live row. Null for conflicts predating the column (UI falls back to the live `asset` relation).
  conflictFields    String[]       -- Field names that differ
  status            ConflictStatus @default(pending)
  resolvedBy        String?
  resolvedAt        DateTime?

Setting                         -- Key-value configuration store
  key           String PK
  value         Json
  -- Notable keys:
  --   "manualMonitorSettings"                  -- tier-3 settings for assets with no integration source. Same shape as Integration.config.monitorSettings (8 fields).
  --   "monitorSettingsHierarchyMigratedAt"     -- one-shot marker stamped by migrateMonitorSettingsHierarchy. Presence = migration ran; deleting it forces a re-run on next boot.
  --   "mapRegions"                              -- Operator-drawn map regions: `MapRegion[]` ({ id, name, polygon: [[lat,lng],...], color: "#rrggbb", createdBy, createdAt, updatedAt }). `color` is the polygon stroke + fill hue on the map; on create it defaults to a random palette pick (same palette `mapRegionService` uses for the matching Tag registry row) and can be overridden in the create modal or via the polygon-click popup's "Change color" action. Legacy regions written before this field existed are back-filled at read time with a random pick. See `mapRegionService`.
  --   "appMapAutoMap"                           -- Service/process DISCOVERY RULES (Integrations → Polaris Agent): `{version:2, rules:[{id, name, enabled, mode, source, scope, assetIds, processes:{names,patterns,regex}, services:{…}}]}`. `mode` = "map" (monitor + Application Map) | "monitor" (monitor-only); `source` = "manual" | "auto" (minted/consolidated from per-asset Services-tab pin toggles; single-item, scope:null + explicit assetIds — null scope + assetIds targets JUST those assets, and an auto rule losing its last asset is deleted). Each rule pins its items on union(scope matches, assetIds); several rules' pins union per asset. Applied inline on save and re-applied by the 30-min `reconcileAppMapAutoMap` job — the "and future assets too" mechanism. Additive only; `unmapEverywhere` is the separate subtractive path. The pre-rules single-selection shape folds forward into one rule at read time. See `appMapDiscoveryService`.

MonitorClassOverride            -- Tier-2 of the monitor settings hierarchy. **As of Phase 2, this table is manual-scope only (`integrationId IS NULL`)** — integration-discovered assets get per-class settings via `Integration.config.<klass>Monitor.streams` blocks instead. The `POST` and `PUT` routes reject integration-scoped writes with 400; the `migrateMonitorSettingsPerClass` startup job folds historical integration-scoped rows into the integration streams blocks and deletes them. One row per (assetType, NULL) tuple; each field is nullable so an override can supply just the values that diverge from the tier below.
  id                        UUID PK
  integrationId             UUID? FK → Integration (cascade delete) -- null = override applies to manual-tier (orphan / non-integration-discovered) assets.
  assetType                 String   -- "firewall" | "switch" | "access_point" | "server" | "workstation" | "router" | "printer" | "other" — matches Asset.assetType.
  intervalSeconds           Int?
  failureThreshold          Int?
  probeTimeoutMs            Int?
  cpuMemoryTimeoutMs        Int?  -- Per-request timeout (ms) for the CPU+memory collector. null = inherit from the tier below. Range 1000..120000.
  temperatureTimeoutMs      Int?  -- Per-request timeout (ms) for the temperature collector. null = inherit. Range 1000..120000.
  systemInfoTimeoutMs       Int?  -- Per-request timeout (ms) for the interface / storage / LLDP collector. null = inherit. Range 1000..120000.
  cpuMemoryIntervalSeconds  Int?
  temperatureIntervalSeconds Int?
  systemInfoIntervalSeconds Int?
  customWidgetIntervalSeconds Int?
  customWidgetTimeoutMs     Int?
  -- Legacy single-tier retention (unused going forward — global Setting("sampleRetention") supersedes):
  sampleRetentionDays       Int?
  telemetryRetentionDays    Int?
  systemInfoRetentionDays   Int?
  -- Tiered retention (3 streams × detail/hourly/daily) seeded by migrateRetentionTiers; also superseded by the global Setting going forward but present on the row:
  sampleDetailRetentionDays      Int?
  sampleHourlyRetentionDays      Int?
  sampleDailyRetentionDays       Int?
  telemetryDetailRetentionDays   Int?
  telemetryHourlyRetentionDays   Int?
  telemetryDailyRetentionDays    Int?
  systemInfoDetailRetentionDays  Int?
  systemInfoHourlyRetentionDays  Int?
  systemInfoDailyRetentionDays   Int?
  -- Per-stream polling overrides. storagePolling has no companion credential /
  -- MIB column — storage reuses the interfaces credential at probe time and
  -- HOST-RESOURCES-MIB + the vendor disk fallback in pickVendorProfileMerged
  -- covers OID selection.
  responseTimePolling       String?
  cpuMemoryPolling          String?
  temperaturePolling        String?
  interfacesPolling         String?
  lldpPolling               String?
  storagePolling            String?
  customWidgetPolling       String?
  -- Per-stream credential FKs (set null on delete) — surfaced onto the resolved
  -- *CredentialId fields by resolveMonitorSettings; looked up via loadClassOverrideStreamCredential.
  responseTimeCredentialId  UUID? FK → Credential
  cpuMemoryCredentialId     UUID? FK → Credential
  temperatureCredentialId   UUID? FK → Credential
  interfacesCredentialId    UUID? FK → Credential
  lldpCredentialId          UUID? FK → Credential
  customWidgetCredentialId  UUID? FK → Credential
  @@unique([integrationId, assetType])
  -- Postgres treats nulls as distinct in unique indexes, so the
  -- @@unique([integrationId, assetType]) alone won't prevent two
  -- (null, "switch") rows. The route layer enforces uniqueness for the
  -- manual-tier case before insert.

Tag
  id            UUID PK
  name          String @unique
  category      String @default("General")
  color         String @default("#4fc3f7")
  criteria      Json?            -- optional auto-assignment criteria; NULL = ordinary manual tag. Shape `{version:1, match:"all", rules:[{field, op, values[]} | {field:"subnet", op:"inCidr", cidrs[]}]}` (rules ANDed, values/cidrs ORed). When set, `tagAssignmentService` keeps the tag synced onto matching assets (managed sync). See `tagAssignmentService`.

TagAutoAssignment                -- Provenance for criteria-based tag auto-assignment: one row per (tag, asset) pair the engine itself applied. Lets managed sync strip a tag when an asset stops matching WITHOUT touching a hand-applied copy of the same tag name (no provenance row). No FK to Tag/Asset (denormalized tags-by-name design, same no-cascade rationale as sample tables); rows cleaned by the engine on tag delete / criteria clear / asset drift.
RegionTagAssignment              -- The same provenance pattern for map-region tags: one row per (regionId, targetType, targetId) pair mapRegionService itself tagged, where targetType is "asset" | "subnet" (regions propagate to both halves, which is why tag_auto_assignments' (tagId, assetId) PK can't be reused). Keyed by region id rather than tag name so a rename leaves it untouched. Bounds the reconcile's strip half: a target that drifted out of the region loses the tag only when a provenance row says we put it there — no row = operator-owned (or predates provenance) and survives forever. No FKs (regions live in a Setting JSON blob; the asset/subnet side follows TagAutoAssignment's rationale); rows cleaned on region delete and on drift.
  tagId         String
  assetId       String
  createdAt     DateTime @default(now())
  @@id([tagId, assetId])

GeocodeCache                    -- Positive+negative cache for `geocoderService.geocode()`. Negative results (no Nominatim hit) are stored too so gibberish sysLocation strings don't repeatedly hit upstream. Refreshed on TTL expiry; transport failures don't poison the cache.
  id           UUID PK
  query        String @unique  -- normalized lookup key: trim + collapse whitespace + lowercased
  displayQuery String           -- original-case query string for UI display
  latitude     Float?           -- null = geocoded but no result found (negative cache)
  longitude    Float?
  provider     String           -- "nominatim"
  fetchedAt    DateTime
  ttlExpiresAt DateTime         -- default fetchedAt + 90 days

MibFile                         -- Admin-uploaded SNMP MIB modules used to resolve vendor-specific OIDs during monitoring
  id            UUID PK
  filename      String           -- original upload filename
  moduleName    String           -- parsed from "<NAME> DEFINITIONS ::= BEGIN" (validated as a real SMI module on upload — non-MIB text or binaries are rejected)
  manufacturer  String?          -- null = generic/shared MIB (loaded for every probe). Normalized through the ManufacturerAlias map on every write via the Prisma extension in src/db.ts.
  model         String?          -- null = applies to all models from this manufacturer
  contents      String           -- raw MIB text, stored inline (MIBs are normally <100 KB; cap = 1 MB)
  imports       String[]         -- module names referenced via IMPORTS ... FROM (used to surface missing dependencies in the UI)
  size          Int              -- byte length of contents
  notes         String?
  uploadedBy    String?
  uploadedAt    DateTime
  @@unique([manufacturer, model, moduleName])  -- Postgres treats NULLs as distinct, so the service layer also rejects duplicate generic MIBs
  -- `assetId` (Slice 6a) pins a MIB to one specific asset — the most-specific tier of the resolver priority (asset → model → manufacturer → generic → seed). SetNull on asset delete so the MIB text stays reachable for download/audit. Selectable from a new Scope radio group on the MIB upload form.

ManufacturerProfile             -- Operator-editable per-manufacturer telemetry profile. Replaces the hardcoded VENDOR_TELEMETRY_PROFILES constant at runtime; the constant stays as a fresh-install fallback until the resolver swap lands. Seeded idempotently from the constant on first boot via `seedManufacturerProfiles` startup job.
  id            UUID PK
  manufacturer  String @unique     -- canonical form via the ManufacturerAlias map
  createdBy, createdAt, updatedAt
  -- One row per alias-canonicalized manufacturer. Metric rows + per-model overrides + custom widgets are nested below. Edited from Server Settings → Credentials → Manufacturer Profiles. Cache lives in manufacturerProfileService.refreshProfileCache; hot reads are sync.

ManufacturerProfileMetric       -- One row per System-tab metric the profile owns: cpu / memory / temperature / interfaces / lldp / storage / wirelessStations
  id              UUID PK
  profileId       UUID FK → ManufacturerProfile (cascade)
  metricKey       String           -- "cpu" | "memory" | "temperature" | "interfaces" | "lldp" | "storage" | "wirelessStations"
  defaultSymbol   String?          -- null = use built-in seed for this metric. For `defaultType="double_scalar"` this is the "A" OID; for `scalar`/`table` it's the single OID.
  defaultSymbolB  String?          -- Second OID for the `double_scalar` shape (the "B" OID). Combined with `defaultSymbol` via the combiner in `defaultTransform` at probe time. Null on `scalar` / `table` — the service write-path force-nulls it whenever `defaultType !== "double_scalar"` so an old value from a previous double_scalar config can't get accidentally re-promoted.
  defaultMibId    UUID? FK → MibFile (set null on delete)
  defaultMibStdKey String?         -- Operator-pinned standard MIB hint (e.g. `"std:lldp"`, `"std:host-resources"` — keys mirror `_SNMP_STANDARD_MIBS` in `public/js/assets.js` and `STD_MIB_KEYS` in `manufacturerProfileService.ts`). Mutually exclusive with `defaultMibId` — picking a standard MIB in the UI clears the uploaded-MIB FK and vice versa; the service rejects requests that set both as non-null. Display-only at probe time (the resolver still walks asset → model → vendor → generic → seed); lets the Manufacturer Profile MIB column show a meaningful label for metrics whose symbol comes from a built-in seed rather than the literal word "seed".
  defaultType     String           -- "scalar" | "double_scalar" | "table"
  defaultTransform String?         -- For `scalar`/`table`, a unary `TransformKind` (`celsius_to_fahrenheit` / `bytes_to_mb` / `ratio_to_percent` / ...); for `double_scalar`, a binary `CombinerKind` (`a_over_b_as_percent` / `a_over_a_plus_b_as_percent` / `b_minus_a_over_b_as_percent` / `a_minus_b` / `a_plus_b` / `a_over_b_ratio`). Null on `table`, optional on the other two. Validated at write time against the matching registry in `src/utils/symbolTransforms.ts` based on `defaultType` — a unary transform on a `double_scalar` row (or a combiner on a `scalar` row) is a 400 at the service layer.
  composition     Json?            -- DEPRECATED. Was the memory-only multi-OID blob (`{ shape, usedSymbol?, totalSymbol?, freeSymbol?, pctSymbol? }`). Superseded by the generic `defaultType="double_scalar" + defaultSymbolB + defaultTransform=<CombinerKind>` shape that any metric can now use. Kept on the schema for one release as a rollback safety net for the data migration that promoted existing rows; the `20260531000000_manufacturer_profile_double_scalar` SQL migration walks every row with a non-null composition and rewrites it into the new columns (`percent → scalar`; `bytes_used_total → double_scalar + a_over_b_as_percent`; `bytes_used_free → double_scalar + a_over_a_plus_b_as_percent`). New writes MUST NOT populate this column; new reads ignore it. To be dropped in a follow-up migration once production has settled.
  @@unique([profileId, metricKey])

ManufacturerProfileMetricOverride -- Per-model exception inside one metric row
  id             UUID PK
  metricRowId    UUID FK → ManufacturerProfileMetric (cascade)
  modelPattern   String            -- regex matched against Asset.model
  symbol         String            -- For `type="double_scalar"` this is the "A" OID; for `scalar`/`table` it's the single OID.
  symbolB        String?           -- Second OID for the `double_scalar` shape. Same write-path rules as `ManufacturerProfileMetric.defaultSymbolB` — force-nulled whenever `type !== "double_scalar"`.
  mibId          UUID? FK → MibFile (set null on delete)
  mibStdKey      String?           -- Per-override standard MIB hint; same mutual-exclusion contract as `ManufacturerProfileMetric.defaultMibStdKey`.
  type           String            -- "scalar" | "double_scalar" | "table"
  transform      String?           -- TransformKind on scalar / table; CombinerKind on double_scalar; null on table.
  order          Int               -- evaluation order (lower wins)
  composition    Json?             -- DEPRECATED. Same rationale + removal plan as `ManufacturerProfileMetric.composition`.
  -- Resolved at probe time by walking overrides in `order` and picking the first whose `modelPattern` regex matches `Asset.model`; no matches falls back to the parent metric row's defaults. Seeded entries cover the Fortinet sub-families: `FortiSwitch → fsSysCpuUsage / fsSysMemUsage / fsSysDiskUsage`, `FortiAP → fapCpuUsage / fapMemoryUsage / fapTemperature`. The FortiSwitch memory override is stamped as `type="double_scalar", symbol="fsSysMemUsage", symbolB="fsSysMemCapacity", transform="a_over_b_as_percent"` so the editable profile matches the hardcoded baseline's bytes-form semantics. Existing installs receive the promotion via the `backfillManufacturerProfileMemoryComposition` startup job (kept its legacy name for marker-key back-compat).

ManufacturerCustomWidget        -- Powers Slice 7's Custom MIB tab. Every asset whose alias-normalized manufacturer matches the parent profile (and whose model satisfies the optional `modelPattern` gate) renders this widget against its own SNMP data.
  id             UUID PK
  profileId      UUID FK → ManufacturerProfile (cascade)
  name           String            -- operator-set label, e.g. "Connected Wireless Clients"
  symbol         String
  mibId          UUID FK → MibFile -- required (custom widgets always reference an uploaded MIB)
  type           String            -- "scalar" | "table" (auto-detected from MIB; operator may override)
  widgetType     String            -- "gauge" | "line" | "table" | "state"
  transform      String?
  displayOptions Json              -- type-specific blob (gauge min/max + thresholds; line aggregate/range/unit; table column list / decode rules)
  order          Int
  modelPattern   String?           -- optional per-model gating
  stateMap       Json?             -- STATE PROBE (widgetType="state") only: the declared 0/1 mapping `{mode, values[], trueLabel, falseLabel, trueIsProblem}` — see src/utils/stateProbes.ts. Nullable, and forced to NULL on non-state widgets by stateFieldsForWrite so flipping a widget's type can't leave a stale mapping for a later flip back to resurrect. Read back through normalizeStateMap (never throws) so a row predating a mode still yields a usable mapping on the telemetry hot path.
  labelSymbol    String?           -- STATE PROBE only: optional sibling symbol supplying each TABLE row's name, joined to the value walk on the shared OID index suffix (fgHwSensorEntName beside fgHwSensorEntAlarm). Without it rows are only nameable by bare index, which differs per model — so an alert would read "row .14 is in Alarm". Ignored on scalar probes.
  -- Widget definitions are configured under their parent ManufacturerProfile. The Slice 7 collector + asset details tab consume these rows; Slice 6a only owns persistence and the admin CRUD surface.
  -- A widgetType="state" row is a STATE PROBE rather than a rendered widget: the same walk, but each reading is mapped to a boolean at scrape time and written to AssetStateSample, which makes it alertable per row via the `customStateValue` automation metric. It still renders on the Custom MIB tab (as a per-row OK/Alarm list). `listStateProbes()` flattens every profile's probes for the automation builder, which needs each probe's NAME (its dimension value is this UUID) and its two state LABELS.

ManufacturerAlias               -- Vendor name normalization map; collapses IEEE legal forms into a single canonical brand
  id            UUID PK
  alias         String @unique  -- input string to rewrite, stored lowercased + trimmed (e.g. "fortinet, inc.")
  canonical     String          -- canonical name the alias rewrites to (e.g. "Fortinet"), stored as-typed
  -- Loaded into an in-memory cache by manufacturerAliasService.refreshAliasCache() at startup and after every CRUD mutation. The Prisma extension in src/db.ts reads the cache to canonicalize Asset.manufacturer / MibFile.manufacturer on every create/update/updateMany/upsert. Mutations also run applyAliasesToExistingRows() in the background so admin edits propagate to historical data. Default seed (idempotent) ships ~25 common IEEE → marketing-name mappings (Fortinet, Inc. → Fortinet, Cisco Systems, Inc. → Cisco, etc.); admins extend the map from Server Settings → Identification → Manufacturer Aliases.

DeviceIcon                      -- Operator-uploaded topology node icons; resolved per (scope, key) most-specific-first (manufacturer-model → manufacturer-type)
  id            UUID PK
  scope         String          -- "manufacturer-model" | "manufacturer-type"
  key           String          -- canonical "<manufacturer>/<model|assetType>" lookup key
  filename      String
  mimeType      String          -- PNG/JPEG/WebP; SVG uploads are rasterized to PNG on upload (see deviceIconService + rasterizeStoredSvgIcons job)
  data          Bytes           -- raw image bytes stored inline
  size          Int
  uploadedBy    String?
  uploadedAt    DateTime
  @@unique([scope, key])

NotificationRule                -- Operator-defined alert definition (plain table notification_rules). Flexible discriminated `trigger` JSON (asset_metric | asset_state | host_metric | event | change) + asset `scope`, per-rule `clearBehavior` (manual | auto | timed) + clearAfterSec + cooldownSec, messageTemplate, channels (default ["in_app"]), and `targets` JSON (outbound delivery: array of { channelId, recipientUserIds?, addresses?, recipientScopeRegion?, recipientTags?(legacy) } referencing NotificationChannel rows — recipients combine individual users + custom emails + (when recipientScopeRegion) users matching the rule's scope region: tag(s); routing applies only to email/web_push channels). Optional `emailComposition` JSON (rule-level outbound-email customization: subjectTemplate/bodyTextTemplate/bodyHtmlTemplate + cc/bcc {recipientUserIds?, addresses?}; single-brace {token} templates from src/utils/notificationTemplate.ts; when set, each email target sends one To+Cc+Bcc message instead of per-address fan-out; NULL = legacy behavior) and optional `escalation` JSON (stored as posted — legacy email tiers { afterMin, channelId, to, cc?, bcc?, template overrides?, repeatEveryMin?, maxRepeats? } OR v2 tiers of actions { afterMin, actions[≤10], repeatEveryMin?, maxRepeats? }; ≤5 tiers, stopOn acknowledge|clear; every reader normalizes via normalizeEscalationToV2; swept by escalateNotifications through executeActions — the email-only tier restriction is gone). Evaluated by `notificationEngine` on the evaluateNotificationRules job; targets expanded by `notificationRecipientService` on fire. CRUD gated `automationManagement`. Owned by `notificationRuleService`; vocabulary in `notificationTypes`. **Rule-shape v2 (2026-07):** nullable `reset` Json ({mode manual|auto|timed|condition, clearThreshold? hysteresis, sustainSec? clear-sustain, afterSec?, condition? reset tree}) supersedes clearBehavior/clearAfterSec, and nullable `actions` Json (array of notify | api_call | script) supersedes `targets`. Every reader goes through `normalizeRuleToV2`; the `migrateAutomationRuleShape` one-shot persists v2 onto pre-v2 rows; CRUD writes v2 AND rewrites the legacy columns as a lossless mirror (`legacyMirrorOfV2` — condition mode mirrors as clearBehavior="auto") so pre-wizard UIs / pre-upgrade backups stay coherent. Script actions validate against the AutomationScript registry at save and additionally require automationScripts=fullwrite at the route. **Composite triggers (2026-07):** the trigger union gains `{type:"composite", kind:"asset"|"host", op:and|or, children:[leaf|group], forDurationSec}` — a nested AND/OR tree whose leaves are the asset_metric/asset_state (kind=asset) or host_metric (kind=host) conditions minus per-leaf forDurationSec; ≤3 deep / 2–10 leaves, and/or only (negation ops would fire on data absence), validated by `validateCompositeTrigger`. Composite rules evaluate PER ASSET (multi-dimension leaves met on ANY dimension, one alert per device at dimensionKey "") while single-condition rules keep per-dimension alerting + hysteresis; the input transforms enforce that split via `collapseCompositeTrigger` (a 1-leaf composite folds to the legacy single trigger with forDurationSec hoisted, whatever client authored it). Reset mode `condition` = a custom reset tree (same leaf vocabulary, v1-restricted to composite triggers of the same kind); `isAssetScopedTrigger` is the scoped-trigger check (composite is scoped iff kind="asset"). **Severity bands + precedence (2026-07, migration 20260726000000):** nullable `severityBands` Json (numeric asset_metric/host_metric triggers only) stacks higher tiers on tier 0 (base severity+threshold) — each `{threshold, severity, operator?, forDurationSec?, actions[], escalation?}` carries its own actions + time-escalation + **sustained duration** (omitted = inherit the base trigger's `forDurationSec`; 0 = apply immediately); `severityForValue` picks the most-severe satisfied tier instantaneously while `resolveTierLadder`/`updateTierMetSince`/`sustainedSeverity` add the per-tier hold time (the engine's actual severity decision, backed by `NotificationRuleState.bandMetSince`), the alert climbs/eases severity in place per the nullable `bandNotify` Json policy ({onIncrease, onDecrease, onResolved, resolvedMode reuse|dedicated, resolvedActions?}), validated by `validateSeverityBands`. Precedence carve-out (no column — derived at eval time): `triggerSignature` (metric/field+dimensionFilter; null for host/event/change/composite) + `scopeRank` ladder (all<type<os<manufacturer<model<tag<region<subnet<hostname) let a more-specific automation shadow same-signature lower-rank ones (`buildShadowIndex`/`isAssetShadowed`); `scope.condition` `assetId` still evaluates but is off the builder + off the ladder. **Reset actions (2026-08, migration 20260812010000):** nullable `resetActions` Json — plain (non-escalatable) actions that run when the alert ENDS: auto/hysteresis/condition recovery via `recover()`, both timed sweeps, `runEventRuleTimedClear` (which now selects the alerts rather than bulk-updating a count, since an action is per-alert), and an operator clear via notificationService.clearNotifications. Executed by `fireReset` BEFORE the notification is cleared so deliveries + ack tokens attach to a live id; context uses the `resolved` pseudo-severity and the message names how it ended. NULL = silent (every pre-feature rule). Eighth location in `allRuleActionRefs`. **Actions redesign (2026-08):** top-level + severity-band actions may carry their OWN `escalation` chain (`escalatableActionSchema`; tier actions + resolvedActions stay bare so chains can't nest — state keys `a<i>:t<j>` per `escalationTierStateKey`, level chain keeps bare numeric keys), notify actions/targets take `recipientDeviceRegion` (route to users matching the TRIGGERING asset's region: tags; scope-region flag still honored on old rules), and `allRuleActionRefs` is the canonical walk every gate (automationScripts route check, assertActionRefs, ruleWantsAssetDetail) collects through.
NotificationChannel             -- Operator-configured outbound delivery integration (plain table notification_channels; Automations → Delivery tab). `type` (smtp | oauth_m365 | pushbullet | slack | teams | web_push) selects transport + config shape; `config` JSON holds type-specific settings with secrets masked on read / preserved on write. web_push is a singleton (one server VAPID keypair). Owned by `notificationChannelService`; CRUD gated `automationManagement`.
Notification                    -- A triggered notification instance (plain table notifications; View tab + asset-details tab). Snapshotted `regionTags` (region: prefix stripped → compares to viewer region tags) + assetHostname so it survives asset deletion. `templateCtx` JSON (fire-time token→string context, written only when the rule has emailComposition/escalation; escalation emails render from it) + `escalationState` JSON (per-tier { firstSentAt, lastSentAt, count } from the escalation sweep; drives the View-tab "Escalated" marker). Soft-clear (`cleared`) keeps history. `dimension` + `metric` snapshot WHAT fired (the engine's dimensionKey — for a hardware-sensor automation the bare sensor name — and the metric key), because the email is rendered at DELIVERY time and needs both to chart the right sensor and to lead with the chart that explains the alert. `testRun` marks an alert raised by the automation wizard's Test-delivery buttons rather than a real trigger — such a row ALWAYS carries ruleId = null (notificationEscalationService sweeps { cleared:false, ruleId: IN enabled }, so a test alert with a real ruleId would enter the escalation ladder and start paging people), which is why the flag is a column and not an inference. Acknowledge links for its recipients hang off it via NotificationAckToken. View `alerts:read`, acknowledge `alerts:write`, clear `alerts:fullwrite`. ruleId FK → NotificationRule (SetNull). Owned by `notificationService`.
NotificationRuleState           -- Per-(rule, asset, dimension) firing state machine (plain table notification_rule_states; clear→pending→firing) for sustained-duration + debounce + auto-clear, plus `recoveredSince` (the clear-sustain timer for reset.sustainSec — firing-state only, distinct from the pending-side conditionMetSince) and `firingSeverity` (the severity band the active alert is in — severity-bands feature; drives increase/decrease/same detection) and `bandMetSince` Json (per-tier "continuously satisfied since" map `{[severity]: epochMs}` backing PER-BAND sustained durations — one shared conditionMetSince can't express "warning after 30m, critical after 5m"; rewritten only when a tier enters or leaves). assetId="" for host/global rules. Writes only on transition (capacityWatch-style guard). ruleId FK → NotificationRule (cascade). Owned by `notificationEngine`.
AutomationScript                -- Operator-authored script registry for Automation `script` actions (plain table automation_scripts). name unique, interpreter (bash|sh|powershell|cmd|python3), body ≤64KB, runTarget (server|agent|either), timeoutSec default 60 (≤600), sha256 recomputed on every save (agents verify), enabled. RCE-EQUIVALENT surface — CRUD + attaching script actions gated by `automationScripts`; create/body-change stamp warning Events. Owned by `automationScriptService`.
AutomationScriptRun             -- One execution of a registry script (plain table automation_script_runs), server- or agent-side. scriptId FK SetNull + scriptName/sha256 snapshots (survive deletion), notificationId/ruleId/assetId (NO FK — alert lifecycle independent), runOn, agentCommandId (agent runs), args snapshot, status pending|running|succeeded|failed|timeout, exitCode, stdout/stderr ≤64KB, requestedBy/At, startedAt, completedAt. Server runs claimed by runAutomationScripts; pruned after ~90d. Owned by `automationScriptService` + `automationScriptRunner`.
MaintenanceSchedule             -- Operator-defined maintenance window definition (plain table maintenance_schedules; Assets page → Maintenance modal, gated maintenanceManagement). name + enabled + `criteria` JSON (tagAssignmentService vocabulary — hostname/model/manufacturer/os/osVersion contains|exact|pattern, subnet inCidr, assetType, integration (exact-only Integration id; matches discoveredByIntegrationId OR any AssetSource row), fortigate ("behind FortiGate" device name, string ops over learnedLocation + AssetFortigateSighting rows); `status` rules rejected at save since the feature itself flips status) + `assetIds` String[] (explicit targets — the ad-hoc pill path; unioned with criteria matches, always ∩ monitored=true) + `schedule` JSON (recurrence shape validated by src/utils/maintenanceRecurrence.ts: oneshot {startAt,endAt} | recurring daily/weekly(daysOfWeek)/monthly(dayOfMonth, clamped)/yearly(month+day) with optional startTime/endTime (endTime ≤ startTime spans midnight, matched on the START day) + optional activeFrom/activeUntil date bounds — all SERVER-LOCAL wall-clock, evaluated per tick so DST needs no special handling). Also carries `suppressChildren` (default true): whether an in-window asset counts as DOWN for child dependency suppression — false = suppression ignores the maintenance status and the asset evaluates by its frozen monitorStatus, so dependents keep monitoring/alerting (redundant-path / clustered parents). OR-ed across an asset's open windows by `reconcileDependencySuppression`. Reconciled by the maintenanceScheduler job (30s) AND inline on every CRUD write. Ad-hoc-shaped schedules (one-shot + no criteria + one explicit asset) self-delete once spent: on operator release and on natural window end (reconcile sweep, `nextWindow` guard; disable never auto-deletes) — closed windows keep the scheduleName snapshot. Owned by `maintenanceScheduleService`. See CLAUDE.md business rule 16.
AssetMaintenanceWindow          -- One realized maintenance window per (asset, schedule) (plain table asset_maintenance_windows). Opened when the reconcile enters the asset for that schedule; closed with endedAt + endReason ("schedule" | "operator" | "disabled" | "deleted" | "criteria" | "decommissioned" — the last written by `releaseAssetsForDecommission` when a discovery sweep finds the device deleted at its source mid-window and decommissions it outright). Open rows (endedAt NULL) are the restart-safe source of truth for "in maintenance" — an asset enters on its FIRST open row (status parked to Asset.maintenanceReturnStatus, flipped to "maintenance") and exits when its LAST closes (status restored). scheduleName snapshot keeps chart-band labels after schedule deletion. assetId FK → Asset (cascade — plain table, the hypertable no-FK rule doesn't apply); scheduleId FK → MaintenanceSchedule (SetNull). Closed rows > ~400 days pruned by the reconcile. Read by GET /assets/:id/maintenance-windows (chart bands) + /maintenance-info.
Contact                         -- An address-book entry (plain table contacts): a named email address alerts can route to, whether or not the recipient holds a Polaris account — a distribution list, an on-call rotation, a vendor NOC. `email` is UNIQUE and stored trimmed + lower-cased (so the index is case-insensitive and the value compares directly against resolveEmailRecipients' normalized set), plus optional `name` / `description`. Device ownership rides the MaintenanceSchedule target shape: `assetCriteria` JSON (tagAssignmentService vocabulary) UNIONED with `assetIds` String[] explicit pins — deliberately NOT intersected with monitored=true (an unmonitored device still has an owner worth emailing; event/change automations fire on it). `createdBy` backs the ownership dimension on the `contacts` function key: write = manage your own rows, fullwrite = anyone's, the same mechanism subnets/reservations use. Owned by `contactService`; surfaced on Automations → Address Book and in the automation wizard's recipient picker.
HostMetricsSample               -- Polaris host CPU/mem/load time-series (plain prunable table host_metrics_samples) sampled every 30s by `hostMetricsCollector`; `host_metric` rules read the latest row. 7-day retention. NO FK.
NotificationDelivery            -- One outbound delivery per (notification, channel, concrete recipient) (plain table notification_deliveries). `channelId` FK → NotificationChannel (SetNull; a null channel on a pending row is a permanent fail — except api_call, where NULL is the designed shape) + `transport` (email | webhook | web_push | pushbullet | api_call, dispatch routing — api_call rows carry channelId NULL by design with the full request spec in meta {apiCall, method, url, headers, body, timeoutSec}) + target (recipient address / push endpoint; "" for fixed-destination channels whose URL/token lives on the channel; joined To list for composed emails) + meta (web_push keys, or the composed-email snapshot { composed: true, to[], cc[], bcc[], subject, text, html?, escalation?: {tier, attempt} } — rendered content + addresses only, never channel secrets) + status (pending | sent | failed) + attempts. Expanded at fire time by `notificationRecipientService` (escalation rows inserted by the escalation sweep); drained by the deliverNotifications job — rows without meta.composed take the legacy per-address path. notificationId FK → Notification (cascade). In-app delivery is NOT represented here (it's the Notification row).
NotificationAckToken            -- A single-use, opaque one-click acknowledge link (plain table notification_ack_tokens). One row per (notification, user recipient, channel), minted at delivery fan-out by notificationRecipientService and delivered inside the alert email / web-push payload; redeemed by the public /ack page. tokenHash (base64url sha256, UNIQUE — the raw token exists only in the delivered message and in NotificationDelivery.meta.ack) + notificationId FK → Notification (Cascade) + userId FK → User (Cascade) + channel ("email" | "web_push", provenance for the acknowledged Event) + expiresAt (30 days) + usedAt. Minted ONLY for recipients who are configured Polaris users holding alerts:write — an address-book contact is an address with no account to attribute the acknowledgement to — and redemption re-checks that permission live, so a role downgrade invalidates links already sitting in mailboxes. sha256 rather than the argon2id + prefix-walk ApiToken/agent tokens use: see src/utils/ackToken.ts for why (entropy, and ~50ms/recipient on the fan-out path). Swept hourly by the deliverNotifications tick (`pruneAckTokens`). Owned by `notificationAckService`.
PushSubscription                -- A browser/PWA Web Push subscription owned by a user (plain table push_subscriptions). endpoint (unique) + p256dh + auth keys + userAgent + surface. Stored via POST /push-subscriptions; the web_push delivery channel sends to a recipient user's endpoints via web-push signed with the server VAPID keypair; a 410/404 prunes the row. userId FK → User (cascade). `surface` ("desktop" | "mobile", default desktop — migration 20260807000000) records which Polaris surface enrolled, because subscribe time is the ONLY moment we know: on Android the installed PWA and the browser share one subscription, so nothing downstream can tell them apart. notificationRecipientService snapshots it into the delivery row's meta and the drain turns it into the push deep link (mobile → /mobile.html#more/alerts, desktop → /automations.html) via `pushDeepLinkUrl`. A rotation (sw.js `pushsubscriptionchange`) mints a NEW endpoint, so the POST may carry `oldEndpoint` — the retiring row's surface is carried forward and the row retired, scoped to the caller's own userId so a guessed endpoint can't read or delete another user's row.
ManagedAgent                    -- Polaris Agent install record; one row per asset (@@unique assetId). `installScriptId` = curated OS-locked install-method variant (agentInstallScripts catalog; null = per-OS default). `privilegeTier` (String, default "unprivileged"; Linux-only) selects the systemd unit via utils/agentUnit.linuxServiceBlock: "unprivileged" = hardened DynamicUser/NoNewPrivileges/ProtectSystem=strict; "ptrace" = that + AmbientCapabilities=CAP_SYS_PTRACE CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH for Application Map connection→PID attribution without full root (operator opt-in with a warning — the pair also reads any process's memory and any file on the host; both are required, since /proc/<pid>/fd of a foreign process DAC-fails without DAC_READ_SEARCH — agents installed with the earlier SYS_PTRACE-only unit collect no connections until reinstalled). Legacy "root" survives only on pre-migration rows (backfilled from the old runAsRoot Bool by migration 20260725000400) and is never emitted for new installs — full root was retired with service control; reinstalling a legacy-root agent downgrades it. Ignored on Windows (LocalSystem) / macOS (LaunchDaemon = root). `reportedCapEff` (migration 20260729000100) is the VERIFIED counterpart to the requested tier: the raw CapEff hex the agent reads from its own /proc/self/status and reports on heartbeat (agent ≥0.17.1, Linux only; null = not reported). Decoded by utils/capEff; a ptrace-tier row whose mask lacks CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH renders as "stale unit — reinstall" on the Privilege surfaces. Full lifecycle in ARCHITECTURE.md → Monitoring Architecture.
AgentCommand                    -- The agent command queue (plain table agent_commands). Only action is agent-side automation script runs (action="run_script", nullable payload Json {runId, interpreter, body, sha256, args, timeoutSec} — body inline ≤64KB, sha256 verified agent-side; queued by automationScriptService.requestScriptRun for active agents ≥0.13.0 only). status pending|sent|succeeded|failed. The agent polls `GET /agents/commands` (marks them sent; the ≤20s poll is the guaranteed floor, a `commands-pending` WS frame from agentCommandWake wakes it sooner), executes via the scriptexec sandbox, reports `POST /agents/command-result` (→ succeeded|failed + audit). Owned by `agentCommandService` (fetchPendingCommands / recordCommandResult). NO FK. **Process/service start/stop/restart control was removed** (Satellite-posture change): the stop/start/restart actions, their routes, requestProcessControl/requestServiceControl, and the agent servicecontrol collectors are gone; the agent refuses any non-run_script action.
  id                    UUID PK
  assetId               UUID FK → Asset (cascade delete) @unique  -- binds the bearer to one asset; defends against stolen-bearer cross-asset reuse
  osPlatform            String          -- "linux" | "darwin" | "windows"
  arch                  String          -- "amd64" | "arm64"
  agentVersion          String?         -- semver reported on enroll; null until first enroll
  installedBy           String          -- operator username who clicked Install
  installedAt           DateTime
  installCredentialId   UUID? FK → Credential (set null on delete) -- SSH/WinRM creds, reused by the default remote-uninstall path
  installTransport      String          -- "ssh" | "winrm"; chosen at install time. linux/darwin = ssh only; windows defaults to winrm but can be ssh when the target runs OpenSSH Server. Persisted so retry / uninstall / upgrade replay the same transport.
  installStatus         String          -- pending → uploading → enrolling → active; plus uninstalling / uninstall_failed / upgrading / upgrade_failed / revoked. `/enroll` is the normal enrolling→active transition; `verifyBearer` ALSO self-heals enrolling→active on any bearer-gated call, covering a re-push that reset status to "enrolling" while the agent reused its existing bearer and skipped /enroll.
  installError          String?
  enrollmentTokenHash   String?         -- one-shot 10-min enrollment token (argon2id); NULLed atomically on successful POST /agents/enroll
  enrollmentTokenPrefix String?
  enrollmentExpiresAt   DateTime?
  bearerHash            String?         -- long-lived per-agent bearer (argon2id, prefix-indexed); wire format polaris_<32-char-base62>
  bearerPrefix          String?
  bearerIssuedAt        DateTime?
  bearerRevokedAt       DateTime?
  lastSeenAt            DateTime?
  lastSeenIp            String?
  wsConnectedAt         DateTime?
  wsDisconnectedAt      DateTime?
  serverCertFingerprint            String   -- canonical sha256:<hex> pinned at install; checked server-side at enroll + client-side on every TLS handshake. Phase 2 dual-pin: the FIRST pin in the trust set (legacy `cert_fingerprint` line in agent.conf points here).
  additionalServerCertFingerprints String[] -- Phase 2 dual-pin: operator-staged additional pins for zero-downtime cert rotation. Empty in steady state. Enroll cross-check accepts ANY pin in the union; agent's TLS verifier accepts the presented cert if its SHA-256 matches ANY pin. See cross-cutting/polaris-agent → "Cert pin rotation" in TOUCHES.md.
  createdAt             DateTime
  updatedAt             DateTime
```

---

## API Endpoints

All routes are prefixed `/api/v1/`. Auth guards are applied in `src/api/router.ts`.

### Auth — public
- `POST   /auth/login`
- `POST   /auth/logout`
- `GET    /auth/me`                             — Session probe. Returns `{ authenticated: false }` for unauthenticated callers; otherwise `{ authenticated: true, username, authProvider, role: { id, name, color, isProtected, permissions, updatedAt }, regionTags: { user, role, group, effective }, otherTags: { user, role, group, effective } }` (`color` read live each call; `group` is re-resolved from `User.ssoGroups` via `resolveGroupsToAccess` so a GroupMapping edit shows next page load without re-login). The frontend reads `role.permissions[functionKey]` to gate menu items / buttons (see `permAtLeast()` in `public/js/app.js`).
- `GET    /auth/azure/config`                   — Azure SSO feature flag
- `GET    /auth/azure/login`                    — Initiate Azure SAML login
- `POST   /auth/azure/callback`                 — SAML assertion callback
- `POST   /auth/azure/logout`                    — SAML single-logout
- `GET    /auth/oidc/config`                    — OIDC feature flag (login page button)
- `GET    /auth/oidc/login`                     — Initiate OIDC Authorization-Code login (stashes state/nonce/PKCE in session, redirects to IdP)
- `GET    /auth/oidc/callback`                  — OIDC code exchange + ID-token validation + provision. Top-level GET, so SameSite=Lax session cookies are sent (unlike the SAML POST callback)
- `GET    /auth/entra-proxy/config`             — Entra App Proxy header-SSO flag: `{ enabled, available }` (`available` = this request arrived from an allowlisted connector carrying identity headers → drives the fallback login button; booleans only). Public.
- `GET    /auth/entra-proxy/login`              — Read Entra App Proxy identity headers on THIS request, validate source-IP trust, provision, stamp session, redirect to validated `?next=` (default `/`). Both the login-page button and the app.ts silent auto-login land here; all failures redirect to `/login.html?error=…`. Rate-limited (`entraProxyLoginLimiter`, 60/5min).
- LDAP login uses the shared `POST /auth/login` form (routes to LDAP when the account is an LDAP user or the username is unknown and LDAP is enabled)
- SSO/LDAP config (admin, `serverSettingsSystem:write`): `GET|PUT /auth/azure/settings` + `POST /auth/azure/test`, `GET|PUT /auth/oidc/settings` + `POST /auth/oidc/test`, `GET|PUT /auth/ldap/settings` + `POST /auth/ldap/test`, `GET|PUT /auth/entra-proxy/settings` + `POST /auth/entra-proxy/test`
- `POST   /auth/login/totp`                     — Second step of two-phase login when TOTP is enabled. Body: `{ pendingToken, code, isBackupCode? }`. `pendingToken` is returned by `POST /auth/login` whenever the caller's account has `totpEnabledAt` set — until this endpoint consumes it, the session is not issued.

### TOTP self-management — `requireAuth`
- `GET    /auth/totp/status`                    — `{ authProvider, enabled, enrolling, backupCodesRemaining }`
- `POST   /auth/totp/enroll`                    — Starts enrollment for the current user. Returns `{ secret, otpauthUri, qrSvg }`. Only allowed on `authProvider = "local"` accounts that are not already fully enrolled.
- `POST   /auth/totp/confirm`                   — Finalize enrollment by verifying the first 6-digit code. Body: `{ code }`. Returns `{ ok, backupCodes: string[] }` — shown once.
- `DELETE /auth/totp`                           — Self-disable. Requires a current TOTP or backup code. Body: `{ code, isBackupCode? }`.

### IP Blocks — `requireAuth`
- `GET    /blocks`                              — List (filter by tag, ipVersion)
- `POST   /blocks`
- `GET    /blocks/:id`                          — Get + utilization summary
- `PUT    /blocks/:id`
- `DELETE /blocks/:id`                          — 409 if active reservations exist

### Subnets — `requireAuth`
- `GET    /subnets`                             — List (filter by blockId, status, tag, createdBy)
- `POST   /subnets`
- `GET    /subnets/:id`                         — Get + reservation list
- `PUT    /subnets/:id`
- `DELETE /subnets/:id`                         — 409 if active reservations exist
- `POST   /subnets/next-available`              — Auto-allocate next available subnet of given prefix length
- `POST   /subnets/bulk-allocate`                — Allocate multiple subnets in one call from a template. Body: `{ blockId, prefix, entries: [{name, prefixLength, vlan?} | {skip: true, prefixLength}], tags?, anchorPrefix? }`. Each non-skip entry becomes a subnet named `<prefix>_<entry.name>` (e.g. `Jefferson_Hardware`). **Skip entries** reserve address space inside the packed region without creating a subnet — used to leave gaps between allocations. **Anchor-based, all-or-nothing:** entries are packed into a single contiguous region aligned to `max(anchorPrefix, smallest-block-containing-the-group)`; `anchorPrefix` defaults to 24 if omitted. The whole call happens in one transaction — either every subnet is created or none are. Response: `{ created, anchorCidr, effectiveAnchorPrefix }`.
- `POST   /subnets/bulk-allocate/preview`        — Non-mutating preview of the above. Same body minus `prefix` and `tags`, with a lenient entry schema (no name required) so the modal can live-update footprint while the user is still filling rows. Response: `{ fits, anchorCidr, effectiveAnchorPrefix, assignments, totalAddresses, slashTwentyFourCount, blockCidr, error }`.
- `POST   /subnets/:id/refresh`                  *(user-or-above)* — Per-subnet "refresh from device" action invoked by the **Refresh** button in the IP panel slide-in. Queries the originating FortiGate for ONE DHCP scope (CMDB reservations + live leases) using whichever transport the integration is configured for (FMG proxy / FMG direct / standalone FortiGate REST), reconciles against Polaris's reservation rows for the same subnet, and bumps `Subnet.lastDiscoveredAt` on success. Intentionally narrower than the full `discoverDhcpSubnets` pipeline — only touches `dhcp_reservation` + `dhcp_lease` rows on this subnet, leaves manual / VIP / interface-IP rows alone (the IP-level conflict reconciliation that the full sync runs is deferred to the next integration-wide discovery cycle). 400 when the subnet wasn't discovered by an FMG/FortiGate integration or has no `fortigateDevice`. Returns `{ lastDiscoveredAt, created, updated, released, skipped }`. Writes one `subnet.refresh` Event. See `subnetRefreshService.ts`.

### Reservations — `requireAuth`
- `GET    /reservations`                        — List (filter by owner, projectRef, status, createdBy). Each row is decorated with `pushEligible: boolean` computed from the row's `subnet.integration` (true when the originating integration is `fortimanager`/`fortigate` AND `config.pushReservations === true` AND `ipAddress` is non-null). The integration config blob is stripped from the response — callers only need the computed flag and config can carry credentials. The mobile Reservations tab uses this flag to color the **Reserve** button green when confirming will also write the entry to the FortiGate.
- `POST   /reservations`                        — Create. An omitted `owner` auto-stamps to the caller's username (mirrors the PUT auto-stamp; an explicitly typed owner wins). Body accepts an optional `macAddress` (12 hex with optional `:`, `-`, or `.` separators). When the target subnet was discovered by an FMG integration with `pushReservations=true`, MAC becomes **required** and the create attempts a write+verify against the FortiGate — see `reservationPushService.ts`. Outcomes: (a) push success → reservation returned with `pushStatus="synced"` and `pushedScopeId`/`pushedEntryId` stamped; (b) **transient device-side failure** (FortiGate offline, FMG unreachable, network timeout, generic 5xx — classified by `classifyPushError`) → reservation persists with `pushStatus="pending"`, `pushQueuedAt=now`, `pushAttempts=1`, `pushError=<message>`, and the retry job pushes it once the gate recovers (see "Queued push lifecycle" below); (c) **permanent failure** (4xx, verify mismatch, auth) → create aborts with a clear 4xx/5xx (no Polaris ghost). **Pre-flight optimization**: if the originating FortiGate's firewall Asset is monitored AND `monitorStatus="down"`, the transport attempt is skipped entirely and the row is queued immediately (saves the 15s+ transport timeout on the create critical path). Audit Events: `reservation.push.succeeded` (info, synced path), `reservation.push.queued` (info, transient path), `reservation.push.failed` (warning, permanent path) — in addition to the usual `reservation.created` Event. The same MAC + push behavior applies to `POST /reservations/next-available`.
- `GET    /reservations/:id`
- `PUT    /reservations/:id`                    — Update. Body accepts `hostname` / `owner` / `projectRef` / `expiresAt` / `notes` plus `macAddress` (string; empty clears it, only allowed on non-push-eligible subnets). When the subnet is push-eligible AND the MAC changes, the service pushes a PUT to the FortiOS reserved-address entry via `updatePushedReservation()`, verifies on read-back, then commits the Polaris write — device-side failure throws and the Polaris row stays untouched so the two views never drift. Discovered (never-pushed) DHCP reservations look the entry up by IP on the resolved scope and are upgraded to "Polaris-pushed" on success. Hostname-only or notes-only changes are NOT re-pushed (the FortiOS description only refreshes as a side effect of a MAC update — when MAC changes, the new hostname/notes are picked up alongside). **Queued rows (`pushStatus="pending"`) skip the device-update path entirely** — the new payload is just stashed in Polaris and the retry job will use it on the next push attempt. MAC may be freely changed on a queued row (still required, can't be cleared). Audit: `reservation.push.updated` (info) on success, `reservation.push.update_failed` (warning) on failure.
- `DELETE /reservations/:id`                    — Release. Best-effort unpush from the FortiGate before flipping the row to `released`. Device-side failure does **not** block the release — Polaris release proceeds and writes `reservation.unpush.failed` (warning) so the orphan on the device is auditable. "Already absent" (operator deleted on the device) writes `reservation.unpush.succeeded` with `alreadyAbsent: true`. **Queued rows (`pushStatus="pending"`) skip both the unpush AND the lease-release blocks** — nothing has been written to the device yet, so there's nothing to clean up; the release just flips the Polaris row and writes `reservation.push.queued.released` (info) for the audit trail. **Discovered `dhcp_lease` rows additionally fire a best-effort lease release** against the originating FortiGate (`POST /api/v2/monitor/system/dhcp/release-lease` with `{ip}`, routed through the same FMG-or-standalone-FortiGate transport as reservation push), gated on the originating integration's `pushReservations` toggle (the **DHCP Push** tab — both halves of the Polaris → FortiGate DHCP write path live under that single toggle). When the toggle is off, freeing a lease only flips the Polaris row and the FortiGate is not contacted. When it's on, FortiOS only forgets the *current* lease — the same client can DHCP-acquire the IP back on its next request, so this is "expire now" not a block. Success writes `reservation.lease_release.succeeded` (info); device-side failure writes `reservation.lease_release.failed` (warning) without blocking the Polaris release.

#### Stale-reservation alerts (mixed scoping)
- `GET    /reservations/stale-settings`         *(auth)* — `{ staleAfterDays }`. 0 = disabled.
- `PUT    /reservations/stale-settings`         *(admin)* — `{ staleAfterDays }`. Default 60. The setting feeds both the `flagStaleReservations` job and the alert lister; lowering it is reflected within ~6 hours (the next job tick).
- `GET    /reservations/alerts?show=active|ignored` — Default `active` returns non-ignored stale rows **on non-deprecated subnets**; `ignored` returns every row the operator has set `staleIgnored=true` regardless of threshold or subnet status so admins can review and un-silence. Each entry: `{ id, ipAddress, hostname, macAddress, subnetId, subnetCidr, subnetName, createdAt, lastSeenLeased, lastSeenArp, staleNotifiedAt, daysSinceSeen, fortigateDevice, pushedToId, pushedToName, assetLastSeen, assetPresenceMatch }`. `assetPresenceMatch` (`"mac" | "ip" | null`) + `assetLastSeen` report the Asset that correlated to the reservation; `daysSinceSeen` counts from the freshest of the DHCP lease, the ARP confirmation (`lastSeenArp`), and that asset's lastSeen, so a statically-addressed device that's still on the network never appears here. Reservations whose subnet is `deprecated` (its owning FortiGate was decommissioned) are excluded from the active list/count entirely — the network is gone, so per-IP stale alerts would be noise.
- `GET    /reservations/alerts/count`           — Just `{ count }`. Always counts the **active** list — ignored rows don't drive the sidebar badge.
- `POST   /reservations/:id/snooze`             *(user-or-above)* — Sets `staleSnoozedUntil = now + staleAfterDays` so the row is suppressed from the active alert list. Cleared automatically when discovery sees the IP active again. Returns `{ reservationId, snoozedUntil, daysAdded }`. Writes `reservation.stale.snoozed` (info).
- `POST   /reservations/:id/stale-ignore`       *(networkadmin)* — Permanently ignore stale alerts on this row (`staleIgnored=true`). NOT cleared by discovery activity; operator's intent persists across online/offline cycles. Writes `reservation.stale.ignored` (info).
- `DELETE /reservations/:id/stale-ignore`       *(networkadmin)* — Un-ignore. Writes `reservation.stale.unignored` (info).

#### Queued push lifecycle (mixed scoping)
- `GET    /reservations/push-queue`             *(auth)* — Lists every reservation in `pushStatus IN ("pending", "failed_permanent") AND status="active"`, sorted by `pushQueuedAt` ascending (oldest first). Each row carries the full reservation plus `subnet: { id, cidr, name, vlan, fortigateDevice }` and `pushedTo: { id, name, type, enabled }` so the UI can render hostname / IP / MAC / target FortiGate / integration name without N+1 fetches. Drives the **Push queue** filter view in the Events page Alerts panel.
- `GET    /reservations/push-queue/count`       *(auth)* — `{ count }`. Contributes to the Events Alerts button badge and the single Events sidebar dot, alongside discovery conflicts (`/conflicts/count`) and stale-reservation alerts (`/reservations/alerts/count`). The dot is red when there are conflicts and yellow otherwise (red precedence); there is no separate IPAM dot.
- `POST   /reservations/:id/retry-push`         *(reservations write — own rows; fullwrite for any)* — Operator-triggered single-row retry. Allowed when `pushStatus IN ("pending", "failed_permanent")`. Bypasses the monitored-gate `monitorStatus="up"` readiness gate AND the unmonitored-gate exponential backoff window. `failed_permanent` rows are flipped back to `pending` first so the retry path treats them uniformly. Still respects eligibility re-check (subnet drift cancels the queue + keeps the Polaris row as plain manual) and discovery-supersede (collision → `failed_permanent`). Returns `{ outcome: "synced" | "transient" | "permanent" | "cancelled" | "superseded", reservation }`. Writes `reservation.push.queued.retry_manual` (info) on entry, plus the same per-outcome Events the periodic retry tick emits.

### Utilization — `ipBlocks read`
Blanket-gated at the mount: the reports enumerate the IP space, so they carry the same read gate as the blocks they describe. Bearer tokens (no role snapshot) and `ipBlocks=none` roles get 403.
- `GET    /utilization`
- `GET    /utilization/blocks/:id`
- `GET    /utilization/subnets/:id`

### Dashboard — `requireAuth` (per-section permission filtering)
- `GET    /dashboard/summary[?sections=blocks,recent,assetTypes,monitorAlerts][&recentSourceTypes=manual,dhcp_reservation,...]` — Backs the home Dashboard's built-in IP-space widgets. `?sections=` narrows the response to the named sections so each widget fetches only what it renders (widgets call it via the 15s-memoized `PolarisWidgets.getSummary({sections,...})`); absent = the full legacy shape `{ blockUtilization, recentReservations, assetTypeCounts, monitorAlerts, monitorAlertsOverflow }`. Unknown section names drop silently. Every section is served through a 10s server-side TTL cache (keys carry the recent-section params) so concurrent widgets/tabs share one computation; permission-denied sections return empty without entering the cache. `blockUtilization` is reused from `utilizationService.getGlobalUtilization()` (no extra DB hit). `recentReservations` is the 10 most-recent active reservations — default filter is `sourceType="manual"` so DHCP discoveries / leases / VIP echoes don't crowd out reservations a person actually typed in; the optional `recentSourceTypes` query param (comma-separated source-type names) lets a widget broaden the filter (e.g. include `dhcp_reservation` to surface Polaris-pushed reservations alongside manual rows). Unknown source-type values are dropped silently; if every value is unknown the filter becomes a no-op rather than 0 rows. Each row includes hostname, MAC, createdBy, and the resolved `{subnetId, subnetCidr, subnetName, vlan}` so the card renders without a second fetch. `assetTypeCounts` is a `prisma.asset.groupBy` over `assetType` excluding `status in (decommissioned, disabled)` — feeds the SVG pie chart. `monitorAlerts` is monitored assets currently in `warning` or `down`, ordered by `monitorStatusChangedAt desc nulls last` (newest transitions first), capped at 50 with `monitorAlertsOverflow` flagging when there's more. **Filter-don't-403 gating**: the dashboard is the redirect target for users bounced off gated pages, so the endpoint never 403s — instead each section is gated on the caller's read access (`ipBlocks≥read` → blockUtilization, `reservations≥read` → recentReservations, `assets≥read` → assetTypeCounts + monitorAlerts) and denied sections return empty arrays with the response shape unchanged. Bearer-token callers have no role snapshot → all sections empty. Covered by `tests/integration/permissionGates.test.ts`.
- `GET    /dashboard/noc-summary[?feeds=topCpu,downNodes,...]` — Feed endpoint backing the SolarWinds-style NOC widgets (status tiles, Down Assets, Down Interfaces, Highest Avg CPU/Memory, Slowest Response, Packet Loss, Highest Disk Usage, Highest Temperature, Stale Polls, Recent Reboots, Active Alerts, Sites with Issues, Status Map uses `/map/sites` instead). `?feeds=` (names from `nocDashboardService.NOC_FEED_NAMES`; `status` = the three tile keys, `downNodes` unwraps `.nodes`) narrows to the named subset so each widget fetches only its own feed and renders as soon as that query returns; unknown names drop silently; absent = the full payload. Every (feed, filter, cap) computation is served through a 10s server-side TTL cache (`NOC_FEED_CACHE_TTL_MS`) shared across widgets/tabs/kiosk walls. The full shape: `{ statusCounts:{total,up,down,warning,unknown,recovering,maintenance}, uptimePercent, activeAlertCount, downNodes[], downInterfaces[], downIpsecTunnels[], topCpu[], topMemory[], slowestResponse[], packetLoss[], diskUsage[], temperature[], stalePolls[], recentReboots[], activeAlerts[], sitesWithIssues[] }` (`diskUsage[]` rows carry a `detail` = mount path; `temperature[]` rows are per-sensor — latest reading per (asset, sensorName) from the temperature-class rows of `asset_hardware_sensor_samples`, always °C, with `detail` = sensor name). **Maintenance-window assets are excluded from every down/warning/stale feed** (`status="maintenance"` freezes `monitorStatus`, so the frozen value is not live state — the shared `NOT_IN_MAINTENANCE` where-spread in `nocDashboardService`, mirrored in the sites-with-issues raw SQL and the `/summary` monitorAlerts clause) and are instead counted into `statusCounts.maintenance` (still in `total`, never in up/down/warning/unknown or the uptime gauge) — the Status Summary widget's purple "Maint" tile. `?includeDependencyDown=1` (the Down Assets widget's gear toggle; "1"/"true"/"yes") drops the `dependencySuppressed: false` filter from the `downNodes` feed — absent (the default) keeps suppressed assets out so a dead gate reads as ONE outage rather than one per device behind it, and the flag participates in that feed's cache key (`usesDepDown`) so a toggled widget can never be served the excluded list. Every `downNodes[]` row carries `dependencySuppressed`, which the widget renders as a "Dep. Down" badge. `downNodesTotal` = the TRUE (uncapped) down-asset count from an indexed `asset.count` over the same where — the Down Assets widget stamps it as a red pill on its header, so the overall number is exact even when `downNodes[]` is clipped by the row cap. `downInterfaces[]` = interfaces that are admin-up but oper-down AND selected for monitoring — the CTE joins `assets` on `ifName = ANY(monitoredInterfaces)` so only pinned interfaces qualify, filtered before the LIMIT (`getDownInterfaces`, one windowed single-pass CTE over `asset_interface_samples` for latest-per-`(asset,ifName)` + last-up timestamp, then a monitored-scope hydrate findMany), each row `{assetId, hostname, ipAddress, assetType, ifName, ifLabel, gate, lastUpAt}` where `gate` = the FortiGate the interface lives on (firewall → own hostname; managed FortiSwitch/FortiAP → parent `learnedLocation`). `downIpsecTunnels[]` = fully-down IPsec tunnels that are ALSO selected for monitoring — same pin gate as interfaces, joining `assets` on `tunnelName = ANY(monitoredIpsecTunnels)` before the LIMIT, so an unpinned tunnel (e.g. one riding a dead parent link, whose CMDB-synthesized samples stay perpetually fresh) never shows as an outage (`getDownIpsecTunnels`, same CTE shape over `asset_ipsec_tunnel_samples` where `status='down'`), each row `{assetId, hostname, ipAddress, assetType, tunnelName, parentInterface, remoteGateway, gate, lastUpAt}` — `parentInterface` is the phase1-interface WAN port the tunnel rides. The frontend `downInterfaces` widget (labeled "Down Interfaces") merges both arrays into one gate-grouped list — gates ordered **youngest outage first** (newest `lastUpAt` among the gate's rows; the row-limit clip also keeps the freshest outages), rows **alphabetical by name within each gate**, and the merged pre-clip total stamped as a red pill on the widget header (`PolarisWidgets.setHeaderCount`) — rendering a down tunnel's parent physical interface inline; its config has per-kind toggles (`showInterfaces` / `showTunnels`). Sections computed by `nocDashboardService.getNocSummaryPayload` (feed registry + per-feed TTL cache), each scale-checked flat to 2000 assets (groupBy / count / one windowed DISTINCT-ON or aggregate / one bounded findMany — no per-row awaits). Same **filter-don't-403** contract as `/summary`: asset-sourced sections gate on `assets≥read`, Event-sourced sections (`activeAlerts`, `recentReboots`) on `events≥read`; denied sections return empty/zero with the shape unchanged (and never enter the cache). Accepts optional per-widget filters `?assetTypes=` (the enabled built-in types) + `?regionTags=` (region names — the caller's "My regions" or a widget's Selected-regions pick) + `?fortigates=` (FortiGate device names — the widgets' Selected-FortiGates per-site narrowing; matches assets behind any named gate via `learnedLocation` / `AssetFortigateSighting`, exact-insensitive — the same haystacks as the tag/maintenance "Behind FortiGate" criteria — with the `__none__` sentinel = the picker's "(No FortiGate)" entry for gate-less assets; combined with regions + asset types this builds one-site dashboards, e.g. a single gate's switches/APs) → `resolveFilteredAssetIds` (cached per filter) constrains every requested feed to the matching asset set. Frontend memoizes for ~15s **per (feeds, filter, limit)** via `PolarisWidgets.getNocSummary(opts, feeds)`. `topCpu`/`topMemory` rank by the per-asset **average of the most-recent N samples** (not the instantaneous last reading) — N comes from `?samples=` (the widgets' "Average over" gear control; default 10, clamped to a 100 ceiling, 1 = latest sample only; the frontend omits the param at the default so those widgets share one cached payload, and only the sample-averaged feeds key their server cache on it); `slowestResponse` averages a fixed most-recent 10. `packetLoss[]` excludes assets at 100% loss (zero successful probes in the window, enforced in the SQL HAVING) — a hard-down node is Down Assets material, not packet loss. Every list widget has a shared Row-limit control (`5/10/20/50/100/1000`; helpers in `public/js/widgets/index.js`); a widget picking the **1000** option sends `?limit=N` (clamped to a 1000 ceiling) which caps every *requested* feed at N — ≤100 omits the param, shares the default-cap payload, and clips client-side (the four `_topnBar` widgets default to a 20-row limit with the red-row guarantee; see the widgets file-map entry). The `summary` endpoint takes a parallel `?recentLimit=` (default 10, clamped 1000) for the recentReservations widget. The `getNocSummary`/`getSummary` fetches carry a 20s client abort-timeout so a large request degrades instead of hanging the widget.

### User Dashboard — `requireAuth`
Per-user dashboard layout. One row per user in `UserDashboard`; absent row = empty dashboard. No admin override (strictly per-caller); no Event audit log (UI preference, not security-relevant).
- `GET    /me/dashboard` — Returns the caller's layout, or `{ version: 2, columns: [] }` when no row exists yet (drives the "Customize Page → Add Widgets" empty-state). NOT re-validated — a stored legacy v1 row is returned untouched and migrated to v2 client-side.
- `PUT    /me/dashboard` — Zod-validates the full v2 layout, upserts, returns the saved shape. Layout shape: `{ version: 2, columns: Column[] }` where `Column = { id (uuid), width 3|4|6|12, widgets: WidgetInstance[] }` and `WidgetInstance = { id (uuid), type, height 1|2|3, config }`. Caps: ≤12 columns, ≤64 widgets total (superRefine). The client always migrates v1→v2 before saving, so PUT only accepts v2.

### Table tabs — scope-resolved function key (per-user)
The Assets page's view tabs. Same scope→key resolution as saved filters below, but both verbs need only **read**: a tab is the operator's own view of data they can already see, so a readonly user gets tabs. Strictly per-caller (no admin override), no Event audit — UI preference, the `/me/dashboard` pattern. Session callers only.
- `GET /me/table-tabs?scope=assets` — `{ version: 1, tabs: [{ id, name, state, savedFilterId, savedFilterName }], activeId }`, or the empty layout `{version:1,tabs:[],activeId:""}` when the caller has never saved tabs (the client then materializes one default tab from whatever the table is showing and doesn't write until something changes).
- `PUT /me/table-tabs?scope=assets` — full replace. ≤20 tabs, unique ids, names ≤40 chars; each tab's `state` goes through the same `sanitizeFilterState` a preset does. A stale `activeId` (tab closed in another window) falls back to the first tab instead of 400-ing the layout away.

### Saved table filters — scope-resolved function key
Named filter+sort presets for a list page (Assets → Filters ▾). There is no dedicated function key: the request's `scope` resolves to the key that already gates that page (`assets` → `assets`), checked inline with `ensureRoleSnapshot` + `hasPermission` because the key isn't known until the body/query is read. Session callers only — a preset has an owner, and bearer tokens have no user identity (401).
- `GET    /saved-filters?scope=assets`   *(scope key: read)* — `{ filters: [{ id, scope, name, visibility, ownerId, ownerName, isOwner, state, createdAt, updatedAt }] }` — everything the caller owns plus every other user's `public` preset, name-ascending. Orphaned private rows (owner deleted) match nobody and are invisible.
- `POST   /saved-filters`                *(scope key: read; `write` when `visibility:"public"`)* — Body `{ scope, name, visibility, state }`. Publishing to everyone is a write to shared state; keeping a private preset only needs the read the page already required. A same-(scope, owner, name) POST **updates** the existing row instead of duplicating, so the client's "save over this name" flow is one call. 201 with the saved DTO.
- `PUT    /saved-filters/:id`            *(owner only, same level rules)* — Rename / re-scope visibility / replace state. `scope` cannot be changed.
- `DELETE /saved-filters/:id`            *(owner: read; someone else's: `fullwrite`)* — 204. The fullwrite branch is housekeeping (a departed colleague's shared preset).
`state` is validated by `sanitizeFilterState` on every write — see the service entry; anything table-sf.js can't itself produce is a 400 rather than stored.

### Users — `users` function key
- `GET    /users`                               *(read)* — Every row is returned with the joined `role: { id, name, color, isProtected, isBuiltIn }` and `regionTags: string[]` (per-user scope).
- `POST   /users`                               *(write)* — Body: `{ username, password, roleId, regionTags?, otherTags? }`. The legacy `role: <enum>` field is no longer accepted.
