- `GET    /users/:id`                           *(read)*
- `DELETE /users/:id`                           *(write)* — Refused with 409 when this would leave Polaris with zero users holding `users=fullwrite` AND `roles=fullwrite` (last-admin-equivalent invariant).
- `PUT    /users/:id/password`                  *(write)* — Local accounts only.
- `PUT    /users/:id/role`                      *(write)* — Body: `{ roleId }`. Refused with 400 when reassigning yourself; 409 when this would break the last-admin-equivalent invariant. Auto-clears `needsRoleReview` since picking a role is an implicit review.
- `PUT    /users/:id/regions`                   *(write)* — Body: `{ regionTags?: string[], otherTags?: string[] }` (each optional; omitted dimension left unchanged, empty array clears). Validation via `tagNormalize`: trim, drop empties, dedupe case-insensitively, ≤64 entries, each ≤64 chars. Writes one `user.regions_updated` Event with the per-dimension from/to diff. These are operator-set tags only — group-derived tags are computed at `/auth/me`, never written here.
- `DELETE /users/:id/totp`                      *(write)* — Admin-initiated TOTP reset (for "lost device" recovery). Clears the secret and backup codes so the user can re-enroll on next login.
- `GET    /users/role-review-notifications`     *(read)* — Sidebar feed. Returns `{ users, count }` where `users` is every row with `needsRoleReview=true`, ordered by `lastLogin` asc, projected to `{ id, username, role: { id, name, ... }, regionTags, displayName, authProvider, email, lastLogin, createdAt, ... }`. Polled every 30s by [public/js/app.js](public/js/app.js) for admins only.
- `DELETE /users/:id/role-review`               *(write)* — Dismiss the new-user notification for one user (global — hides the row for every admin).

### Roles — `roles` function key
- `GET    /roles`                               *(read)* — Every Role with `{ id, name, description, permissions, regionTags, color, isBuiltIn, isProtected, userCount, createdAt, updatedAt }`. The frontend filters `isProtected=true` rows (admin + readonly) out of the editable list.
- `GET    /roles/:id`                           *(read)*
- `GET    /roles/functions`                     *(read)* — `{ accessLevels: ["none","read","write","fullwrite"], functions: FunctionKeyDef[] }` — the 25-key catalogue with `{ key, label, description, hasOwnershipDimension? }`. Single source of truth backing the permissions slide-over matrix.
- `POST   /roles`                               *(write)* — `{ name, description?, permissions, regionTags?, color? }`. Name validated against `/^[A-Za-z0-9_-]{2,32}$/` + case-insensitive uniqueness against existing names + the reserved `admin` / `readonly`. `color` validated as `#rrggbb` (empty/null clears). Permissions normalized: unknown function keys dropped, missing keys defaulted to `"none"`.
- `PUT    /roles/:id`                           *(write)* — Body accepts any subset of `{ name?, description?, permissions?, regionTags?, color? }`. Refused with 403 when the role is `isProtected=true` (admin / readonly). Bumps the role-version cache + writes one `role.updated` Event with per-field diff (including a per-functionKey `permissionChanges` map listing only the keys whose level changed).
- `DELETE /roles/:id`                           *(write)* — Refused with 409 when `isBuiltIn=true` OR when any user holds the role (admin must reassign first).

### Group Mappings — mounted at `/group-mappings`, gated `users:fullwrite`
- `GET    /group-mappings`                      — All mappings (optional `?provider=oidc|ldap|saml`). Each: `{ id, provider, groupKey, groupLabel, roleId, roleName, regionTags, otherTags, enabled, description, createdAt, updatedAt }`.
- `GET    /group-mappings/:id`
- `POST   /group-mappings`                      — `{ provider, groupKey, roleId?, regionTags?, otherTags?, enabled?, description? }`. `groupKey` normalized per provider (LDAP lowercased-DN, OIDC/SAML exact); 409 on duplicate `(provider, groupKey)`. Warning Event when `roleId` is admin-equivalent.
- `PUT    /group-mappings/:id`                  — Subset of the above (provider is immutable).
- `DELETE /group-mappings/:id`

### Integrations — `integrations` function key
> Mount requires `integrations=read`; all write endpoints inside the file are upgraded to `integrations=write` via an inline `router.use(...)`.
- `GET    /integrations`                       — List integrations (paginated). Each row carries `discoveryBaseline: { avgMs, sampleCount } | null` from `discoveryDurationService.getBaselines()` so the card UI can render an "Avg Discovery Time" line operators can size `pollInterval` against. `null` until the rolling window has ≥3 successful runs.
- `POST   /integrations`
- `GET    /integrations/:id`
- `PUT    /integrations/:id`
- `DELETE /integrations/:id`
- `POST   /integrations/:id/test`                — Test connection (also `POST /integrations/test` for unsaved config; `POST /integrations/:id/test/fortigate-sample` + `POST /integrations/test/fortigate-sample` for sample-pull dry runs)
- `POST   /integrations/:id/discover`           — Trigger full discovery run
- `GET    /integrations/discoveries`            — List in-flight discoveries. Each entry: `{ id, name, type, startedAt, elapsedMs, activeDevices: string[], slow: boolean, slowDevices: string[], totalDevices: number | null, completedCount: number, skippedOfflineCount: number, skippedErrorCount: number }`. `slow` flips true when the overall run exceeds its rolling-duration baseline; `slowDevices` lists FortiGates (FMG-only) whose per-device elapsed exceeds that device's baseline. The four progress counters power the sidebar's "N/M complete · K skipped (offline)" line for FMG runs: `totalDevices` is parsed from the `discover.devices` info-level message ("Found N managed device(s) …") and stays null until the roster is fetched; `completedCount` bumps on `discover.device.complete`; `skippedOfflineCount` on info-level `discover.device.skip` (conn_status mismatch — gate down or unmanaged); `skippedErrorCount` on error-level skips and per-device errors. Standalone FortiGate runs leave the counters at their initial values since there's one device. This endpoint also calls the slow-run checker inline, so the UI sees amber within one 4 s poll cycle. See `discoveryDurationService` + the `discoverySlowCheck` job. For FMG-type discoveries, `activeDevices` additionally has the integration name prepended whenever the per-integration FMG worker has any inflight calls (proxy or native), so the sidebar shows the FMG itself as busy during roster fetch + mgmt-IP resolves + native CMDB scrapes — not just during per-device work. In the sidebar popup each `activeDevices` name is clickable (`openDiscoveryDevice` in [public/js/app.js](public/js/app.js)): it resolves the FortiGate name to its firewall Asset by hostname and opens the asset slide-over (in place on `/assets.html`, else via the `#view=asset:` hash); a no-match — the transient FMG self-entry, or a not-yet-inventoried FortiGate — surfaces a toast.
- `GET    /integrations/health-summary`          — Sidebar polling target. Returns `{ failed: [{ id, name, type, lastTestAt }] }` listing enabled integrations whose latest connection test failed (`enabled=true AND lastTestOk=false`). Gated by `integrations=read`. Polled every 30 s by [public/js/app.js](public/js/app.js); rendered as a red sidebar notice (`#integration-failed-status`) that links to `/integrations.html` on click. Pairs with the [integrationConnectionTester](src/jobs/integrationConnectionTester.ts) background job which is the writer that keeps `lastTestOk` fresh.
- `DELETE /integrations/:id/discover`            — Abort an in-flight discovery. *(admin-equivalent: upgraded to `integrations=fullwrite` via an inline `requirePermission` guard — `networkadmin` with `write` can run discoveries but cannot abort them. The frontend hides the abort ✕ for callers below `fullwrite`.)*
- `POST   /integrations/:id/query`              — Manual API proxy. FortiManager: `{method, params}` (JSON-RPC) or `{mode:"fortigate", deviceName, method, path, query?, body?}` (REST direct to a managed FortiGate — FMG resolves the mgmt IP, the integration's direct-mode FortiGate API token authenticates). FortiGate: `{method, path, query?, body?}` (REST). Both REST forms take `method ∈ GET|POST|PUT|DELETE`; `body` is a JSON payload attached for POST/PUT only, and any non-GET writes a warning-level `integration.query.write` Event (ad-hoc device writes are audited, body included). **Both REST forms also accept an optional per-request credential override `{apiToken?, apiUser?}`** (`overrideFortigateCreds`): it swaps `apiToken`/`apiUser` for a standalone FortiGate, or `fortigateApiToken`/`fortigateApiUser` for an FMG in bypass mode — never the FMG's own `apiToken`, which is still needed to resolve the gate's management IP. Exists because bypass mode stores ONE FortiGate token for the whole fleet, so testing a different per-gate token otherwise means editing the integration and repointing discovery/polling/DHCP-push at an unproven credential. The override is used for that one request and persisted nowhere: not on the integration, not in the Event (which records only `usedTokenOverride: true`), and not in the browser's saved-query localStorage entry. A masked-placeholder value (`••••••••`) is rejected rather than sent as a token. It widens no privilege — the route already requires `integrations:write`, which can rewrite the stored token outright. Entra ID: `{path, query?}` GET-only against `graph.microsoft.com`; path must begin with `/v1.0/` or `/beta/`. Active Directory: `{filter?, baseDn?, scope?, attributes?, sizeLimit?}` LDAP search; baseDn defaults to the integration's configured base DN.
- `GET    /integrations/:id/interface-aggregate?class=fortigate|fortiswitch|fortiap|workstation|server` — Auto-Monitor Interfaces "By name" data source. **Served from `Integration.interfaceAggregateCache`** (`getCachedInterfaceAggregate`), the precomputed checklist refreshed at the end of every successful discovery run — so the modal loads instantly instead of running a fleet-wide DISTINCT ON over `asset_interface_samples` on every open. Returns `{ rows: [{ ifName, ifType, deviceCount }], computedAt }` (the heavy per-row `devices[]` list is dropped from the cache — the UI only renders the three fields + a device count), sorted by deviceCount desc. **Live-compute fallback**: when the cache has no entry for this class yet (the window before the integration's first post-feature discovery) the route falls back to `getInterfaceAggregate` and returns `computedAt: null`. The expensive aggregate (latest `AssetInterfaceSample` per `(assetId, ifName)` for assets where `discoveredByIntegrationId = :id` AND `assetType` matches the class, plus synthetic IPsec-tunnel rows for the fortigate class) now runs in the discovery process at end-of-run, not on the interactive web path. There is no operator "Refresh from latest discovery" button anymore — the list re-populates each discovery cycle and the modal shows an "As of last discovery: …" timestamp.
- `POST   /integrations/:id/interface-aggregate/preview` — Live preview for the modal. Body: `{ class, selection: AutoMonitorInterfacesSchema | null, baselineSelection?: AutoMonitorInterfacesSchema | null }`. Returns `{ deviceCount, interfaceCount, perDeviceMax, sampleDevices: [{hostname, pinNames: string[]}], diff? }`. Read-only: does not persist or write `monitoredInterfaces`. `interfaceCount` is the sum of pin lengths produced by `selection` alone (not unioned with operator-pinned interfaces). **`baselineSelection` is optional**: when supplied, the service computes pin sets for BOTH selections from a single DB fetch and returns a `diff: { addedCount, removedCount, addedSample: [{hostname, ifName}], removedSample: [{hostname, ifName}] }` block enumerating per-`(assetId, ifName)` adds/removes. Drives the "+X added · −Y removed" inline delta hint on the auto-monitor card; frontend tracks the previously-sent selection per-card and passes it as the baseline so each checkbox toggle's preview shows what THAT toggle just changed (not the delta from saved). First preview-after-modal-open uses the saved selection as baseline so it shows no diff; subsequent toggles each show their own per-click change. Older UI builds that don't send `baselineSelection` get the same response shape as before — no `diff` field. **As of the cache work, the frontend only calls this endpoint for `byLldp` selections** (topology isn't in the cache); `byNames` / `byPatterns` / `byTypes` previews are computed instantly client-side from the already-loaded `interfaceAggregateCache` rows (`computeClientPreview` in `public/js/integrations.js`) — exact for `byNames`, an upper bound for `byPatterns`/`byTypes` with `onlyUp` (the cache has no per-device `operStatus`), labeled as such. This endpoint stays the authority for the LLDP case and for the **Test against fleet** button.
- `POST   /integrations/:id/interface-aggregate/apply` — Apply-on-save trigger. Body: `{ class }`. Reads the current `selection` from `Integration.config.<klass>Monitor.autoMonitorInterfaces` (whatever was most recently saved) and runs the same apply pass that fires at the end of every discovery: union into each matching asset's `monitoredInterfaces` (additive only). **Fire-and-forget: returns `202 { queued: true }` immediately** and runs `applyAutoMonitorForClass` in the background — the resolve scans every asset's latest interface samples (a multi-second-to-minutes query at fleet scale) and awaiting it wedged the modal's "Applying…" state for minutes. Safe because the apply is strictly additive + idempotent AND re-runs on every discovery (Phase 2c), so a fire-and-forget lost to a process restart self-heals. Writes one `integration.auto_monitor_interfaces.applied` Event on completion when something changed, or `integration.auto_monitor_interfaces.error` (warning) on failure. Called by the integration edit modal's **Save Changes** button for each per-class block whose selection is non-null; the modal confirms "applying in the background" rather than reporting pin counts.
- `POST   /integrations/:id/auto-monitor-assets/preflight` — Save-Changes confirm-modal data source. Body: `{ proposed: { firewall?, switch?, access_point?, workstation?, server? } }` carrying the operator's in-flight `addAsMonitored` choices. Returns `{ integrationId, integrationName, classes: { <classKey>: { currentAddAsMonitored, proposedAddAsMonitored, total, overridden, wouldEnable, wouldDisable } } }` — `wouldDisable` counts assets that would have monitoring swept OFF if this save lands (non-override only), `wouldEnable` counts the inverse, `overridden` counts assets with `monitorOverride=true` that are protected from either direction. Each class entry is included only when `proposed[class]` was supplied. The frontend (`public/js/integrations.js`) calls this from the Save Changes click handler and renders a confirm modal when `wouldDisable > 0` on any class so the operator sees the blast radius before committing.

### Asset Types — `assets` function key
Operator-extensible asset-type registry. The eight historical built-ins (server / switch / router / firewall / workstation / printer / access_point / other) are seeded as `isBuiltIn=true, isProtected=true` rows by the registry-cutover migration and cannot be renamed or deleted. Custom rows are admin/assetsadmin-managed from the Assets page → **Manage asset types** slide-over (Phase 2; the route + service ship in Phase 1). Behavioral special-cases (FortiGate / switch / access_point branches in dependency tree, fortinetTopology, polling source defaults, topology rendering, inferAssetTypeFromOs) only fire for the eight built-ins — custom types fall through to "other"-like generic behavior. Mounted at `/api/v1/asset-types` BEFORE `/assets` so Express's first-match routing picks the registry endpoints instead of treating "types" as an asset id.
- `GET    /asset-types[?withUsage=1]`           *(read)* — `{ types: [{ id, name, label, description, isBuiltIn, isProtected, createdBy, createdAt, updatedAt, usageCount? }] }`. `usageCount` only included when `?withUsage=1` (one extra `prisma.asset.groupBy` to count assets per type — used by the Manage modal to show "N assets" badges and refuse delete when in-use).
- `GET    /asset-types/:id`                     *(read)* — Single row with `usageCount`.
- `POST   /asset-types`                         *(write)* — Body: `{ name, label, description? }`. `name` is lowercased + validated against `/^[a-z0-9_-]{2,32}$/` and rejected if it collides with a built-in. Writes one `asset_type.created` Event. Cache refresh fires immediately so the registry is hot for the next `/assets` write.
- `PUT    /asset-types/:id`                     *(write)* — Body accepts any subset of `{ name, label, description }`. **Refuses with 403 on built-in rows** (`isProtected=true`). Rename is transactional: every `Asset` row holding the old name is rewritten to the new name atomically with the registry row update via a `$transaction([asset.updateMany(...), assetTypeDef.update(...)])`. Writes one `asset_type.updated` Event.
- `DELETE /asset-types/:id`                     *(write)* — **Refuses with 403 on built-ins**, and **with 409 when any Asset still references the type** (operator must reassign or delete those assets first). Writes one `asset_type.deleted` Event.

### Assets — `requireAuth`
- `GET    /assets`                              — List, **server-side filter / sort / pagination** (the assets page runs `TableSF` in server-side mode like Events; see TEMPLATES.md → "Sortable + filterable data table"). Returns `{ assets, total, limit, offset }`. Filters: `status` / `assetType` (CSV multi-select, single value back-compat), `monitor` (the `_monitor` synthetic chip → `monitored` + `monitorStatus`), per-column operator-aware text filters (`<col>` + `<col>Op` of `contains|not_contains|empty|is_not_empty`), `server` (spans `location`+`learnedLocation`), `lastSeenFrom`/`lastSeenTo`, plus the legacy `department` / `search` / `createdBy`. `sortBy`/`sortDir` are whitelisted (400 otherwise); default `createdAt desc`. `favoriteIds` (CSV) floats the operator's starred assets to the top of the whole result set via a two-bucket query. Indexed by `assets(createdAt)` + `assets(lastSeen)`.
- `POST   /assets`
- `GET    /assets/:id`
- `PUT    /assets/:id`
- `DELETE /assets/:id`
- `DELETE /assets`                              — Bulk delete
- `POST   /assets/import`                       — CSV import: backdate `createdAt`/`firstSeen` from serial+date rows (assets admin; `dryRun` for preview). PDF/CSV *export* is client-side (bundled jspdf + client CSV), not a route.
- `POST   /assets/import-pdf`                    — PDF import (assets admin)
- `POST   /assets/oui-lookup` / `POST /assets/:id/oui-lookup`  — OUI vendor lookup (by MAC in body; the `:id` form also stamps the asset)
- `POST   /assets/:id/dns-lookup`               — Reverse PTR lookup (IP → hostname); per-asset, user-triggered
- `POST   /assets/:id/forward-lookup`           — Forward A/AAAA lookup (hostname/dnsName → IP); fills ipAddress when missing
- `DELETE /assets/:id/macs/:mac`                — Remove one MAC from an asset's history (requires `assets` write)
- `GET    /assets/:id/ip-history`               — List IP history entries for an asset (filtered by retention days). Auto-populated by the Prisma query extension in `src/db.ts` whenever any `asset.create` / `asset.update` writes an `ipAddress`, so discovery-sourced IPs are captured without changes to integration services.
- `GET    /assets/ip-history-settings`          — `{ retentionDays }`; 0 = keep forever (default).
- `PUT    /assets/ip-history-settings`          *(assets admin)* — `{ retentionDays }`; saving immediately prunes any history rows with `lastSeen` older than the new cutoff.
- `GET    /assets/source-priority`              — the operator's Sources-column priority `{ order[], integrationPrefix, contributors[{kind,label,mode,describe,fortinetDevice}] }`. `contributors` arrives IN the operator's order (catalogue entries from `utils/assetSourceLocation.ts`) so the drag-and-drop list renders labels + "what this contributes" hints without hardcoding them client-side. Declared before `/:id`.
- `PUT    /assets/source-priority`              *(assets:write)* — `{ order?[], integrationPrefix? }`. Unknown or duplicated source kinds are 400s (the read path self-heals stored rows; a client posting a typo should hear about it); omitted kinds are appended in default order. Returns the same shape as the GET. Audited `asset.source_priority.updated` with the previous order. Takes effect per integration on its next discovery run — that's when `Asset.learnedLocation` is rewritten.
- `GET    /assets/:id/effective-monitor-settings` — Resolved settings for one asset PLUS per-field tier provenance (`asset` / `class` / `integration` / `manual` / `default` — the last meaning no tier set a compatible polling method and the materialized runtime source default is what `resolved` carries), `tier3Source` (`"integration"` or `"manual"`), `classOverrideId` when a class override applies, and `mibLookup: { [uuid]: {moduleName} }` mapping every non-null MIB UUID across the four streams to its `MibFile.moduleName` so the asset-details monitoring chips can render a `MIB: <module>` segment alongside the polling method / cadence / tier label without a second round-trip. Standard MIB ids (the `std:` namespace) are skipped — those resolve through the frontend-local `_SNMP_STANDARD_MIBS` table. Drives the asset edit modal Monitoring tab tier badges AND the asset details monitoring chip stack. See **Monitor Settings Hierarchy** below for the resolution order.
- `POST   /assets/bulk-monitor`                 *(assets admin)* — `{ ids, monitored, monitorCredentialId?, monitorIntervalSec?, probeTimeoutMs? }`. Flips `monitored` on every selected row + applies the supplied credential / cadence overrides uniformly. After the bulk write lands, runs `recomputeMonitorOverrideForAssets(prisma, ids)` (single SQL UPDATE) so each touched asset's `monitorOverride` reflects whether the new `monitored` value diverges from its discovering integration's per-class `addAsMonitored`. Manual / non-integration assets keep `monitorOverride=false`. The polling method comes from the resolver — per-asset choices live on PUT /assets/:id, not here. Returns `{ updated, errors: [{id, error}] }`.
- `POST   /assets/:id/monitor-override/reset`   *(assets write)* — Clears the explicit `monitorOverride` pin and realigns the asset to its discovering integration's per-class Auto-Monitor default: resolves the flag via `getAddAsMonitoredFromConfig`, sets `monitored = <flag>` and `monitorOverride = false`, so discovery resumes auto-managing the asset. 400 when the asset has no `discoveredByIntegrationId` or its assetType isn't subject to Auto-Monitor. Writes one `monitor.override_reset` Event. Backs the "Reset to integration default" button beside the **Asset Override** badge on the asset-details System tab.
- `GET    /assets/:id/monitor-history?range=1h|24h|7d|30d` *or* `?from=ISO&to=ISO`  — Sample stream for the chart. With `range`, the window ends at *now*; with `from`/`to`, both bounds come from the query (span capped at 1 year). Returns `{ range, since, until, tier, bucketSeconds, lastSuccessAt, samples, stats: { total, failed, successRate, packetLossRate, avgMs, minMs, maxMs } }`; `range` is `"custom"` when `from`/`to` was used. `responseTimeMs` is null on failed samples (the "packet loss" signal). `lastSuccessAt` is the newest **successful detail** sample at/after `since` (`readLastMonitorSuccessAt`), populated only on rollup tiers and null on detail (where the series answers it) or when no detail success exists in the window: on a rollup tier every sample timestamp is a `bucketStart`, so the chart's stale banner would read a healthy 1-minute probe as ~a day stale the moment the operator switched to 30d.
- `POST   /assets/:id/snmp-walk`                *(admin)* — Operator-driven SNMP walk for the asset details **SNMP Walk** tab. Body: `{ credentialId, oid?, maxRows? }`. `credentialId` is any stored SNMP credential (not necessarily the asset's monitor credential — admins can spot-check a host with a different community). `oid` defaults to `1.3.6.1.2.1.1` (system subtree); validated as a numeric dotted OID. `maxRows` defaults to 500, hard-capped at 5,000. Returns `{ rows: [{oid, type, value}], truncated, durationMs, oid, host }` — `type` is the symbolic ASN.1 type name (Counter32, OctetString, OID, IpAddress, ...) and `value` is a printable representation (UTF-8 OctetString when printable, hex otherwise; IpAddress is dotted-quad). Walks the asset's `ipAddress` directly — does not consult the asset's resolved polling method, so it works on any asset including unmonitored ones. Each call writes one `asset.snmp_walk` Event (`info` on success, `warning` on failure). 400 if the asset has no IP or the credential is not type `snmp`; 502 if the SNMP session itself fails.
- `POST   /assets/:id/probe-now`                *(user-or-above)* — Run an immediate response-time probe AND telemetry (CPU/memory), temperature, and system-info pulls in parallel; returns `{ success, responseTimeMs, error?, telemetry: { supported, collected, error? }, temperature: { supported, collected, error? }, systemInfo: { supported, collected, error? } }`. Per-stream statuses let the System tab's **Poll Now** button toast tell the operator which streams polled and which failed (`collected: false` with an `error` is the common case when, e.g., FortiManager-discovered assets in proxy mode have no direct `fortigateApiToken` configured — the SNMP-override probe succeeds but the FortiOS REST system-info call throws "FortiManager direct-mode API token not configured"). The `temperature` stream dispatches on `temperaturePolling` independently from `telemetry`'s `cpuMemoryPolling`, so the toast can show "CPU/memory ok · temperature failed via REST" when only the sensor-info endpoint is unreliable on a branch-class FortiGate. An empty sensor list is rendered as `temperature: n/a (no sensors)` rather than a failure. The endpoint first runs the originating integration's filter via `assetMatchesIntegrationFilter` in `src/utils/integrationFilter.ts` — FMG/FortiGate/Entra check `deviceInclude`/`deviceExclude` against the asset's hostname; AD checks `ouInclude`/`ouExclude` against the OU path. If the asset is out of scope the call returns `409` with the reason in `error` and on every stream's `error`, no probe traffic leaves the host, and one `asset.refresh` Event is written at level `warning` with message `Poll blocked: <name> — <reason>`. The FMG/FortiGate `interfaceInclude` / `interfaceExclude` is applied a layer down inside `collectSystemInfoFortinet` so the System tab interface table mirrors discovery's scope — VLAN sub-interfaces are kept when their parent survives the filter (hiding the parent would orphan its children, so the filter walks the parent → child relationship before dropping rows). Otherwise each call writes one `asset.refresh` Event (level `info` on full success, `warning` on any partial failure) so manual polls are auditable — the periodic monitorAssets job only writes events on up/down transitions.
- `POST   /assets/:id/rediscover`               *(assets write)* — Re-run discovery for ONE FortiGate. Only valid on a firewall asset carrying a `fortinetTopology.role === "fortigate"` stamp discovered by an enabled FortiManager or standalone-FortiGate integration (400 otherwise). Resolves the FMG device name from `fortinetTopology.deviceName` (hostname fallback — same resolver precedent as descriptionSyncService's device-targeted writes), re-checks `assetMatchesIntegrationFilter` against both the hostname and the resolved device name (409 + warning `asset.rediscover` Event when the gate is filtered out — mirrors probe-now), and 409s while any discovery is already running for the integration (`isRunActive` pre-check + `triggerDiscovery`'s coalescing boolean return closing the TOCTOU window; the pg-boss `singletonKey` is the last-line guard). FMG assets queue a **scoped** run — `triggerDiscovery(integrationId, actor, { scopeDeviceName })` rides the full run machinery (DiscoveryRun row with `scopeDeviceName` stamped, progress, abort, pg-boss handoff) but narrows the roster to the one device inside `discoverDhcpSubnets` (AFTER the raw roster is captured into `knownDeviceNames`, same protection as the device filter) and finalizes in `"finalize-scoped"` mode (Phase 2b per-controller switch/AP decommission ONLY — see the SyncMode notes in the FMG Discovery Workflow section); standalone-FortiGate assets get a plain full run (the integration IS the single gate). Scoped runs do NOT stamp `Integration.lastDiscoveryAt` (the scheduler's next full run is unaffected) and skip the integration-level slow-run duration sample. 202 `{ message, integrationId, integrationName, deviceName }` + one `asset.rediscover` Event. Backs the **Re-discover** button on the asset-details System tab (rendered next to the Status pill for FortiGate firewall assets; watches the shared `/discoveries` poll for appear→disappear to refresh the asset, with a graceful fallback toast for roles that can't read `/discoveries`).
- `GET    /assets/:id/system-info`              — Asset details System tab: latest interface + storage + telemetry snapshot. Returns `{ monitored, lastTelemetryAt, lastSystemInfoAt, telemetry: {...}|null, interfaces: [...], storage: [...], temperatures: [...], ipsecTunnels: [...], lldpNeighbors: [...] }`. Both the `interfaces` and `ipsecTunnels` queries anchor to `lastSystemInfoAt` (the full pass's write timestamp) rather than the raw newest sample — the fast cadence only writes PINNED rows, so ordering by raw timestamp would hide every unpinned interface/tunnel within a minute of a fast walk. Each anchor clamps down to the newest sample when it's ahead (transient collect failure / agent split-push), and the ipsec query additionally falls back to the newest batch when the anchor pass produced zero ipsec rows. `lldpNeighbors` is the full set of `AssetLldpNeighbor` rows for the asset (current state, not a time-series); each entry includes `localIfName`, full LLDP TLVs (chassisId/portId + subtypes, port description, system name/description, management IP, capabilities), `firstSeen` / `lastSeen`, the source transport (`"fortios"` | `"snmp"`), and a `matchedAsset: { id, hostname, ipAddress, assetType } | null` cross-link when the neighbor resolved to a Polaris asset by management IP, chassis MAC, or hostname. Empty arrays when no scrape has run yet. The set additionally carries **peer-inferred** rows (`source = "peer-inferred"`) synthesized from `Asset.fortinetTopology` via `peerInferredLldpService` so a FortiSwitch's ports facing managed APs, and a FortiGate's FortiLink interfaces facing managed switches, show up in the Neighbor column even though those edges don't appear in a direct LLDP scrape (FortiSwitches in managed mode consume LLDP without re-publishing via SNMP LLDP-MIB). Inferred rows are deduped against real rows on `(localIfName, matchedAssetId)` — real LLDP wins on collision, including the aggregate/member case (a row learned on a FortiLink member port suppresses the inferred row on the `fortilink` aggregate). The frontend renders inferred entries in italic with a tooltip explaining the inference.
- `GET    /assets/:id/custom-widgets`            — Custom MIB tab payload (Slice 7). Resolves the asset's manufacturer through the `ManufacturerProfile` cache, applies optional per-widget `modelPattern` gating against `Asset.model`, and returns each applicable widget's definition plus a window of recent `AssetCustomWidgetSample` rows (up to 60 per widget, oldest first — line charts read the window directly; gauges + tables use `latest`). Response: `{ manufacturer, profileId, polling, lastCustomWidgetAt, widgets: [{ id, name, symbol, mibId, type, widgetType, transform, displayOptions, order, modelPattern, samples, latest, stateMap, labelSymbol, stateRows? }] }`. **State probes** (`widgetType="state"`) carry no `samples`/`latest` — their 0/1 readings live in `AssetStateSample`, so the handler additionally fetches the recent rows for every applicable state probe and attaches each probe's CURRENT state as `stateRows: [{rowKey, rowLabel, value, rawValue, timestamp}]` (newest-first scan keeping the first sighting of each `(probeId, rowKey)`; one scrape writes a probe's whole row set at one timestamp, so the take cap covers several full snapshots). Rows are sorted problem-first (per the probe's `stateMap.trueIsProblem`) then by name, since an operator opening the tab is looking for what's wrong and shouldn't have to scan a 60-row sensor table. Empty `widgets` array when the manufacturer has no widgets defined (the frontend hides the tab in that case) or the widget set doesn't match the asset's model. Samples are produced by `collectAndRecordCustomWidgets()` which rides the telemetry cadence (Slice 7b): after every successful `runTelemetryFor` pass, the helper walks each applicable widget over the asset's resolved SNMP transport, applies the widget's transform, and persists scalar or table rows into `AssetCustomWidgetSample` while bumping `Asset.lastCustomWidgetAt`. A `widgetType="state"` widget takes the state-probe branch instead: walk the value symbol, walk `labelSymbol` too when set (a failed label walk degrades to bare indexes rather than costing the alarm state), map every reading through `joinStateRows`/`evaluateStateMap`, drop the unreadable ones, and write `AssetStateSample` rows (a scalar probe keeps only the first readable row with `rowKey=""` and the probe's name as its label). Table probes are capped at `MAX_STATE_ROWS_PER_PROBE` (500) rows per scrape with a warn-level log when truncated — each row costs a per-scrape DB row AND a NotificationRuleState row in the engine, and a probe silently dropping rows would look like a healthy one. Both sample writes plus the `lastCustomWidgetAt` bump ride one `$transaction`. SNMP-only in v1; FortiOS REST custom widgets land in a follow-up.
- `GET    /assets/:id/telemetry-history?range=1h|24h|7d|30d` *or* `?from&to`  — CPU/memory time-series. Returns `{ range, since, until, samples, stats: { total, avgCpuPct, maxCpuPct, avgMemPct, maxMemPct } }`. memPct is computed from `memUsedBytes / memTotalBytes` if the source supplied bytes only.
- `GET    /assets/:id/interface-history?ifName=...&range=...`  — Per-interface counter samples; sized by interface (a 30-port switch with one row per 10 min ≈ 4,300 samples per 30-day range). Includes `inErrors` / `outErrors` (cumulative IF-MIB / FortiOS error counters) so the asset-detail interface slide-over can derive a per-interval error rate. The response also surfaces the latest sample's `alias` / `description` at the top level (FortiOS CMDB `alias` + `description`, SNMP `ifAlias`) so the slide-over header can show `<alias> (<ifName>)` and render the comment in the **Interface Comments** editor. `description` is the *resolved* value (override if set, else discovered); `discoveredDescription` and `overrideDescription` are also returned separately so the editor can label the source and show the device-reported value as ghost text when no override is set. The response also carries `lldpNeighbors`: the LLDP rows whose `localIfName === ifName` (usually 0 or 1, sometimes >1 on shared media); each row includes the same fields as the system-info endpoint plus a `matchedAsset` cross-link, so the slide-over can render an LLDP neighbor card with a clickable system name that opens the matched asset's view modal. Peer-inferred rows are merged in here too (same dedup rule as `/system-info` — see that endpoint for details), filtered to the requested ifName.
- `PUT    /assets/:id/interfaces/:ifName/comment` *(assets admin)* — Set or clear the Interface Comments override. Body: `{ description: string | null }` (max 255 chars; null or empty string deletes the override row so the discovered FortiOS CMDB description shows through again — the device-side description is never deleted). Polaris-local by default; when the asset's originating integration has `syncDescriptions` on (business rule 14), a saved comment is also pushed to the device via `descriptionSyncService.syncDescriptionsOnSave` and the response gains `sync: { attempted, status?, error? }` (best-effort — the override row persists even when the push fails; the discovery reconcile retries). Writes one `asset.interface.comment_updated` Event (+ `asset.interface.description.pushed|push_failed` when a push was attempted).
- `GET    /assets/:id/hardware-history?range=...[&sensorName=...]`  — Per-sensor hardware-reading time-series. Samples carry `{ timestamp, sensorName, sensorClass, unit, value, alarmStatus? }`; returns `{ samples, stats: { total, avgValue, minValue, maxValue } }`. Backed by the `hardware` retention entity / tier router.
- `GET    /assets/:id/metric-thresholds?metric=…[&sensorName=&sensorClass=]` — The severity thresholds that would fire on this asset's charted metric (`assets:read`), so a detail chart can shade its line with the engine's own numbers. Returns `{metric, tiers[{severity, operator, threshold, ruleId, ruleName}]}` ordered least → most severe, from `notificationRuleService.getMetricSeverityTiers`: every enabled scope-matching automation contributes either its `resolveTierLadder` (numeric single trigger — tier 0 plus each severity band) or each composite leaf on that metric at the rule's severity. `sensorName`/`sensorClass` identify the charted sensor so a rule whose dimensionFilter doesn't select it is skipped. Only ordered comparators appear (`==`/`!=` shade nothing); ties at one severity keep the more sensitive threshold; hot (`>=`) and cold (`<=`) tiers of the same severity are both returned. Consumed by `_severityChartLayer` in assets.js.
- `GET    /assets/:id/storage-history?mountPath=...&range=...`  — Per-mountpoint usage samples. SNMP-monitored assets only.
- `GET    /assets/:id/ipsec-history?tunnelName=...&range=...`  — Per-tunnel IPsec samples (status timeline + cumulative bytes). FortiOS-monitored assets only.
- `GET    /assets/:id/sdwan-members`  — Per-WAN-member health summary (aggregate up/down, per-health-check latency/jitter/loss, recent up/down status strip, + IP/link/bytes joined from the latest interface sample). Drives the "SD-WAN Members" table above the rules.
- `GET    /assets/:id/perf-sla-links`  — Distinct (healthCheck, link) pairs + latest SLA thresholds. SD-WAN data-exists gate + selector source for the SD-WAN tab.
- `GET    /assets/:id/perf-sla-history?healthCheck=...&link=...&range=...`  — Per-member SD-WAN Performance SLA latency/jitter/packet-loss gauges over time (tier-aware).
- `GET    /assets/:id/sdwan-rules`  — Current-state SD-WAN service rules (selected member + members/criteria/health-checks/destination/status + priority zones), one row per rule from the `asset_sdwan_rules` table, ordered by FortiOS rule priority. No history endpoint — SD-WAN rules are current-state.
- `GET    /assets/:id/mclag-peers`  — Current-state MCLAG ICL peers from the `asset_mclag_peers` table (FortiSwitch only; empty for switches not in an MCLAG pair), one row per local ICL port ordered by port name. Each row carries `localPort` / `iclTrunk` / `peerSn` / `peerName` / `peerPort` + `matchedAsset { id, hostname }` (the peer switch resolved by serial, for a clickable link). No history — current-state.
- `GET    /assets/:id/virtualization`  — Current-state vCenter facts for the asset-details Virtualization section (General tab), assembled per role from the `Asset.virtualization` blob. VM role: the blob + `hostAsset {id, hostname, monitorStatus}` (clickable running-host link, re-resolved every discovery cycle) + `diskDatastores` (name/type/backingLabel for the disks table). Host role: the blob + `datastores` (VcenterDatastore rows whose `hostMorefs` contain this host, BigInt→string) + `vms` (assets whose `virtualization.hostAssetId` points here, with power state + monitor status). Assets without vCenter data return `{virtualization: null}` and the UI skips the section.
- `GET    /assets/:id/processes`  — Current-state process inventory (one row per program, cpuPct desc) + the `monitoredProcesses` / `alertWatchedProcesses` pin arrays. Drives the merged Services tab's *Include processes* view + its Monitor/Map checkbox state (the standalone Processes tab was folded into Services 2026-07; the Alert pin column was dropped from the UI — alerting is handled by Automations — though `alertWatchedProcesses` is still returned).
- `GET    /assets/:id/services`  *(assets=read)* — Current-state service inventory (one row per systemd unit / Windows service, unit-sorted) from `AssetService` + the `monitoredServices` (Logs) / `mappedServices` (Map) pin arrays. Drives the merged Services tab (units by default; the *Include processes* checkbox folds `/processes` rows into the same table). Read-only — Start/Stop/Restart control was removed (Satellite-posture change). `memBytes` BigInt→string.
- `GET    /assets/:id/service-logs?unit=...&since=...&limit=...&flagged=1`  *(assets=read)* — recent journalctl lines for a pinned unit (newest-first, capped 2000) from `asset_service_log_samples`, each annotated with matching `LogFlagRule`s (read-time `evaluateLogFlags`; global/asset-scoped rules apply, unit passed as the process key). Drives the Services detail-panel log viewer. Phase 2.
- `GET    /assets/:id/process-history?name=...&range=...`  — Per-pinned-program CPU/RAM history, tier-routed (detail → hourly → daily) via `readProcessHistory` + `pickSampleTierForAsset("process")`. Drives the per-process detail slide-in charts.
- `GET    /assets/:id/process-logs?name=...&since=...&limit=...&flagged=1`  — Recent log lines for a pinned program (newest-first, capped), from the standalone `asset_process_log_samples` table, each annotated with the `LogFlagRule`s it matches (read-time eval via `evaluateLogFlags`). `flagged=1` returns only matched lines. Drives the slide-in log viewer + its Flagged-only toggle.
- `GET    /assets/:id/process-connections?name=<processName>|unit=<unit>`  *(assets=read)* — Ports & Connections for the process detail slide-in AND the Services detail panel (Application Map data, per-asset view): `{ listening[], outbound[], inbound[] }` from `AssetProcessConnection`, sorted lastSeen desc, capped 500/section; remote endpoints hydrated with the matched asset id + hostname via `applicationMapService.resolveIpsToAssets`. Optional `name` filters to one process; optional `unit` (Phase 3) filters to one systemd unit / Windows service.
- `GET/POST/PUT/DELETE /log-flag-rules` (`src/api/routes/logFlagRules.ts`)  — CRUD for user-defined log-flag rules. List = `assets:read`; writes = `assets:write`. Backed by `logFlagRuleService` (read-time eval + compiled-rule cache).
- `GET /alerts` (`alerts:read`, region-scoped) / `POST /alerts/acknowledge` (`alerts:write`) / `POST /alerts/clear` (`alerts:fullwrite`) (`src/api/routes/notifications.ts`; deprecated alias mount `/notifications`) — triggered-alert list + lifecycle. Backed by `notificationService`. Per-asset bundle at `GET /assets/:id/alerts` (alias `/assets/:id/notifications`; `assets:read`) → `{active, matchingRules}` — `matchingRules` are full v2 rule rows, which is what lets the asset-details Alerts tab render each automation's TRIGGER SENTENCE (the same summary the edit modal shows, severity ladder included) and open that rule in the wizard when its name is clicked. `active` rows are whole Notification records, and the tab's **Detail** column is their `dimension` — without it a per-interface automation's alerts all render one message template at one timestamp and are indistinguishable, which is also why the tab's acknowledge/clear run over a multi-select through the batch routes rather than one row at a time. All notification-era alias mounts answer with `Deprecation: true` + a successor-version `Link` header (`deprecatedAlias` helper in `src/api/router.ts`).
- `GET /automations` / `POST` / `PUT/:id` / `DELETE/:id` (`automationManagement:read` for list/schema/recipient-users, `fullwrite` for CRUD/preview), `GET /automations/schema`, `GET /automations/scope-options` (device-filter picker lists: distinct manufacturers/models of **MONITORED** assets + non-deprecated IPAM subnets {id,name,cidr} + region + role catalogues — backed by `notificationRuleService.listScopeOptions`. Monitored-only because a value that only unmonitored inventory reports is a filter choice that can't produce a metric alert; the subnet list is IPAM rather than inventory and stays unfiltered, and MATCHING is unaffected — `scopeWhere` still selects unmonitored devices, since event/change triggers fire on them), `GET /automations/recipient-users` (users for the recipient picker), `POST /automations/dimension-values` (`automationManagement:read`; body `{metric, dimension, scope, narrow?}` → `{values[{value, assetCount}], strict, noun, narrowLabel, scopedAssets, sampledAssets, assetsWithData, windowHours}` — what the DRAFT'S OWN devices currently report for a metric's dimensionFilter field, so the builder renders a picker instead of free text; backed by `notificationDimensionService.listDimensionValues`. Both operator-pinned dimensions read the pin set rather than the samples: `ifNamePattern` from `Asset.monitoredInterfaces` (which is also the engine's gate) and `mountPathPattern` from `Asset.monitoredStorage` (which is NOT — the storage stream samples every mountpath at `cadence:"slow"`, so a stored rule on an unpinned mount still evaluates; the picker steers to the mounts that keep history, since a multi-day aggregate over a 24h retention window reads almost nothing)), `POST /automations/preview` (accepts partial drafts via `previewInputSchema`: a `{scope}`-only body lists the matched devices — the wizard's Step-2 preview — and `{trigger, scope}` works without a name; the result carries `totalAssets` = DISTINCT devices alongside `totalEvaluated` = readings, since per-dimension metrics fan out to one reading per sensor/interface/mount) (`src/api/routes/notificationRules.ts`; deprecated alias mount `/notification-rules`) — automation (rule) CRUD (incl. delivery `targets` + recipient routing, `emailComposition`, and `escalation` — escalation tier channels are validated email-type at save with a friendly 400) + builder vocabulary (`/schema` includes `templateVariables`, the {token} catalog for the builder's insert-variable palette) + dry-run (preview additionally returns `emailPreview` {subject, text, html?} rendered against the first match when the draft has emailComposition). Backed by `notificationRuleService` + `notificationRecipientService.listRecipientUsers` + `notificationEngine.previewRule`.
- `GET /maintenance-schedules` / `POST` / `PUT/:id` / `DELETE/:id` (`maintenanceManagement:read` for list, `fullwrite` for CRUD), `POST /maintenance-schedules/preview` (`fullwrite`; `src/api/routes/maintenanceSchedules.ts`) — maintenance-schedule CRUD + target-filter dry-run. Preview returns `{ total, assets[≤50] }` (hostname/ip/model/manufacturer, hostname-sorted, monitored-only). Body: `{ name, enabled?, criteria? (tagAssignmentService vocabulary, status rules rejected), assetIds?, schedule (maintenanceRecurrence shape; a oneshot may carry `startNow: true` — resolved to a SERVER-stamped startAt by `resolveStartNow` before validation, marker stripped, so ad-hoc entry is immediate regardless of client clock/TZ skew), suppressChildren? (default true — whether in-window assets count as down for child dependency suppression; a PUT that omits it snaps back to true, so callers pass it through) }`. Every mutation runs `reconcileMaintenance()` inline before responding — a now-active one-shot (the pill's ad-hoc path) has already flipped its assets to `status="maintenance"` when the 201 returns. Backed by `maintenanceScheduleService`.
- `GET /maintenance-schedules/occurrences?from=YYYY-MM-DD&to=YYYY-MM-DD` (`maintenanceManagement:read`) — the Maintenance modal's **calendar** tab. Expands EVERY schedule's occurrences across the inclusive day range (`expandOccurrences` per schedule; range capped at 400 days, response at 2000 occurrences with a `truncated` flag) and returns `{ from, to, truncated, occurrences: [{ scheduleId, name, enabled, kind, adhoc, start, end }] }`, start/end as **server-local wall-clock strings** (`"2026-08-12T22:00"`), never instants — the recurrence engine runs on the server's clock, so handing the browser a UTC Date would paint windows on the wrong day for any operator in another timezone. A schedule whose stored shape no longer validates is skipped, not fatal. Backed by `maintenanceScheduleService.listOccurrences`.
- `GET /maintenance-schedules/server-time` (`maintenanceManagement:read`) — `{ now, timeZone, offsetMinutes }`: the server's wall clock as the same local-ISO minute string every schedule shape carries (`"2026-08-19T14:30"`), its resolved IANA zone (`""` on a stripped image with no zone data), and its UTC offset **east-positive** (Central DST = `-300`, the sign operators write, opposite `getTimezoneOffset`). Declared **before `/:id`** so the literal path isn't captured. Backed by the pure `serverClockInfo` in `src/utils/maintenanceRecurrence.ts`.  **Why it exists:** every maintenance time is server-local wall clock with NO offset — that is the only reading that survives DST (a 22:00 nightly window means 22:00 at the site). The browser broke the other half of that contract: the one-shot pickers were prefilled from `new Date()` in the BROWSER and posted the operator's digits for the server to read as its own. On a UTC-clocked host with a Central operator, "now → now + 2h" mapped onto a server window that started five hours ago and had **already ended** — so a bulk-selected batch of switches/APs saved cleanly, `isInWindow` was false forever, no `maintenance.entered` Event was written, and every asset kept showing Down. `resolveStartNow` covered only the ad-hoc START; every operator-picked END time had the same hole (the ad-hoc path entered maintenance and then exited on the very next 30s reconcile). The browser now folds timezone difference AND clock drift into one minute-rounded skew (`_maintLoadServerClock` in `public/js/assets-maintenance.js`, cached per page) and prefills, validates and LABELS every picker through it.
- `GET /automations/scope-options` additionally returns **`regions: string[]`** (the map-region catalogue via `mapRegionService.listRegions`, bare names, sorted). It rides this payload rather than `GET /map/regions` because that route is gated `mapRegions:read`, which an automation editor may not hold — the region picker would silently degrade to free text. Feeds the Web Push `recipientRegions` chips.
- `GET /contacts/search?q=&directory=1` additionally queries the opted-in AD/Entra directories (live; nothing stored) and returns `directoryAvailable` so the UI can tell "nobody matched" from "no directory configured". Rate-limited by `contactSearchLimiter` (600 / 5 min) because that path proxies an external API from operator keystrokes.
- `GET /contacts` / `POST` / `PUT/:id` / `DELETE/:id`, `GET /contacts/search?q=`, `POST /contacts/preview` (`src/api/routes/contacts.ts`) — the address book. Reads (`list` / `search` / `preview`) are gated `contacts:read`; the three mutations go through `requireOwnership("contacts")` (≥ write) and then `assertOwnership(req, row.createdBy, …)`, so a write-level caller edits or deletes only rows they created and `fullwrite` bypasses the filter — the subnets/reservations mechanism. Body: `{ email, name?, description?, assetCondition? (the DEVICE_FILTER condition tree), assetCriteria? (LEGACY tagAssignmentService vocabulary — still accepted, folded forward on write when the tree can express it), assetAllDevices?, assetIds? }`. A read adds two DERIVED fields the editor needs: `assetConditionEffective` (the filter as a tree whatever it is stored as) and `assetFilterUnconvertible` (fields a legacy blob uses that the tree can't say — non-empty means the builder can't render it). `POST /preview` answers `{ matchCount, unmonitoredCount, sample[] }`: the count and the list are MONITORED matches, with the unmonitored remainder counted rather than hidden — the filter does cover them (an event/change automation fires on an unmonitored device), they're just not what an operator is choosing between. `GET /search` returns `{ entries: [{ source: "user"|"contact"|"entra"|"ad", id, email, name, description, kind, owned? }] }` — Polaris users ∪ contacts, deduped by lower-cased email (user wins), prefix-first ranked, capped at 50; it is the automation wizard's recipient typeahead as well as the address-book picker's list. `POST /preview` returns `{ matchCount, sample[≤100] }` for a (criteria, pins) pair. `/search` and `/preview` are declared before `/:id`. Backed by `contactService`.
- `GET /contacts/filter-schema` (`contacts:read`) — the device-filter builder's vocabulary + value suggestions: `{ scopeCondition, options: { manufacturers, models, subnets, regions, roles, assetTypes, tags } }`. `scopeCondition` is `scopeConditionMeta(DEVICE_FILTER_FIELD_OPS)` — the same catalog builder `/automations/schema` uses, over the wider contact vocabulary, so field labels and operator wording can't drift between the two surfaces. Its own route rather than reusing `/automations/schema` + `/scope-options`, which are gated `automationManagement:read`: browsing the address book must not require permission to edit automations. `assetTypes` + `tags` ride this payload for the same reason regions/roles ride `/scope-options` — their own endpoints are gated `assets:read`, and without them the value pickers would silently degrade to free text. Declared before `/:id`.
- `GET /assets/:id/contacts` (`assets:read` AND `contacts:read`, chained — reading it exposes address-book content) — the address-book entries responsible for this device, for the slide-over's General-tab Contacts rows. Returns `{ contacts: [{ id, email, name, description, via }] }` where `via` is `"pinned"` (an explicit `Contact.assetIds` entry) or `"filter"` (a device-filter match) — an operator chasing an unexpected recipient needs to know which. Backed by `contactService.resolveContactsForAsset`.
- `GET /assets/:id/maintenance-windows?range=…|from&to` (`assets:read`) — `AssetMaintenanceWindow` rows overlapping the range (`{ windows: [{scheduleName, startedAt, endedAt, endReason}] }`); fetched once per asset-panel open and rendered as the labeled chart maintenance bands. `GET /assets/:id/maintenance-info` (`assets:read`) — `{ inMaintenance, returnStatus, openWindows[{scheduleName, startedAt, until}], schedules[{name, enabled, activeNow, nextStart, nextEnd}] }` for the edit-modal Monitoring tab.
- `GET|POST /delivery-channels`, `GET|PUT|DELETE /delivery-channels/:id`, `POST /delivery-channels/:id/test`, `POST /delivery-channels/:id/generate-vapid` (`automationManagement:read` for GET, `fullwrite` for mutations/test) (`src/api/routes/notificationChannels.ts`; deprecated alias mount `/notification-channels`) — delivery-channel registry CRUD (secrets masked on GET, preserved on PUT) + per-channel test send + VAPID keypair generation. Backed by `notificationChannelService` + the channel senders.
- `GET|PUT /delivery-channels/web-push` (`automationManagement:read` / `fullwrite`) — **Web Push as a single on/off capability**, not a channel to assemble. Every other type names a destination (SMTP host, webhook URL, Pushbullet account) and so earns a form; Web Push names nothing — the VAPID keypair is generated, the destinations are whichever devices users enrolled, and WHO receives a given alert is chosen per Notify action when an automation is built. `PUT {enabled:true}` creates the singleton + generates the keypair in one call; `{enabled:false}` flips `enabled` and **never deletes the row or the keys** (every `PushSubscription` is signed against that keypair — dropping it would silently invalidate every enrolled device). `GET` returns `{enabled, configured, subscriberCount, channelId}`; `subscriberCount` is what makes the toggle non-feedback-free. **Both routes must stay declared before `/:id`** or the literal path is captured as an id. The Delivery tab renders this as a toggle card and filters `web_push` out of both the channel cards and the add-channel type picker — but it remains in `GET /delivery-channels` because the automation builder must still be able to target it.
- `POST /delivery-channels/web-push/test` (`automationManagement:fullwrite`) — send a real push to **the caller's own** enrolled devices (`sendWebPushTest`). Scoped to `req.session.userId` deliberately: a test that could notify arbitrary other people is a nuisance vector, not a diagnostic. Sends directly rather than queueing a `NotificationDelivery`, so the operator gets the true per-device result instead of a "queued" shrug — but still builds the payload with `pushDeepLinkUrl(surface)`, so what lands on the device is shaped exactly like a production alert. A 404/410 prunes the row, mirroring the delivery drain. Returns `{ok, sent, failed, pruned, message}` and writes a `notification_channel.test` Event. Must be declared **before `/:id/test`**.
- `GET /push-subscriptions/key` / `POST /push-subscriptions` / `DELETE /push-subscriptions` (`alerts:read`) (`src/api/routes/pushSubscriptions.ts`) — VAPID public-key handoff (from the web_push channel) + per-user Web Push subscription store/remove. Backed by `notificationChannelService.getWebPushChannel` + the PushSubscription table.
- `GET /manifest.webmanifest` / `GET /icons/:file` (**no auth**) (`src/api/routes/pwa.ts`) — the mobile SPA's web app manifest, generated from the `branding` Setting so a custom logo/app name becomes the install identity, plus its home-screen icons rasterized on demand by `appIconService`. Mounted OUTSIDE `/api/v1` in `src/app.ts` **before `express.static`** (neither is a file on disk). Unauthenticated deliberately: a `<link rel="manifest">` without `crossorigin` is fetched with credentials omitted, so a session-gated manifest would 401 for every caller — and the payload is the same branding already served unauthenticated at `/server-settings/branding`. `:file` is matched against the `ICON_SPECS` allowlist (anything else 404s — an operator-supplied size would let resvg allocate an unbounded canvas). Manifest is `no-cache` + weak ETag; icons are `immutable` on the manifest's `?v=<version>` URLs and `max-age=300` on the bare paths `sw.js` uses.

### One-click acknowledge links (`/ack`, PUBLIC)

- `GET /ack/:token` / `POST /ack/:token` (**no auth**) (`src/api/routes/ack.ts`) — the acknowledge link carried in alert emails and behind the web-push Acknowledge button. Mounted in `src/app.ts` **after body parsing and BEFORE `session()` + `csrfMiddleware`**, outside `/api/v1`. The token in the path IS the credential: single-use, 30-day expiry, bound to one Notification AND one user, and worth exactly "acknowledge that alert as that user".
  - **The GET never changes state.** Outlook Safe Links, Proofpoint and every other mail gateway fetches links before a human sees them, so an acting GET would acknowledge every alert Polaris mails the moment it is scanned. The GET renders (confirm / already / used / expired / cleared / forbidden / invalid); only the POST redeems.
  - **Mount point is load-bearing.** Below `session()`, `csrfMiddleware` would stamp `req.session.csrfToken` on every scanner GET, dirtying an uninitialized session and making `connect-pg-simple` persist a row per scan. Above it, there is no session to mint.
  - HTML is self-contained with **no inline `<script>`** (CSP `scriptSrc: 'self'`; `styleSrc` allows inline and `formAction` allows `'self'`, so the control is a plain self-posting form that also works with scripting off). The route **never calls `next(err)`** — the shared errorHandler answers JSON, and this surface owns HTML for every outcome. `Cache-Control: no-store`, `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`, `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`.
  - `POST` answers JSON instead of HTML when `Accept: application/json` — that is what `public/sw.js`'s Acknowledge action button posts, with `credentials: "omit"` (no cookie, no CSRF header needed).
  - Status codes: 200 valid/already/cleared, 403 forbidden (the bound user's role lost `alerts:write` after the mail went out), 410 used/expired, 404 unknown — rendered vaguely, since an unknown token is the one case a stranger can reach. Rate-limited by `ackLinkLimiter` (300 / 5 min); an unknown token writes **no** Event (attacker-reachable unbounded audit writes), while a token Polaris really issued that then failed writes `notification.ack_link.rejected` at warning.
  - Backed entirely by `notificationAckService`; the acknowledgement itself goes through the same `acknowledgeNotifications` the API uses, with `details.source` = `ack_link` / `web_push_action`.
- `PUT    /assets/:id/processes/:name/config`  — Operator log-path config for a pinned program (`logSource` auto|journald-unit|file-glob + `logPathGlob` wildcard + notes). Upserts `AssetProcessConfig`; delivered to the agent via `GET /agents/config`'s `pinnedProcesses`. Writes `asset.process.log_config_set`.
The assets list and single-GET attach a synthesized `ipContext` field to each row: `{ subnetId, subnetCidr, reservation: { id, createdBy, sourceType } | null } | null` (null when the asset has no IP, or no non-deprecated subnet contains the IP). The list also attaches `monitoringMethods: string[]` — the reduced set of transports the asset is actually monitored by, computed by `computeMonitoringMethods` in `enrichAssetList` (`assets.ts`): `[]` when unmonitored, `["agent"]` when a `ManagedAgent` is `active` (the agent owns all streams), else the distinct resolved per-stream polling methods from `resolveMonitorSettings` (cached tiers, no per-row DB hit) with ICMP treated as subordinate — reachability-only, so it surfaces only when it's the sole method. Drives the Assets table's **Monitored Via** column (label per method, "Multiple" when several differ). The Assets page reads it to render a **View Lease** button on rows whose IP lives in a known subnet — clicking it navigates to `/subnets.html#ip=<subnetId>@<ipAddress>`, where the network slide-over opens scrolled to that IP's row. To reserve or release IPs, operators use the network slide-over directly (no asset-row Reserve/Unreserve buttons).

#### Quarantine (admin + assetsadmin, or bearer token whose bound role grants `assetsQuarantine` ≥ write)
- `GET    /assets/sighting-settings`            *(assetsQuarantine read)* — `{ sightingMaxAgeDays }` (default 180).
- `PUT    /assets/sighting-settings`            *(assetsQuarantine write)* — `{ sightingMaxAgeDays }`. Max 3650.
- `GET    /assets/:id/sightings`                *(auth)* — DHCP sighting history for this asset (list of `{ fortigateDevice, source, ipAddress, lastSeen, integrationId, subnetName, vlan }`). `subnetName` + `vlan` are resolved at request time by matching the stored `ipAddress` against subnets discovered on the same `fortigateDevice` — both are null when the IP doesn't fall inside any known subnet on that device (e.g. the subnet has been deleted or the sighting predates the `ipAddress` column).
- `GET    /assets/:id/sources`                  *(auth)* — Per-discovery-source view of an asset (Phase 3a of the multi-source asset model). Returns every `AssetSource` row attached to this asset with the originating integration's name + type joined in, sorted in stable presentation order (`entra` → `intune` → `ad` → `fortigate-firewall` → `fortiswitch` → `fortiap` → `manual`). Each entry: `{ id, sourceKind, externalId, integration: { id, name, type } | null, observed, state, inferred, syncedAt, firstSeen, lastSeen }`. `state` is `deriveAssetSourceState(sourceKind, observed)` from `src/utils/assetSourceState.ts` — the source's own enabled/disabled verdict normalized to `{ state: "enabled" | "disabled" | "unknown", kind: "account" | "runtime" | "none", label, field, value }`, so a caller doesn't have to know that Entra says `accountEnabled: false` where AD says `accountDisabled: true` and vCenter says `powerState: "POWERED_OFF"`. Rows are **collapsed by `(sourceKind, integrationId)`, keeping the most-recent (`lastSeen`-desc) row per source** — so a `fortigate-endpoint` source whose MAC-keyed `externalId` churned (each MAC change spawns a new `AssetSource` row and orphans the old one) renders as a single card instead of several near-identical ones. Serial/GUID-keyed kinds (`fortigate-firewall`/`switch`/`ap`, `ad`, `entra`, `intune`) have stable externalIds and never collapse; the dropped MAC/IP detail still surfaces in the Firewall Sightings + IP History tables on the same tab. Powers the **Sources** tab on the asset details modal — operators can see what each integration independently said about the device.
- `POST   /assets/:id/sources/:sourceId/split`  *(admin)* — Recovery action. Detaches the chosen `AssetSource` row from this asset and binds it to a freshly-created Asset whose discovery-owned fields are seeded from the source's `observed` blob via `projectAssetFromSources([source])`. The new Asset gets a `split-from-asset` tag plus a source-kind hint (`entraid` / `activedirectory` / `fortigate` / etc.). **Phase 4d retired the `assetTag` write here** — the AssetSource row that just got re-bound is the canonical identity link; the legacy `entra:`/`ad:`/`fgt:` assetTag prefixes were back-compat markers that re-discovery already stopped consulting in Phase 2. Refusal rules: source not on this asset (404), source is the asset's only source (409 — would leave the original orphaned), source is `sourceKind="manual"` (409 — backfill marker, not a real discovery source). Returns `{ originalAssetId, newAssetId, movedSourceId, newAsset }`. Asset-row FKs (monitoring samples, IP history, sightings, quarantine, conflicts) all stay on the **original** asset; the new Asset starts clean. Writes one `asset.split` Event with details `{ originalAssetId, newAssetId, sourceId, sourceKind, externalId }`.
- `GET    /assets/:id/polling-history`          *(auth)* — Polling-history summary for the merge comparison: how much sample history the asset holds across the monitor-probe + telemetry streams and all three retention tiers (detail / hourly / daily rollups). Returns `{ oldestAt, newestAt, spanDays, sampleCount, monitor: { oldestAt, newestAt, sampleCount }, telemetry: {...} }`. `sampleCount` is **stitched** so overlapping tier coverage isn't double-counted (all of daily + hourly buckets past daily coverage + detail rows past hourly coverage — `readPollingHistorySummary` in `sampleHistoryService.ts`); the UI presents it as approximate. Feeds the Merge Assets modal, which shows each side's history, **auto-selects the survivor with the longer history** (span first, count as tiebreak — the absorbed side's samples are orphaned by a merge), and warns in the confirm step when the operator overrides toward the shorter side.
- `POST   /assets/:id/merge`                    *(admin)* — Operator-driven asset merge — the **inverse of Split**. Absorbs another asset into this one. Body: `{ otherAssetId, survivor: "this" | "other" (default "this"), fieldWinners?: { <field>: "this" | "other" } }`. The operator picks which side survives (keeps its monitoring history + dependency edges + quarantine state + FKs) and resolves each differing field; `fieldWinners` keys are a subset of `MERGEABLE_FIELDS` (`src/services/assetMergeService.ts`), any omitted field defaults to blank-fill. Delegates to `mergeAssets()` in `assetMergeService.ts`: **re-binds ALL of the absorbed asset's `AssetSource` rows onto the survivor** (via the shared `absorbAssetRelations` — no `(sourceKind, externalId)` collision possible — globally unique — so the survivor becomes multi-source; this is the key difference from the automatic `mergeDuplicateHostnameAssets` job, which cascade-deletes the ghost's sources. `acceptAssetConflict`'s sibling-conflict absorb calls the same helper as of the fix below, so both operator-facing merges preserve provenance identically), transfers `AssetMacAddress` / `AssetAssociatedIp` / `AssetIpHistory` / `AssetFortigateSighting` (delete-on-conflict against the survivor's existing rows), re-binds the `ManagedAgent` enrollment iff the survivor has none, union-merges tags, keeps the more-recent `lastSeen`, applies field winners (clamping `acquiredAt ≤ lastSeen`), **OR-s `monitored`** (either side monitored ⇒ survivor monitored; when that flips the survivor ON it also adopts the absorbed row's `MONITOR_CONFIG_FIELDS` — per-stream polling methods / credentials / MIB pins / interval+timeout overrides, ghost's non-null wins — and UNIONs its `MONITOR_PIN_FIELDS` monitored/mapped arrays, resets `monitorStatus` + failure/success counters, and recomputes `monitorOverride`; skipped when the merged status resolves to `decommissioned`/`disabled` per business rule 10. Response: `carriedMonitoring` + `monitorFieldsAdopted`, both also stamped on the `asset.merged` Event), then deletes the absorbed asset. The absorbed asset's interface-comment overrides, dependency edges, LLDP/wireless rows, and pending Conflicts **cascade-delete**; its sample/telemetry/rollup/custom-widget time-series are **orphaned and aged out via `drop_chunks`** (no FK since migration `20260615000000` — a cascade delete would decompress their TimescaleDB chunks into bloat, prod incident 2026-06-08). Either way the survivor keeps its own history and the absorbed asset's is not carried over (the UI surfaces monitored status + sources + each side's polling-history size from `GET /assets/:id/polling-history` and auto-selects the longer-history side as survivor — operator-overridable; the confirm dialog quantifies the history being deleted, warns when the shorter side was kept, and warns the loss is permanent). Refusal rules: self-merge (400), either asset missing (404). Returns `{ survivorId, absorbedId, movedSources, movedMacs, movedIps, movedIpHistory, movedSightings, movedManagedAgent, appliedFields }`. Writes one `asset.merged` Event. Powers the **Merge asset…** button on the Sources tab.
- `GET    /assets/:id/dependencies`             *(auth)* — Read effective + computed + override parents AND direct children for the dependency-suppression DAG. Returns `{ asset: { id, hostname, assetType, dependencyLayer, dependencySuppressed, dependencySuppressedAt }, effectiveParents, computedParents, overrideParents, hasOverride, children, childrenTruncated, childCount }`. Each parent entry is `{ id (row id), parent: { id, hostname, assetType, dependencyLayer, monitorStatus, monitored }, source, detectedVia }`. **Resolution rule**: if any `source="override"` rows exist for this asset, the override set is the effective set (computed rows ignored); otherwise every NON-override row is effective — `computed` (Fortinet infra), `endpoint` (an endpoint's leaf edge) and `vcenter` (VM→host) alike. Both this split and the per-child binding rule tested `source === "computed"` literally until 2026-08, which hid the endpoint and vCenter halves from the tree even though the reconciler was suppressing on them. Empty override set = explicit "no parents" pin. The `children` array carries two layers down (direct children + grandchildren) — every asset that has THIS asset in its **effective** parent set plus, nested under each direct child, that child's own effective children. Each child entry: `{ id, hostname, assetType, dependencyLayer, monitorStatus, monitored, dependencySuppressed, source, detectedVia, childCount, grandchildren: [...] }` where each grandchild has the same shape minus `grandchildren`/`childCount`. Sorted within each layer by type (firewall→switch→access_point) then hostname. **The downward view is INFRA-ONLY at both layers** (`FORTINET_INFRA_ASSET_TYPES`, filtered in SQL — `take` applies before any in-memory filter, so a gate with 300 switch children would otherwise fill the read and report nothing). The endpoint half of the DAG makes every workstation / server / printer a child of the switch, AP or gate that last saw it, and a site gate is the last-seen device for the entire site, so those rows would bury the two or three an operator opened the tree to read. They are excluded here deliberately even though they are real edges the reconciler suppresses on — an endpoint's dependency is shown on its OWN General tab, as the parent above it, which is where the suppression it drives is worth explaining. Caps therefore bound a controller FortiGate's managed switches/APs, not the endpoint half: `DEP_INFRA_CHILD_CAP` 300 direct + `DEP_GRANDCHILD_CAP` 500 grandchildren, with `childrenTruncated` set when the direct read overflowed. `childCount` counts INFRA children only (a findMany over the indexed `parentAssetId` with the relation type filter, deduped per child — a groupBy can't filter on a relation) so the UI's "+N" hint can never become an endpoint tally, which is exactly the noise the type filter removes. Drives the General-tab Dependency Tree block on the asset details modal so the common firewall → switch → AP chain renders without click-through; operators still click through for anything deeper than two layers.
- `PUT    /assets/:id/dependencies/override`    *(admin)* — Replace the asset's `source="override"` rows. Body: `{ parentAssetIds: string[] }` (max 20). Each id must reference a real Fortinet infra asset (`firewall` / `switch` / `access_point`). Cycle check walks back through every proposed parent's existing effective parents — if any path reaches `id`, returns 400. Empty array = explicit "no parents" pin (asset opts out of suppression entirely; the GET response will then show `hasOverride: true` with empty `effectiveParents`). Writes one `asset.dependency.override_set` Event.
- `DELETE /assets/:id/dependencies/override`    *(admin)* — Clear all override rows; computed set takes effect. Writes one `asset.dependency.override_cleared` Event when at least one row was deleted.
- `POST   /assets/:id/dependency-test`           *(admin)* — Start a dependency-suppression test: marks the asset down (via `dependencyTestUntil`/`dependencyTestStartedBy`) for a window so operators can watch suppression propagate to children without a real outage.
- `DELETE /assets/:id/dependency-test`           *(admin)* — End the test early (clears `dependencyTestUntil`).
- `GET    /assets/:id/connection-path`          *(auth)* — Resolve the upward chain from this asset to its upstream FortiGate so the Device Map topology overlay can dim everything off-path. Returns `{ asset: {id, hostname, ipAddress, macAddress, assetType, monitorStatus}, hops: ConnectionPathHop[], alternateUplinks: number, siteId: string | null }`. Each hop carries `kind: "endpoint" | "switch" | "firewall"`, the asset row's id + hostname + ipAddress + macAddress + assetType + monitorStatus + monitored flag, plus optional `endpointPort` (port label parsed from the leaf endpoint's `lastSeenSwitch`, populated on the first switch hop) and `uplinkInterface` (the switch's local interface that goes UP, from `fortinetTopology.uplinkInterface`). Resolution: firewall short-circuits to a single-hop self-path; switches/APs walk upward from themselves; endpoints (workstations / servers / printers / other) parse `Asset.lastSeenSwitch = "<switchId>/<port>"` to find the upstream switch, then walk. The upward walk reads `AssetDependencyParent` rows (override rows take precedence over computed) and picks the parent with `monitorStatus="up"` AND most-recent `lastMonitorAt` for MCLAG / dual-homed switches; remaining-parent counts are summed across hops into `alternateUplinks` so the UI can hint "+N alternate uplinks." Falls back to `fortinetTopology.controllerFortigate` / `parentSwitch` when dependency rows are empty (fresh installs before the backfill job runs, or freshly-discovered switches awaiting recompute). Capped at 16 hops as a sanity guard against pathological data. `siteId` is the firewall asset id at the top of the chain when the walk reached one; null when the chain terminated short (orphan asset with no `lastSeenSwitch`, or upstream chain not yet discovered). Resolver lives at [src/services/connectionPathService.ts](src/services/connectionPathService.ts); consumed by the Device Map topology modal which overlays the endpoint as a Cytoscape node + dims off-path elements.
- `GET    /assets/:id/quarantine-status`        *(auth)* — `{ status, quarantineReason, quarantinedAt, quarantinedBy, quarantineTargets }`.
- `POST   /assets/:id/quarantine`               *(assetsQuarantine ≥ write — session or token role)* — Push MAC block to every FortiGate that has a sighting within `sightingMaxAgeDays`. Body: `{ reason? }`. Returns `{ message, succeededCount, failedCount, targets[] }`. On at least one push success the asset `status` is set to `quarantined` and `quarantineTargets` is stamped. actor is derived from session username or `req.apiToken.name`. **Infrastructure assets (`assetType` = `firewall` / `switch` / `access_point`) are rejected with 400** — quarantining the device that does the quarantining would lock the operator out of the network. Release endpoints don't enforce the type guard so a misclassified quarantine can still be undone.
- `DELETE /assets/:id/quarantine`               *(assetsQuarantine ≥ write — session or token role)* — Best-effort unpush from all synced targets, then restores `statusBeforeQuarantine` (defaults to `active`). Device-side failure does not block release.
- `POST   /assets/:id/quarantine/verify`        *(assetsQuarantine ≥ write — session or token role)* — Re-reads each target from the FortiGate and flips any missing ones to `drift`. Persists the updated `quarantineTargets` if drift was detected. Writes `asset.quarantine.drift_detected` Event.
- `POST   /assets/bulk-quarantine`              *(assetsQuarantine ≥ write — session or token role)* — Body `{ ids[], reason? }`. Per-asset errors are collected; partial success is still reported. Returns `{ results: [{ id, ok, message }] }`.
- `POST   /assets/bulk-quarantine/release`      *(assetsQuarantine ≥ write — session or token role)* — Body `{ ids[] }`. Best-effort release per asset.

### API Tokens — `apiTokens` function key (read at mount; writes escalate to `apiTokens=write`)
- `GET    /api-tokens`                          — List all tokens (`{ tokens[], roles[], quarantineIntegrations[] }`). `roles` is the role catalogue (`{ id, name, description, grantsQuarantineWrite, adminEquivalent }`) for the "acts as role" dropdown; `quarantineIntegrations` is the FMG/FortiGate roster (`{ id, name, type, enabled, pushQuarantineEnabled }`) so the UI can render the per-token integration picker and the "push disabled — integration off / pushQuarantine toggle off" alert without a second round-trip. Hashes are never returned.
- `POST   /api-tokens`                          — Create. Body: `{ name, roleId, integrationIds?: string[], expiresAt? }`. `integrationIds` is REQUIRED + non-empty when the chosen role grants `assetsQuarantine` ≥ write; ignored otherwise. Each id must reference a real integration of type `fortimanager` or `fortigate`. Binding an admin-equivalent role logs an `api_token.admin_equivalent` warning Event. Returns `{ token: ApiTokenSummary, rawToken: string }` — `rawToken` is shown once and never recoverable.
- `POST   /api-tokens/:id/revoke`               — Mark as revoked (token stops working immediately); row is kept for audit.
