- `DELETE /api-tokens/:id`                      — Hard-delete the token row.

### Credentials — mixed scoping
- `GET    /credentials`                         *(auth)* — List stored credentials with secrets masked. Read-open so any role's Asset Monitoring tab can render the credential picker.
- `GET    /credentials/usage`                   *(auth)* — Effective-usage asset count per credential, keyed by credential id (`{ [credId]: number }`). Drives the **Assets** column on the Stored Credentials table in one round-trip. Computed by `credentialService.getCredentialUsageCounts()` — one `asset.findMany` + class-override + integration lookups, resolving the FK fall-through (asset stream → asset default → class override → integration default) in memory. Registered before `/:id` so "usage" isn't read as an id.
- `GET    /credentials/:id`                     *(auth)* — Single credential, masked.
- `GET    /credentials/:id/usage`               *(auth)* — Full usage breakdown for one credential (`credentialService.getCredentialUsage`): `{ total, assetLevel[], classLevel[], integrationLevel[], classRefCount, integrationRefCount }`. Each asset lands in its most-specific tier bucket (asset > class > integration), so `total` is a true distinct count. Drives the credential **usage slide-in** in Server Settings → Credentials, whose asset rows deep-link to `/assets.html#view=asset:<id>`. Resolves by FK wiring ("where is this credential configured"), not by polling-method type-match. Since discovery stamps the integration's credential onto each discovered asset's `monitorCredentialId`, a stamped default whose value is one of the asset's integration's credentials is reclassified asset → integration level (only a per-stream slot or a default the integration doesn't provide is genuine asset-level).
- `POST   /credentials`                         *(admin)* — Create. Body: `{ name, type: "snmp"|"winrm"|"ssh", config }`. Type-specific config is validated server-side.
- `PUT    /credentials/:id`                     *(admin)* — Update. Type cannot be changed after creation. Resubmitting the mask sentinel for a secret field preserves the stored value.
- `DELETE /credentials/:id`                     *(admin)* — 409 if any asset effectively uses the credential (via `getCredentialUsage` — asset / class-override / integration-default tiers, all 8 per-stream slots + the `monitorCredentialId` default), with a level-aware message; also 409 when no asset resolves to it but a class override or integration default still references it (deleting would silently null those out).
- `POST   /credentials/test`                    *(admin)* — Exercise a credential against a chosen asset's IP without persisting anything. Body: `{ assetId, type, config, id? }`. When `id` is present, masked secrets in `config` are merged from the stored credential via `mergeConfigPreservingSecrets()` so the operator can edit and test without retyping the password. Resolves the asset's host from `ipAddress || dnsName || hostname`, then dispatches to `monitoringService.probeCredentialAgainstHost()` (icmp/snmp/winrm/ssh — the same one-shot probe primitives used by the response-time monitor). Returns the standard probe shape `{ success, responseTimeMs, error?, host }`. Validation failures are returned in the same shape rather than 4xx so the modal renders them inline alongside probe failures. Drives the **Test Connection** button on the add/edit credential modal in Server Settings → Credentials, which opens a second modal with an asset autocomplete (powered by `GET /assets?search=…&limit=25` — not the global `/search` endpoint, whose 8-per-group cap and pinned-firewall→`sites` partition silently dropped firewalls from the picker) and reports the result inline. Each call writes one `credential.tested` Event (info on success, warning on failure).

### Manufacturer Aliases — `requireAdmin`
- `GET    /manufacturer-aliases`                — List every alias row (`{ id, alias, canonical, createdAt, updatedAt }`).
- `POST   /manufacturer-aliases`                — Create. Body: `{ alias, canonical }`. `alias` is normalized to lowercase + trimmed before insert; uniqueness on the lowercased form. 409 on duplicate. Saving refreshes the in-memory cache and runs `applyAliasesToExistingRows()` in the background so existing Asset/MibFile rows pick up the new mapping.
- `PUT    /manufacturer-aliases/:id`            — Update. Either or both of `alias` / `canonical` can be supplied. Same cache-refresh + backfill on save.
- `DELETE /manufacturer-aliases/:id`            — Remove. Cache is refreshed; existing rows are not rewritten (they already hold the canonical value).

### Monitor Settings — mixed scoping
Reads open to any authenticated caller (the asset edit modal's tier-badge UI needs them); writes require **assetsadmin** (admin also passes). All writes invalidate the in-memory resolver cache for the relevant scope and emit one `monitor_settings.{manual|integration|class_override}.{updated|created|deleted}` audit Event. See the **Monitor Settings Hierarchy** section below for the resolution model.
- `GET    /monitor-settings/manual`              *(auth)* — Manual tier (settings for orphan assets — `discoveredByIntegrationId = null`). Returns the saved JSON or `null` when unseeded.
- `PUT    /monitor-settings/manual`              *(assetsadmin)* — Replace the manual tier with the full tier-3 block: `{ intervalSeconds (1..86400), failureThreshold (1..100), probeTimeoutMs (100..60000), telemetryTimeoutMs (1000..120000, optional), systemInfoTimeoutMs (1000..120000, optional), telemetryIntervalSeconds (15..86400), systemInfoIntervalSeconds (60..86400), sampleRetentionDays (0..3650), telemetryRetentionDays (0..3650), systemInfoRetentionDays (0..3650) }`. `telemetryTimeoutMs` / `systemInfoTimeoutMs` are optional/nullable so existing call sites that didn't supply them keep working — null falls through to the hardcoded floor (10000ms each).
- `GET    /monitor-settings/integration/:id`     *(auth)* — Integration tier (settings stored at `Integration.config.monitorSettings`). Returns `{ integrationId, integrationName, integrationType, settings: TierSettings | null }`.
- `PUT    /monitor-settings/integration/:id`     *(assetsadmin)* — Same body shape as the manual tier. Writes the JSON into `Integration.config.monitorSettings` without clobbering other config keys.
- `GET    /monitor-settings/class-overrides`     *(auth)* — List class overrides. Filterable by `?integrationId=` (use the URL sentinel `null` for the manual-tier scope) and `?assetType=`. Each row carries the joined integration `{ id, name, type }`.
- `POST   /monitor-settings/class-overrides`     *(assetsadmin)* — Create. Body: `{ integrationId: uuid | null, assetType, ...partialTierSettings }`. Every settings field is optional — null means inherit from below. 409 if a row already exists for `(integrationId, assetType)`. 400 if `integrationId` is non-null but doesn't reference a real integration.
- `PUT    /monitor-settings/class-overrides/:id` *(assetsadmin)* — Update. Body accepts any subset of the 8 settings fields; each null clears that field (= inherit from below).
- `DELETE /monitor-settings/class-overrides/:id` *(assetsadmin)* — Remove the row.
- `GET    /monitor-settings/asset-overrides`     *(auth)* — Reverse lookup. Returns assets that have at least one of `monitorIntervalSec` / `cpuMemoryIntervalSec` / `temperatureIntervalSec` / `systemInfoIntervalSec` / `probeTimeoutMs` / `cpuMemoryTimeoutMs` / `temperatureTimeoutMs` / `systemInfoTimeoutMs` set OR any per-stream polling column non-null, filterable by `?integrationId=` (URL sentinel `null` = manual scope) and `?assetType=`. Capped at 500 rows. Drives the asset edit modal's "Show other asset overrides under this scope" slide-over.

#### Monitor Settings Hierarchy

Resolution order, most-specific first:

```
asset override  →  (assetType + manual) class override (manual scope only — Phase 2)
                →  per-class streams block on integration  (when discoveredByIntegrationId is set)
                                      Integration.config.<klass>Monitor.streams.<stream>:
                                        - fortimanager / fortigate: fortigateMonitor (assetType=firewall) /
                                          fortiswitchMonitor (assetType=switch) /
                                          fortiapMonitor (assetType=access_point)
                                        - activedirectory / entraid / windowsserver:
                                          workstationMonitor (assetType=workstation) /
                                          serverMonitor (assetType=server)
                →  integration tier   (when discoveredByIntegrationId is set; flat
                                       Integration.config.monitorSettings — used by endpoint
                                       asset types not covered by a per-class subtab set)
                →  systemInfoIntervalSeconds ONLY: derive from integration.pollInterval × 3600
                                      (when discoveredByIntegrationId is set AND tier-3 left it null AND
                                       the per-class streams block didn't set interfaces.intervalSeconds)
                →  manual tier        (when discoveredByIntegrationId is null)
                →  hardcoded floor    (final fallback; never user-visible)
```

- **Tier-1 / per-asset** — columns on `Asset`: `monitorIntervalSec`, `cpuMemoryIntervalSec`, `temperatureIntervalSec`, `systemInfoIntervalSec`, `lldpIntervalSec` *(Phase 2)*, `storageIntervalSec` *(Phase 2)*, `probeTimeoutMs`, `cpuMemoryTimeoutMs`, `temperatureTimeoutMs`, `systemInfoTimeoutMs`. null = inherit. These cadence/timeout fields are the ONLY settings that cascade to the per-asset tier; `failureThreshold` and the three retentions stop at tier-2. CPU/memory and temperature each carry their own per-stream column set as of Slice 2; LLDP and Storage gained their own per-asset cadence columns in Phase 2 alongside the queue carve-out.
- **Tier-2 / class override** — `MonitorClassOverride` row keyed on `(integrationId, assetType)`. **As of Phase 2 this table is manual-scope only** (`integrationId IS NULL`). The `POST` and `PUT` routes reject integration-scoped writes outright with 400; the `migrateMonitorSettingsPerClass` startup job folds historical integration-scoped rows into the per-class streams blocks on each integration and deletes them in the same transaction. Every settings field is nullable; null = inherit. Includes its own `cpuMemoryTimeoutMs` / `temperatureTimeoutMs` / `systemInfoTimeoutMs` alongside `probeTimeoutMs`.
- **Tier-3a / per-class streams (Phase 2 — integration-discovered assets only)** — `Integration.config.<klass>Monitor.streams.<stream>` where the class block is picked by `Asset.assetType`. Per integration type:
  - `fortimanager` / `fortigate` → `fortigateMonitor` (firewall) / `fortiswitchMonitor` (switch) / `fortiapMonitor` (access_point). FortiAP omits storage.
  - `activedirectory` / `entraid` / `windowsserver` → `workstationMonitor` (workstation) / `serverMonitor` (server).
  Each stream cell carries `{polling, credentialId, intervalSeconds, timeoutMs, mibId, failureThreshold?}` — `failureThreshold` only applies on `responseTime`; the resolver ignores it elsewhere. Null on any cell falls through to the flat tier-3 baseline below. Endpoint asset types (printer / router / other / etc.) discovered via FortiGate DHCP or AD/Entra/WinSrv that don't fall into a per-class subtab set bypass this tier entirely and use the flat baseline directly. See `pickClassStreamsBlock` + `applyClassStreamsOverlay` in `monitoringService.ts`.
- **Tier-3b / integration flat baseline or manual** — full tier-settings block (cadence/retention/threshold + the three timeout fields + the Phase 2 LLDP / Storage cadence + timeout fields), complete (no nulls) **except `systemInfoIntervalSeconds` at the integration tier**, which is nullable. Stored at `Integration.config.monitorSettings` for integration-discovered assets, or in the `manualMonitorSettings` Setting row for orphan assets. Existing tier-3 rows written before the LLDP / Storage tuning fields existed fall through to the hardcoded floor (10000ms timeouts, 600s LLDP+Storage interval) via the resolver's `tierFromJson` default until an operator saves new values.
- **Integration pollInterval linkage** (`systemInfoIntervalSeconds` only). When the integration tier doesn't explicitly set this field (operator left it blank, OR the migration job retroactively nulled the literal-default 600s), `loadIntegrationTierSettings` derives the cadence from `integration.pollInterval × 3600` so interface / LLDP / storage / IPsec scrape on the same schedule discovery already runs (1–24h pollInterval → 3600–86400s systemInfo). Ties the heavy-cadence work to a knob operators already understand and cuts interface-sample volume by 24× at the default 4h pollInterval. Explicit per-asset / class / integration-tier values still win. Tracked in `tierSystemInfoFromPollIntervalCache` (parallel to `tierCache`); `resolveMonitorSettingsWithProvenance` reads it to label the provenance `"integrationPollInterval"` so the integration edit modal's Cadence & Retention input renders `Leave blank to follow this integration's discovery interval (currently 4h)`. Manual-tier orphan assets are not eligible (no integration to inherit from) and fall through to the hardcoded floor. Existing 600s defaults are nulled retroactively by the `migrateSystemInfoCadenceLinkage` startup job. The `/assets/:id/effective-monitor-settings` response includes `integration: { id, name, type, pollInterval }` so frontend hints can be rendered without a second round-trip.
- **Hardcoded floor** — values baked into `monitoringService.ts` (60s probe, 60s telemetry, 600s sysinfo, 5000ms probe timeout, 10000ms telemetry timeout, 10000ms system-info timeout, threshold 3, 30d retentions). Final fallback only used when the migration job hasn't seeded tier-3 yet AND the legacy `monitorSettings` Setting row is also gone.

`resolveMonitorSettings(asset)` (in `src/services/monitoringService.ts`) walks the four tiers and returns the effective values. `resolveMonitorSettingsWithProvenance(asset)` returns the same plus per-field `provenance: "asset" | "class" | "integration" | "integration-class" | "manual" | "integrationPollInterval" | "default"` labels and the `classOverrideId` for UI deep-links. **Both derive from one core (`resolveMonitorSettingsCore`, 2026-08 fold)**, so the UI payload is by construction the runtime resolution — polling values are compatibility-gated at every tier with source-default substitution, and `"default"` labels a polling field where no tier supplied a compatible method (the resolved value carries the materialized source default, which may be null when the stream isn't delivered for the source kind). The UI-only extras (per-class origin sub-labels, `classOverrideId`, the pollInterval sub-label) live in the provenance wrapper so the plain resolver stays hot-path cheap. `"integration-class"` (Phase 2 — sub-label of the integration tier) means the value came from the per-class streams block `<klass>Monitor.streams.<stream>` rather than the flat `monitorSettings` baseline, so the asset modal's tier badge reads "FortiSwitch subtab" instead of generic "FortiManager". `"integrationPollInterval"` is a `systemInfoIntervalSeconds`-only sub-label indicating the value was derived from the integration's discovery `pollInterval` rather than read from explicit tier-3 JSON. **Resolver cache key is now `${integrationId}:${assetType}`** (Phase 2 — was previously `${integrationId}`); each per-class branch gets its own cached snapshot. Write paths (the tier CRUD in `monitorSettingsService.ts`, the integration config save) call `invalidateMonitorSettingsCache({integrationId, assetType?})` after every write — when `assetType` is omitted (integration config save), every `${integrationId}:*` entry is walked and dropped.

There is **no probe backoff for confirmed-down hosts, and no acceleration mid-run either**. Down assets keep probing at the resolved `intervalSeconds`, and so does an asset whose failure/recovery run is still being confirmed -- so `down` is reached after `failureThreshold x intervalSeconds`. (The fast-confirm re-probe that shortened that to ~35s regardless of cadence was removed 2026-08-19; `fastConfirmIntervalSec` survives as a dormant column read by nothing, and in-run resolution is now the ICMP loss sampler's job, feeding packet loss only -- business rule 30.) Heavy cadences (telemetry / systemInfo / fastFiltered) are still suppressed while `monitorStatus = "down"` so a wedged peer doesn't burn worker time, but the cheap response-time probe keeps firing — recovery is detected within one base-cadence tick instead of up to 30 minutes.

**Cross-transport streams — `processes` + `eventLog`** (migration `20260623000000_processes_eventlog_streams`). Two additional streams flow through the same hierarchy as the original six. They are **not agent-only** — `processes` resolves to agent / SNMP (`hrSWRunTable`/`hrSWRunPerfTable`) / SSH (`ps`,`tasklist`) / WinRM (`Get-Process`); `eventLog` resolves to agent / SSH (`journalctl`,`Get-WinEvent`) / WinRM / REST (FortiOS device log). The allowed method set per stream is enforced by `STREAM_METHODS` + `isMethodValidForStream` in `src/utils/pollingCompatibility.ts` (`processes` rejects REST + ICMP; `eventLog` rejects SNMP + ICMP), and `resolveStream` adopts a tier's method only when it passes BOTH the source matrix AND the stream matrix. Both default to **`disabled`** for every source (`defaultPollingForSource`) — opt-in. Columns mirror the storage stream on `Asset` + `MonitorClassOverride`: `processesPolling`/`eventLogPolling`, `processesIntervalSec(onds)`/`eventLogIntervalSec(onds)`, `processesTimeoutMs`/`eventLogTimeoutMs`, `processesCredentialId`/`eventLogCredentialId`, `processesMibId` (eventLog has no MIB). The integration Monitoring tab renders **Processes** + **Event Log** stream subtabs next to Storage (`_ALL_STREAMS` in `public/js/integrations.js`); `_streamsForClass` scopes them — workstation/server get both, FortiGate gets eventLog only, FortiSwitch/FortiAP get neither. Per-transport collectors land in later phases; the foundational layer is the configuration surface + resolution only.

#### Where each tier is edited

- **Tier-3 integration (Phase 2 per-class)** — each integration's edit modal has a **Monitoring tab** with **per-class subtabs** (FMG / FortiGate: FortiGate / FortiSwitch / FortiAP; AD / Entra ID / Windows Server: Workstations / Servers). Each class subtab carries the six per-stream subtabs (Response Time / CPU/Memory / Temperature / Interfaces / LLDP / Storage; FortiAP omits Storage). Each per-stream subtab holds the polling method, credential, cadence, timeout, and (response-time only) failure threshold. Save Changes serializes each class's stream values into `Integration.config.<klass>Monitor.streams.<stream>` via the regular integration PUT; the flat `monitorSettings` JSON is still written from the FortiGate / Workstations subtab as the "default for endpoint asset types" fallback.
- **Tier-3 manual** — Assets page header → **Monitoring Settings** button → modal's **Manual Monitoring** section. Same per-stream layout. Used by orphan / manually-created assets. Writes via `PUT /api/v1/monitor-settings/manual`.
- **Tier-2 class overrides (manual scope only — Phase 2)** — Assets-page **Monitoring Settings** modal → **Class Overrides** section. The source picker no longer surfaces integrations; the section is labelled "Manual scope only — assets without an integration source." Backend `POST` / `PUT` reject integration-scoped rows with 400. Operators who used to add overrides scoped to a specific integration now use that integration's per-class subtabs (above) which deliver the same effect via the streams block instead of the override table.
- **Tier-1 per-asset** — the asset edit modal's **Monitoring tab** carries the cadence/timeout overrides (`monitorIntervalSec`, `probeTimeoutMs`, plus the per-asset `cpuMemoryIntervalSec` / `temperatureIntervalSec` / `systemInfoIntervalSec` columns), tier-source badges from `/effective-monitor-settings`, and a **Show other asset overrides under this scope** button that opens a slide-over listing peer assets with their own per-asset overrides.

The integration's Monitoring tab additionally carries a **Discovery Defaults** section on FMG/FortiGate types only, with three subtabs (FortiGates / FortiSwitches / FortiAPs). Each subtab holds discovery-time concerns: `addAsMonitored`, `snmpCredentialId`, `sshCredentialId`, `autoMonitorInterfaces`. **Cadence inputs are no longer in these subtabs** — they live in the Cadence & Retention section above and apply uniformly across the integration's entire fleet. The credential rows are **type-aware**: the SNMP picker is rendered only when at least one of the four integration-tier polling dropdowns is set to SNMP, the SSH picker only when at least one is set to SSH, and both stay hidden when neither is selected. Credentials persist regardless of visibility, so flipping back later restores the prior selection.

### Events — mixed scoping
- `GET    /events`                              *(auth)* — Audit log (filter by level, action, resourceType, resourceName, actor, message — the text columns are case-insensitive substring by default and take an operator-aware `<field>Op` of contains | not_contains | empty | is_not_empty)
- `GET    /events/resource-types`               *(auth)* — distinct `resourceType` values across the retention window; feeds the full Resource-column filter option set on the Events page
- `GET    /events/archive-settings`             *(admin)* — reveals SSH host/user/path even with password masked
- `PUT    /events/archive-settings`             *(admin)*
- `POST   /events/archive-test`                 *(admin)*
- `GET    /events/syslog-settings`              *(admin)* — reveals host/port/TLS paths
- `PUT    /events/syslog-settings`              *(admin)*
- `POST   /events/syslog-test`                  *(admin)*
- `GET    /events/retention-settings`           *(auth)*
- `PUT    /events/retention-settings`           *(admin)*
- `GET    /events/asset-decommission-settings`  *(auth)*
- `PUT    /events/asset-decommission-settings`  *(admin)* — `{ inactivityMonths }`; 0 disables auto-decommission

### Conflicts — `requireAuth` (role-scoped list + resolve)
- `GET    /conflicts`                           — List. Gated on `discoveryConflicts:read` — any holder sees both entity types (the historical networkadmin↔reservation / assetsadmin↔asset role-name split was dropped 2026-08); others see an empty list.
- `GET    /conflicts/count`                     — Badge count; same role scoping as the list.
- `POST   /conflicts/:id/accept`                — Reservation: apply discovered values. Asset: upsert an `AssetSource` row (`sourceKind` = `entra`/`ad`, `externalId` = `proposedDeviceId`) tying the existing asset to the proposed Entra/AD identity, plus overlay Entra/AD fields into empty existing fields. **Hostname has one extra rule:** when the conflict was raised via 15-char NetBIOS truncation (`proposedAssetFields.matchedVia === "netbios"`), the longer canonical hostname replaces the truncated one even when the existing field is non-empty — the truncated form is a NetBIOS quirk, not a deliberate choice. **Phase 4d retired the legacy `assetTag = entra:<id>` / `ad:<guid>` write** — the AssetSource row is now the canonical identity link, and audit trail is captured by the auto-resolve syncLog event. (`prev-*` breadcrumb tags are still written pending conflict-resolution refactor.) **Ghost-sibling lookup** (when a different asset already owns the proposed source's externalId) now queries `AssetSource` by `(sourceKind, externalId)` instead of by `assetTag` — the ghost's non-empty fields are absorbed and the ghost is deleted so the unique-constraint upsert lands cleanly. 403 if caller's role doesn't cover this conflict's entityType.
- `POST   /conflicts/:id/reject`                — Reservation: keep existing, dismiss. Asset: create a separate new Asset for the Entra/AD snapshot, then upsert its `AssetSource` row (`sourceKind` = `entra`/`ad`, `externalId` = `proposedDeviceId`) so the next discovery run finds the new asset by source and doesn't re-fire the collision.
- `POST   /conflicts/:id/merge`                 — **Asset conflicts only.** Per-field merge with operator-chosen winners. Body: `{ fieldWinners: { hostname?: "existing"|"proposed", serialNumber?, macAddress?, manufacturer?, model?, os?, osVersion?, assignedTo? } }`. Fields not present in `fieldWinners` fall back to the default accept logic (blank-fill for serial/mac/manufacturer/model/assignedTo, always-overwrite for os/osVersion, NetBIOS-upgrade rule for hostname). AssetSource stamping and ghost-asset absorption are unconditional regardless of selections. Reservation conflicts return 400 — they use the regular accept path. Audit Event message appends the selection map when used.

**Asset-conflict flavours.** `proposedAssetFields.collisionReason` distinguishes the pathways that raise an asset conflict. The two discovery-sync collision flavours, in decreasing order of confidence:
- `"untagged-collision"` — incoming Entra/AD/vCenter device's hostname matches an existing asset that has no source tag (DHCP-discovered, manually created, etc.). vCenter raises this flavour for both VMs and ESXi hosts (`proposedAssetFields.sourceType="vcenter"`, `assetType` discriminating VM vs host).
- `"duplicate-registration"` — incoming hostname matches an existing asset already tagged by the same source with a *different* deviceId/objectGUID (Entra returned two distinct deviceIds for the same display name — re-enrol, re-image, dual-boot — or AD has two `objectGUID`s for what looks like the same physical computer). Accepting re-keys the existing asset's source row to the incoming externalId (the prior identity is captured in the auto-resolve syncLog Event for audit).

A `bothAssetsExist: true` flag on `proposedAssetFields` marks the **sibling** sub-case of `"untagged-collision"`: the incoming device *already* has its own Polaris asset, and a second, un-linked asset shares its hostname. Raised by the Entra and vCenter (VM + host) sibling checks. It exists to route duplicate-asset cleanup through the Conflicts queue (Apply merge) rather than the asset-details Sources → Merge search. Accept runs the normal ghost-absorb (collision-target survives, the source-owning duplicate is absorbed + deleted); reject creates nothing — `rejectAssetConflict` short-circuits when the proposed `(sourceKind, externalId)` already owns an asset.

**The absorb preserves the duplicate's provenance.** The ghost here is a real multi-source asset, not a placeholder — it routinely holds discovery sources the collision target knows nothing about. So the absorb runs inside ONE transaction that calls the shared `absorbAssetRelations` (from `assetMergeService`) FIRST: every `AssetSource` row plus `AssetMacAddress` / `AssetAssociatedIp` / `AssetIpHistory` / `AssetFortigateSighting` (delete-on-conflict, survivor's row wins) and the `ManagedAgent` enrollment when the survivor has none are re-bound onto the survivor, *then* the merged field update is applied and *then* the ghost is deleted — so the delete cascade can no longer take them. `resolveMonitoringCarry` OR-s `monitored` across the two rows the same way the operator merge does (adopting the ghost's polling methods / credentials / MIB pins / cadences and unioning its pin arrays when the flip turns the survivor ON, resetting monitor state, recomputing `monitorOverride`, business rule 10 respected), and the blank-fill absorb covers `ipAddress` / `dnsName` / `learnedLocation` / `snmpLocation` / `learnedAddress` / `department` / `location` / `purchaseOrder` / `acquiredAt` / `warrantyExpiry` / `assetType` (only from `"other"`) on top of the original serial/MAC/manufacturer/model/assignedTo/notes set, keeps the more-recent `lastSeen` through `bumpLastSeen` (rule 12 still applies to the absorbed evidence), and unions the ghost's tags. *Before this fix the ghost delete cascaded its `AssetSource` rows*: merging an AD-only target with a ghost carrying entra + intune + fortigate-endpoint + vcenter-vm left the survivor holding only `ad` plus a thin `vcenter-vm` row re-created from the conflict snapshot — the UI promised the assets would be "combined" while three sources' provenance was destroyed. The `conflict.accepted` Event now itemizes what was carried over. Whatever is NOT re-bound still cascades with the ghost (LLDP / wireless / interface overrides / dependency edges / its own pending conflicts) and its sample hypertable rows orphan and age out — identical to the operator merge. The events.js card swaps in duplicate-asset copy + a "Duplicate assets" badge.

A third flavour is not a collision between assets but between an operator pin and discovery:
- `"ip-override"` — a discovery write staged an IP that differs from the asset's operator IP pin (`Asset.ipOverride`); raised by `ipOverrideService` after the db.ts guard re-asserted the pin. Carries `proposedAssetFields = { collisionReason, ipAddress: <discovered>, ipSource, overrideIp, hostname }` and no `proposedDeviceId` / AssetSource identity. One pending conflict per asset (refreshed while open; a rejected row suppresses re-raising the same discovered IP). Accept adopts the discovered IP + releases the pin (`ipAddress`+`ipOverride`+`ipSource` in one write so the guard defers); reject keeps the pin, event-only. `/merge` on this flavour degenerates to accept. Renders as a single-row Accept/Reject card in events.js (no per-field picker).

`proposedAssetFields.matchedVia` indicates the matching mechanism: `"exact"` (full hostname equality) or `"netbios"` (matched only after truncating one side to 15 chars). NetBIOS-truncation matching pairs an AD `cn`-derived 15-char hostname with the full Entra `displayName` and vice versa, so neither side missing the FQDN-aware rename causes a phantom split.

**Note:** The legacy `"mac-collision"` flavour (Entra-only, raised when the incoming Intune Ethernet MAC matched a MAC ever recorded on another asset) was retired — the Entra sync now treats Ethernet MAC as a positive identity-match signal and silently cross-links, the same way SID does for hybrid-joined devices. See "Hybrid-join cross-link" below for the cascade. Existing `mac-collision` conflict rows in production databases keep rendering through the events.js compatibility branch; no new ones are created.

### Search — `requireAuth`
- `GET    /search?q=<query>`                    — Global typeahead. Classifies input (IP, CIDR, MAC, or text), runs parallel entity queries, returns grouped results (`blocks`, `subnets`, `reservations`, `assets`, `ips`, `sites`) capped at 8 per group. **Multi-term matching**: the (post-scope-strip) query is tokenized by `parseSearchTerms` on whitespace, with double-quoted runs kept whole (`"rogers group" metro` → `["rogers group", "metro"]`, dangling-quote-tolerant); the terms are **AND-combined** so every term must match at least one searched column/pathway for a row to surface (per entity: an `AND: [{ OR: [cols…] }, …]` clause). IP / CIDR / MAC classification (plus the exact-match boosts + MAC normalization) only applies when the operator typed exactly **one** term — a multi-term query is always a plain "match all of these" text search. A single term collapses the AND to one element, preserving pre-multi-term behavior exactly. In `runAssetSearch` the JSON-blob raw scan AND-combines each term's ILIKE within a single blob (first + last name must both appear in the same `associatedUsers` / `observed` value); the side-table pathways (`AssetSource.externalId`, `AssetMacAddress.mac`, `AssetAssociatedIp.ip`, `AssetIpHistory.ip`) likewise require all terms in their single field, so cross-pathway AND (term A in hostname, term B in a side-table MAC) is not matched by design. **Asset search reach** spans direct Asset columns (`hostname` / `dnsName` / `assetTag` / `serialNumber` / `ipAddress` / `manufacturer` / `model` / `macAddress` / `assignedTo` / `department`), plus five parallel cross-search pathways merged into the same 8-row budget: `AssetSource.externalId` (Entra deviceId / AD objectGUID / FortiGate serial — accepts the `entra:` / `ad:` / `fgt:` / `intune:` / `fortiswitch:` / `fortiap:` prefix and strips it), `AssetMacAddress.mac` (full MAC history beyond the primary), `AssetAssociatedIp.ip` (secondary interface IPs the asset holds now), `AssetIpHistory.ip` (every IP the asset has held over time — incl. public WAN / since-rotated addresses), and a JSON-blob substring scan over `Asset.associatedUsers` + `AssetSource.observed` (logged-in users, on-prem SID, UPN, `onPremisesSecurityIdentifier`, etc.). The JSON scan is backed by GIN trigram indexes on both columns (migration `20260507200000_search_json_trgm_indexes`); queries shorter than 3 chars fall back to seq scans, but the 2-char minimum at `searchAll` keeps result sets tiny in that range. `sites` carries firewall assets that have lat/lng coordinates (i.e. pinned on the Device Map); these are queried separately with their own 8-row budget so the Device Map section always has a slot regardless of how many endpoints match. Pinned firewalls also ride along in `assets` (no SQL-level exclusion — `searchAssets` passes an empty baseFilter to `runAssetSearch`) so a search like "HARRIMAN-61F-1" shows the FortiGate in BOTH the Device Map section AND the Assets section; operators expecting to find the firewall under Assets find it there, while the dedicated Device Map slot guarantees a pan-to-marker entry point. The frontend dropdown labels the `sites` group "Device Map" and pan-to-marker on click via `window.polarisMapPanToAsset` (or navigates to `/map.html#site=<id>` from other pages). The `ips` hit resolves the containing subnet and any active reservation. **Scope-prefix shortcuts**: a query starting with `block:` / `b:`, `network:` / `n:`, `asset:` / `a:`, `reservation:` / `r:`, or `map:` / `m:` (case-insensitive, whitespace-tolerant) constrains the search to that one group AND lifts the per-group cap from 8 to `SCOPED_LIMIT=200`. Other groups return empty arrays in the scoped path. Min query length drops to 1 char after the prefix so `block:f` works. `results.query` echoes the original raw input (prefix included) for the desktop dropdown's stale-response check. Both surfaces show a hint panel when the search input is focused with no query yet: desktop `_showSearchShortcutHints` in `public/js/app.js` renders inline rows in the search dropdown; mobile `renderSearchEmpty` in `public/js/mobile/tabs.js` renders a 2×2 MD3 chip grid on the Search tab body (tapping the input from any tab routes to /search so the chips are visible before typing). **Page-aware section ordering**: when the operator is on `/map.html` the Device Map section is hoisted to the top of the dropdown; same logic for `/subnets.html` (Networks), `/assets.html` (Assets), `/blocks.html` (Blocks). **Per-group permission filtering**: each result group is gated on the read access of the function that owns it (`blocks`→ipBlocks, `subnets`→subnets, `reservations`→reservations, `assets`→assets, `sites`→deviceMap; `ips` needs subnets AND reservations since resolveIp reveals both) — denied groups come back empty and their query helpers never run, in both the scoped and unscoped paths (`searchAll(rawQuery, allowed?)`, default all-allowed). Bearer tokens have no role snapshot → every group empty. Covered by `tests/integration/permissionGates.test.ts`. Front-end edit modals render in view-only mode for users without write permission. **Monitor Status pill on asset/site hits**: `asset` and `site` hits carry `status: { kind, label }` — the same five-state monitor pill as the assets-table Status column (Unmonitored / Up / Warning / Down / Recovering / Pending, plus the Dependency Test and Dep. Down overlays, same precedence), computed server-side by `assetMonitorPillState` in `searchService.ts` (unit-tested in `tests/unit/assetMonitorPillState.test.ts`). The desktop dropdown maps `kind` onto the existing `.badge-monitor-*` classes and renders the pill after the hit title (`.gs-item-pill` shrinks it to dropdown scale).

### Device Map — `requireAuth` (topology-layout writes escalate to `deviceMap=write`)
- `GET    /map/sites`                           — Every firewall Asset with non-null lat/lng. Includes subnet count (via `Subnet.fortigateDevice` match), last-seen status, and a monitor health snapshot: `monitored`, `monitorHealth` (`"up" | "degraded" | "down" | "unknown"`, `null` when unmonitored), `monitorRecentSamples`, `monitorRecentFailures`. **Health is derived from `Asset.monitorStatus`** via `monitorStatusToHealth` (up→up, warning/recovering→degraded, down→down) so the Status Map's red "down" dots agree with the Down Assets / Status Summary widgets, which key off the same five-state machine; the recent-10-sample counts ride along only for the tooltip's "X/Y samples failed" detail (no longer the dot color). The Status Map frontend additionally renders any `dependencySuppressed` site as the distinct "dep" color (never red) — matching Down Assets' default exclusion of suppressed assets (that widget can be toggled to include them, but badges them rather than counting them as independent outages) — and any `status="maintenance"` site as the purple "maint" color (checked before everything else in `healthKey`; a maintenance window freezes `monitorStatus`, so a frozen "down" must not paint red, pulse, or count as an issue for the issues-only filter). Sidebar page entry: "Device Map" (below Dashboard).
- `GET    /map/sites/:id/topology/search?q=<query>` — Site-scoped endpoint search powering the topology modal's search box. Matches `q` as case-insensitive substring against `hostname` / `ipAddress` / `macAddress` / `assignedTo` / `dnsName`, scoped to endpoints whose `lastSeenSwitch` references one of THIS site's FortiSwitches. Returns up to 25 results: `{ id, hostname, ipAddress, macAddress, assetType, assignedTo, switchId, switchHostname, port, lastSeen }`. The frontend pulses the matching switch on the Cytoscape graph and navigates to the endpoint's asset details on click.
- `GET    /map/sites/:id/topology`              — Graph payload for the click-through modal. Returns `{ fortigate, switches[], aps[], subnets[], edges[], interfaceEdges[], lldpNodes[], remoteAssetNodes[], lldpEdges[] }`. Each entry in `switches[]` carries `endpointCount` (total endpoints learned on the switch's ports via Phase 7.5 of FMG/FortiGate discovery) and `endpoints[]` — top-25 by recency, each `{ id, hostname, ipAddress, macAddress, assetType, assignedTo, port, lastSeen }`. The right-hand info panel renders these as a collapsible "Endpoints (N)" section nested under each switch with click-through to asset details. The full set is reachable via the search endpoint above. The `fortigate` object carries the same `monitored` / `monitorHealth` / `monitorRecentSamples` / `monitorRecentFailures` fields as `/map/sites` so the modal's root node color matches the pin. Every edge id references a node in the same payload. FortiGate→Switch edges are derived from `Asset.fortinetTopology.uplinkInterface` (the FortiLink interface from `managed-switch/status.fgt_peer_intf_name`). AP→Switch edges come from the AP's own LLDP table (authoritative) or `switch-controller/detected-device` MAC learnings matched against AP base_mac during discovery; APs with no peer switch fall back to a direct FortiGate→AP edge. **Mesh/bridge handling:** a wireless-mesh leaf (`fortinetTopology.meshUplink === "mesh"`) never gets a switch→AP edge — even when stale data stamped a `parentSwitch`, that switch is bridged BEHIND the AP — and any AP↔switch LLDP adjacency involving a mesh-leaf AP (or a switch that isn't the AP's controller parent) is emitted as a `bridgeEdges[]` entry (AP→switch); the client renders it mesh-style, routes the switch behind the AP, and demotes the switch's FortiLink controller edge. **FortiLink fallback edges are dropped when redundant:** FortiOS stamps `fgt_peer_intf_name = "fortilink"` on every managed switch (direct or chained), so an unverified FG→switch controller edge represents the fortilink software aggregate, not a cable — the endpoint's final pass BFSes the assembled graph (controller + interface + LLDP + bridge + MCLAG edges) from the FortiGate with the unverified fallbacks removed, and drops each fallback whose switch is still reachable without it; a switch with no other path keeps its fallback so it never renders orphaned (`verifiedUplink` edges are never dropped). **Inter-switch aggregate links expand to one edge per physical member:** FortiOS reports an LACP/ISL bundle between two managed FortiSwitches as a single aggregate interface (usually the opaque serial-named auto-ISL trunk, e.g. `2DPTD21002999-0`), so the map would otherwise draw one edge labeled with the meaningless aggregate name. Instead, each in-site switch↔switch interface edge is expanded: both sides are resolved to their physical member ports and one edge is drawn per member, pairing the two sides by natural port order — so a 2-member bundle renders as **two** lines (`port11 ↔ port24`, `port12 ↔ port25`), a single physical link stays one, and the aggregate name never shows. Member ports come from two sources, per side in priority order: **LLDP local ports** (each switch advertises its OWN physical port in its neighbor rows — reliable even when the CMDB trunk membership hasn't been scraped) then the CMDB trunk membership via `physicalByParent`/`membersOf` (the `ifParent` linkage back-filled by `overlayFortiswitchTrunkMembers` from the managed-switch CMDB). Only pairs that already have an interface-inferred edge are expanded (LLDP only enriches — it never invents a link); MCLAG pairs are excluded (rendered as the single sibling `mclagEdge`). A side that resolves to nothing degrades to the raw interface name (best effort). Non-switch inter-edges (switch↔cross-site remote) still get single-member aggregate names swapped via `preferPhysicalMember`. FortiSwitch and FortiAP nodes use the same monitor-health color scheme as the FortiGate node — green/amber/red/gray driven by `Asset.monitorStatus` (translated via `monitorStatusToHealth` to the three-state `MonitorHealth` shape). Unmonitored switches/APs render gray. The controller probe path (`probeFortinetController`) maintains `monitorStatus` on these assets via the parent FortiGate's managed-switch/managed-AP inventory. **`interfaceEdges`** carries CMDB-inferred peer links from FortiOS interface naming conventions, computed by `interfaceTopologyService.inferInterfaceTopology` against the latest `AssetInterfaceSample` per (assetId, ifName) for every site asset: aggregate names that encode a peer's serial fragment (auto-stamped FortiLink — e.g. `8FFTV23025884-0` ↔ `S108FFTV23025884`) AND operator-named hostname aggregates (custom MCLAG between non-stacked pairs — e.g. `METROR2-T1024E`). Each entry: `{ source, target, sourceIfName, label, via: "interface", matchVia: "serial" | "hostname" }`. Cross-site peers matched via this pathway are added to `remoteAssetNodes` alongside LLDP-matched cross-site assets. Authoritative — duplicates against `edges` (controller-derived) are dropped, and the LLDP dedupe set is seeded with `interfaceEdges` so a peer link confirmed by both signals only renders once. Rendered as solid teal lines (distinct from the muted gray controller-data edges and the dashed orange LLDP edges). **`lldpNodes` / `remoteAssetNodes` / `lldpEdges`** carry LLDP-derived topology that fortinetTopology can't see: every `AssetLldpNeighbor` row whose `assetId` is the FortiGate or any of its sibling switches/APs is examined, neighbors that resolve back to a sibling are skipped (the authoritative FortiLink/MAC edge already covers them), **neighbors matched to a Polaris asset OUTSIDE this site** are surfaced into `remoteAssetNodes` (separate from ghost LLDP nodes — they're real assets, just at another site; rendered with a solid blue border and a tap-handler that pivots to the asset details page), and unmatched neighbors get a synthesized **ghost** node in `lldpNodes` keyed on chassisId so multi-link aggregates collapse to one. Each LLDP edge carries `targetLabel` (hostname/IP/chassisId for the right-hand info panel) and `targetIsAsset` (true → the link in the panel pivots to the asset details page). The cytoscape graph styles LLDP edges as dashed orange lines, ghost nodes with a dashed orange border, and remote-asset nodes with a solid blue border — distinguishing observed-via-LLDP links from authoritative controller data and "real asset elsewhere" from "non-Polaris device." **Location codes per node:** every `fortigate` / `switches[]` / `aps[]` entry carries `location: { area, building, floor, room, junctionBox } | null` (resolved server-side by `utils/locationCodes.ts`: the `Asset.description`'s codes when it carries any, exclusively; else the device admin description discovery stamped on `fortinetTopology.deviceDescription` — notes are never a source) plus the raw `deviceDescription` (switches/aps). The FortiGate resolves from the description only (no device capture — its device surface would be the 35-char system/global alias). These drive the frontend's grouping hulls (nested rounded rectangles color-coded per level — area rose > building sky-blue > floor violet dashed > room green > jb amber dashed, fitted inside-out so outer shapes grow to enclose inner ones, plus a sibling-separation sweep that pushes non-nested shapes apart so no two ever overlap; drawn as synthetic bottom-layer Cytoscape nodes so `cy.png()` screenshots include them; "Locations" chip toggle at `localStorage["polaris.topology.showLocations"]`, rendered only when codes exist), the solver's same-building/floor row clustering, and the **location views**: when any device carries `b:` or `f:`, a top-left two-row drill-down switcher offers Flat (default, never persisted) + one chip per building (area-prefixed label; clicking selects the whole-building view, and the active building's "All" + floor chips appear in a second row — buildings without floors get no second row) — a building view shows ALL of that building's tagged devices, a floor view just that floor's, both + the FortiGate root, with dashed **portal** stubs where a member's edge crosses to another view (label `→ <view>: <device>`; tap jumps there; untagged devices appear only in Flat; keys are area-scoped `b|<a>|<b>` / `f|<a>|<b>|<f>`; `computeFloorViews` / `partitionElementsForFloor` in topology-render.js). **Right-click description editor:** cxttap on any asset-backed node (firewall / switch / AP / endpoint / matched wireless station / remote asset — not portals, hulls, or LLDP ghosts) opens a small modal editing `Asset.description` in place, pre-filled with the current value and showing the `a:`/`b:`/`f:`/`r:`/`jb:` grouping-shortcut syntax; Save goes through the normal `PUT /assets/:id` pathway (description sync to the device applies when the integration has it on) then silently refreshes the topology so hulls / clustering / the view switcher pick up re-resolved codes. Gated client-side on `assets≥write` (`canManageAssets`). **Node positions are persisted per site AND per view, server-first**: the payload embeds `savedLayouts: { [view]: { view, positions, updatedBy, updatedAt } }` (the `TopologyLayout` rows — the shared hand-tuned map every operator sees); the client prefers those, falling back to the per-browser `localStorage` layout (Flat keeps the legacy bare `polaris.topology.positions:<siteId>` key, floor views append `:<viewKey>`), then the solver default. Drags always write localStorage; `deviceMap=write` callers additionally PUT the blob server-side (debounced ~1s per (site, view), only after a real drag/snap gesture — open/close/refresh alone never PUTs). A **Snap** chip (per-user `localStorage["polaris.topology.snapToGrid"]`, default off) lands drag releases — including hull-drag member moves and multi-select drags — on the column solver's 130×95px lattice; enabling it re-snaps every current position (and, for writers, arithmetically snaps the other views' saved blobs). A **Reset Layout** button in the modal toolbar (between Refresh and Fullscreen) drops the saved positions for the current site's ACTIVE view — localStorage plus (for writers) the server row via the DELETE endpoint — and re-runs the layout against the cached topology data; a non-writer facing a shared server layout gets a toast explaining the reset needs Device Map write.
- `PUT    /map/sites/:id/topology/layout`       *(deviceMap=write)* — Full-replace save of one (site, view) shared layout. Body `{ view: "flat" | "b|…" | "f|…", positions: { [nodeId]: {x,y} } }` (Zod + `sanitizePositions` service re-validation: finite coords, |coord| ≤ 1e7, ≤3000 nodes). 404 unless `:id` is a firewall asset. Returns the saved `{ view, positions, updatedBy, updatedAt }`. Writes a `map.topology.layout_saved` Event (view + nodeCount).
- `DELETE /map/sites/:id/topology/layout?view=<key>` *(deviceMap=write)* — Remove one (site, view) layout (the server half of Reset Layout). 400 on missing/invalid view; idempotent 204 (the Event `map.topology.layout_reset` only fires when a row actually existed).

### Application Map (`src/api/routes/applicationMap.ts`, mounted at `/application-map`)

- `GET    /application-map`               *(applicationMap=read)* — The full connectivity graph for appmap.html: `{ generatedAt, nodes[], edges[], savedLayout, stats }` from `applicationMapService.buildApplicationMapGraph()`. Nodes: compound asset parents (**`monitored: true` mapped hosts only** — a stop-monitored / decommissioned / disabled asset drops off the map without losing its pins; with deviceIcon iconUrl), process children (from `Asset.mappedProcesses`, `proc:` id, with listenPorts) AND service children (from `Asset.mappedServices`, `svc:` id — connection rows attributed by their owning `unit`; both child kinds render even with zero connections since they come from the mapped list, not the rows), grey unknown-ip / unknown-ip-group (/24-grouped) / unknown-overflow nodes (resolved-target assets that are only edge endpoints are added regardless of the monitored filter). Edges: one per (source, target) with a per-port breakdown (cap 16 + portOverflow), kind ∈ process | asset | external | external-inbound (child-to-child edges — process↔service alike — are kind `process`). `stats` carries `processCount` + `serviceCount`, and `retentionDays` reports the configured `appMapConnections` retention window (FOREVER = -1) — the client builds its "Seen within" option list from it so the widest option states the real window instead of the old unqualified "All retained", which always meant 7 days regardless of what was kept. Query bounded server-side by that SAME window, so the read and the prune can't disagree.
- `PUT    /application-map/layout`        *(applicationMap=write)* — Full-replace save of the shared drag layout. Body `{ view: "global", positions }` (Zod + the shared `sanitizePositions`). Audited `application_map.layout.saved`.
- `DELETE /application-map/layout?view=global` *(applicationMap=write)* — Reset the shared layout (idempotent 204; Event `application_map.layout.reset` only when a row existed).
- `GET    /application-map/discovery`     *(applicationMap=read)* — The stored discovery-rule set (list UI on Integrations → Polaris Agent) plus the asset types a rule can target and hostname labels for explicit targets: `{version:2, rules[], assetLabels{assetId→hostname}, processCapableAssetTypes[]}`. The client constrains its asset-type picker from that list rather than keeping a second copy of the constant in sync; `assetLabels` lets the list render an auto rule's Devices cell without per-rule round-trips.
- `POST   /application-map/discovery/scope-preview` *(applicationMap=read)* — Body `{ scope, assetIds? }` → `{ total, assets[≤100] }` of monitored assets the scope ∪ explicit assetIds selects (null scope + assetIds = just those assets, matching apply). Backs the wizard's device step so the operator can confirm they picked the hosts they meant before choosing items.
- `POST   /application-map/discovery/inventory` *(applicationMap=read)* — Body `{ scope }` → `{ processes[], services[] }` reported by the assets that scope selects (each row `{ name, deviceCount, mappedCount }`, services adding `platform`/`displayName`). This is what makes the picker granular: it lists what THOSE hosts run, not the whole fleet's inventory. Client-side filtering isn't possible — aggregate rows carry no asset ids.
- `POST   /application-map/discovery/preview` *(applicationMap=read)* — Body `{ rule }` → `{ deviceCount, processPins, servicePins, monitorPins, sampleDevices[≤10] }` counting only what the rule would ADD (a monitor-mode rule adds only monitorPins). Read-gated because it only reports.
- `PUT    /application-map/discovery`     *(applicationMap=write **AND** assets=write)* — Full-replace save of the rule set (the whole config, since cross-rule name/id uniqueness can't be validated per-rule), then applies it inline so pins land immediately; the 30-min `reconcileAppMapAutoMap` tick covers assets discovered later. Both gates are chained because the write changes per-asset pin arrays, the same fields the assets PUT guards. Returns `{ version, rules, assetLabels, applied }`. Events `application_map.automap.saved` + (when anything was pinned) `application_map.automap.applied`. (AUTO rules are additionally written outside this PUT by the assets-PUT pin hook — `recordOperatorPinChanges`, Event `application_map.autorule.synced`.)
- `POST   /application-map/discovery/unmap` *(applicationMap=write **AND** assets=write)* — The only subtractive path (apply is strictly additive by design). Body `{ kind: "process"|"service", name }` → strips the pin from every asset, deletes its `AssetProcessConnection` rows, removes the name from every map-mode rule (monitor-only rules keep theirs), and prunes auto rules the removal emptied. Returns `{ devices, connectionRowsDeleted }`; Event `application_map.automap.unmapped`.

### Weather — `requireAuth` (main router) / prefix-allowlisted on the Dash listener
Status Map weather proxy (see `weatherProxyService.ts`). The widget tries these first and falls back to fetching RainViewer / Open-Meteo directly on failure — so failures here degrade the transport, never the overlay. On the Dash listener these paths ride a dedicated generous rate limiter (`dashWeatherLimiter`, 4000/5min — one radar refresh is hundreds of small tile GETs and would exhaust the wallboard's general 600/5min budget in a single load).
- `GET    /weather/frames`                      — RainViewer radar frame list: `{ frames: [{ id, time }] }` (id = the content-hash path segment; time = unix seconds). 5 min server-side cache with serve-stale ≤30 min on upstream failure.
- `GET    /weather/radar/:frame/:z/:x/:y`       — One radar tile PNG (256px, color scheme 6, "1_1" render options — matches the widget's direct-CDN template). Immutable per frame id → served with `Cache-Control: public, max-age=86400, immutable` (deliberately overriding the Dash listener's blanket no-store). 400 out-of-range z/x/y, 404 unknown frame (client refreshes the frame list), 502 upstream failure.
- `GET    /weather/temp?lat=&lng=`              — Current temperature (°F): `{ temperature: number | null }`. Cached per 1.5° grid cell (the widget's own rounding), 20 min TTL. 502 on upstream transport failure → the widget falls back to Open-Meteo directly for that cell.

### Map Regions — `requireNetworkAdmin` (admin + networkadmin only)
Operator-drawn polygons that auto-tag enclosed FortiGates and their managed FortiSwitches / FortiAPs with `region:<name>`. **Subnet propagation** (in `computeMembership`, which returns `{assetIds, subnetIds}`): beyond the enclosed firewalls and their controller-managed switches/APs, the `Subnet` rows an enclosed firewall serves (`Subnet.fortigateDevice` matching any of that gate's `controllerIdentityKeys` — serial, FMG device name, hostname) inherit the region **themselves**, and so does any asset whose primary IP falls inside one — this is how coordinate-less assets (servers, workstations, standalone devices) get a region tag from the firewall that fronts their subnet (IPv4 only; IPv6 assets are skipped), and how the IPAM Networks list (whose **Sources** column IS `fortigateDevice`) becomes filterable by region. Subnet tags follow the identical provenance-bounded contract, and `ReconcileSummary` counts them separately (`subnetsAdded` / `subnetsRemoved` / `subnetsTouched` alongside the asset counters), so a region edit that touched only networks still writes its Event. Persisted as a single JSON blob in `Setting` keyed `mapRegions` (allocationTemplateService pattern). The reconciler **re-evaluates membership in both directions**, bounded by the `RegionTagAssignment` provenance table (the `TagAutoAssignment` pattern, keyed by region id + a targetType because subnets are targets too): every add records the pair, and the strip half (`diffRegionMembership`) removes the tag only from recorded pairs that no longer belong — so devices that MOVE (a re-pinned gate, a switch repointed to another controller, a subnet re-served by a different gate) shed their old region on the next reconcile, while manual operator attachments (hand-tagging an endpoint server with `region:Atlanta`) and tags predating provenance survive across runs. Manually *removing* the tag from an in-polygon asset will be re-added on the next reconcile — that direction is authoritative by design so polygon membership always implies the tag. Add-then-record ordering makes a crash between the two err toward "operator-owned" rather than toward stripping a tag we never wrote. Region creation upserts a `Tag` registry row at `region:<name>` under category "Map Regions" so it shows up in the asset edit modal's tag picker; rename rotates the registry row (provenance survives — it's keyed by region id); delete removes it and clears the region's provenance. The reconciler runs at three points: inline (await) on every CRUD endpoint, end-of-`syncDhcpSubnets` Phase 13 in `mode in {"full","finalize"}`, and a 6-hour periodic job (`reconcileMapRegions.ts`). Polygon-only edits (drag a vertex without renaming) now re-evaluate like every other pass — targets the smaller polygon no longer covers are stripped where provenance permits. One failing region is logged and skipped rather than aborting the pass. Read access also requires admin/networkadmin since regions are only rendered while editing.
- `GET    /map/regions`                         — List every region: `{ id, name, polygon: [[lat,lng],...], createdBy, createdAt, updatedAt }`. Sorted by name.
- `POST   /map/regions`                         — Create. Body: `{ name (1..64 chars, unique case-insensitive, no control chars), polygon ([[lat,lng],...] with ≥3 and ≤1000 vertices, lat in [-90,90], lng in [-180,180]) }`. Returns the created region. Reconciles inline. Writes `region.created` + (when something was tagged) `region.tags_reconciled` Events.
- `PUT    /map/regions/:id`                     — Update. Body: `{ name?, polygon? }`. Same validation. **Rename path:** strips `region:<oldName>` from every asset that carries it, then add-passes `region:<newName>` to current membership. **Polygon-only edit path:** add-pass only — assets that drifted out of the polygon keep the tag. Returns the updated region. Writes `region.updated` Event with `previousName` for audit.
- `DELETE /map/regions/:id`                     — Delete. Strips `region:<name>` from every asset that carries it and removes the `Tag` registry row. Returns 204. Writes `region.deleted` Event.

### Allocation Templates — mixed scoping
- `GET    /allocation-templates`                *(auth)* — List saved multi-subnet templates used by the Networks "Auto-Allocate Next" modal.
- `POST   /allocation-templates`                *(networkadmin)* — Create a template. Body: `{ name, entries: [{name, prefixLength, vlan?} | {skip: true, prefixLength}] }`.
- `PUT    /allocation-templates/:id`            *(networkadmin)* — Update a template.
- `DELETE /allocation-templates/:id`            *(networkadmin)* — Delete a template.

### Server Settings — `serverSettingsSystem` read floor + per-route escalations
Mounted behind `requirePermission("serverSettingsSystem", "read")` (router.ts). Mutating routes additionally escalate per-route: system-card writes (tags, NTP/DNS incl. their `/test` probes, certificates, OUI refresh/overrides, sample-retention, capacity-advisor stage, agent-event-log, branding, and the whole `/agents/*` build/upgrade/prune/server-url/cert-pins group) require `serverSettingsSystem=fullwrite`; data-surface writes (`/database/backup`, `/database/restore`, backup delete, `/database/backup-schedule` PUT, `/queue-mode`, `/security-tokens/generate`, `/restart`, `/updates/apply|dismiss|settings`) require `serverSettingsData=fullwrite`, and the backup **download** (the full DB dump) requires `serverSettingsData=read`. `POST /tags/preview-criteria` is the one deliberately mount-level route (stateless dry-run). A Data-scoped role still needs `serverSettingsSystem=read` to reach its routes through the mount.
- `GET    /server-settings`
- `PUT    /server-settings`
- `GET    /server-settings/branding`            — Public; used by login page. `{ appName, subtitle, logoUrl, logoAccent, logoOnLogin, logoOnSidebar, temperatureUnit, customLogo, version }`. `appName` may be `""` (an operator whose logo carries their wordmark blanks it — `displayAppName` is the fallback for surfaces that must print one); `customLogo` is derived (`hasCustomLogo`) so the frontends never compare logo paths. `PUT` accepts the three flags (each falling back to the stored value per field, so a caller that omits one can't clear it); `POST|DELETE /branding/logo` carry them forward unchanged — placement is inert while the default logo is in play, and an operator who re-uploads gets their choices back verbatim.
- `GET    /server-settings/branding/logo-accent.png` — **Public** (declared in `src/api/router.ts` above `requireAuth`, since the login page renders it with no session). The operator's logo with the Polaris symbol composited onto its bottom-right corner (`brandLogoService.renderAccentedLogo`). Takes `?theme=dark|light` — the symbol art is theme-paired, and the query is what makes the URL change on a theme flip so the `<img>` re-fetches. `Cache-Control: no-cache` + a strong ETag over the source mtimes AND the theme → 304 on revalidation, which is what makes a fixed URL safe when the upload route reuses one filename. **302s to `branding.logoUrl`** when there's nothing to accent (flag off, default logo, unrenderable source) rather than 404-ing a live `<img>`.
- `POST   /server-settings/https`
- `POST   /server-settings/database/backup`   — Streams the dump to disk then to the client; body `{ password? }` (validated by `utils/backupPassword.ts`, absent = unencrypted).
- `POST   /server-settings/database/restore`  — Multipart upload. Timescale-aware: `timescaledb_pre_restore()` / restore / `timescaledb_post_restore()` in three separate psql sessions, post_restore in a `finally`.
- `GET|PUT /server-settings/database/backup-schedule` — Automatic-backup cadence (`backupSchedule` Setting).
- `GET    /server-settings/pg-tuning`           — Capacity + tuning health check. Returns `{ settings, pgConfigFile, capacity }`. `settings` is the per-`pg_settings` row shape `{ name, current, recommended, ok }` consumed by the Database card to render the inline current → recommended rows under a fired `pg_tuning_needed` capacity reason; empty array (with `pgConfigFile=null`) when row counts are below scale thresholds (`assets≥160` / `subnets≥1600` / `reservations≥160000`) — keeps small dev installs from being told to tune `shared_buffers`. `capacity: CapacitySnapshot` from `capacityService.getCapacitySnapshot()` exposes overall `severity` (`ok` | `watch` | `amber` | `red`), an array of `reasons` ({severity, code, message, suggestion}), `appHost.volumes[]` (per-filesystem free/total bytes + the Polaris-named roles each volume serves: `app`/`state`/`backups`/`db`; pre-deduped by stat.dev so single-LV installs collapse cleanly and STIG-style multi-LV layouts surface each filesystem once), `appHost.dbColocated` flag, `database.sampleTables[]` (rows, bytes, deadTupRatio, lastAutovacuum), `database.dataDirectory` (PostgreSQL `SHOW data_directory` when co-located), `workload.monitoredAssetCount`, `workload.monitoredInterfaceCount` (sum of `Asset.monitoredInterfaces` + `Asset.monitoredIpsecTunnels` array lengths across every monitored asset — IPsec tunnels are folded in as interfaces; the operator-pinned fast-poll subset), `workload.monitoredStorageCount` (sum of `Asset.monitoredStorage` array lengths), and `workload.steadyStateSizeBytes` — the projected DB size at current monitored-asset count × cadences × retention. Also exposes `database.connectionPool` (currentInUse, peakObserved, prismaPoolSize, pgbossPoolSize, maxConnections) for the Maintenance tab Database card and the `db_pool_undersized` watch reason, and `database.io` (trackIoTiming, measured, avgBackendsBlockedOnDisk, windowSeconds) — measured disk-read pressure driving the `db_io_pressure` / `track_io_timing_off` reasons. Severity tiering: **red** (disk free <10% on any volume, DB > 90% of free disk on its volume, autovacuum stale >7d on a populated **and bloated** non-Timescale sample table — bloat gate `deadTupRatio > 0.20` via `isStaleVacuumTable`, so a low-churn install with negligible dead tuples no longer trips this; projected size > 8× host RAM) drives the non-dismissible sidebar critical alert; **amber** (disk 10–20%, dead-tup >20%, projected > 4× RAM, `pg_tuning_needed`, sustained `db_io_pressure`) renders as a card-only reason row — there is no sidebar amber banner; **watch** (disk 20–30% on any volume, `db_io_pressure` building, `track_io_timing_off`) emits the transition Event but does NOT drive the navbar banner — gives ops a "you have weeks, not minutes" early warning that flows out through eventArchiveService → syslog/SFTP. The route handler also calls `recordCapacityTransition()` (best-effort; void) so a flip into a more severe state writes a `capacity.severity_changed` Event in real time the moment an admin loads the Maintenance tab.
- `GET    /server-settings/queue-mode`          — Returns `{ active, persisted, restartRequired, pgbossInstalled }`. `active` is what the running process is using (captured at boot); `persisted` is the current `Setting.monitor.queueMode` value (= what next restart will use). `restartRequired` is true when they differ. UI uses this for the "Pending: pg-boss on next restart" hint on the Maintenance tab Database card.
- `POST   /server-settings/queue-mode`          — Body `{ mode: "cursor" | "pgboss" }`. Writes `Setting.monitor.queueMode` and returns the same shape as GET. Called by the Capacity Advisor's Stage flow for the QUEUE_MODE lever; remains an explicit endpoint for tooling that wants to flip queue mode directly without going through the advisor. 409 if mode is "pgboss" but the package isn't installed in this build. Writes one `monitor.queue_mode.set` Event.
- `GET    /server-settings/capacity-advisor`    — Returns `{ advisor: AdvisorState, capacity: CapacitySnapshot, pgTuning: { settings, pgConfigFile } }` in a single round-trip. `advisor.recommendations` is the per-lever list (current vs recommended vs rationale + breakdown) consumed by the Maintenance-tab Capacity Advisor card. Computes via `getCapacitySnapshotWithAdvisor()` so the advisor-driven capacity reasons (`monitor_workers_undersized`, `max_connections_undersized`) appear in the embedded snapshot. Best-effort `recordCapacityTransition()` fires on every fetch.
- `POST   /server-settings/capacity-advisor/stage` — Body `{ keys: AdvisorLeverKey[] }` (non-empty). Recomputes the advisor fresh, then for each operator-selected key dispatches: `applyMode="env"` writes `setEnvVar(envName, recommended)` to `.env` (restart-required); `applyMode="queue-mode-endpoint"` calls `setQueueMode()` directly (same path as `POST /queue-mode`); `applyMode="advisory-only"` (PG_MAX_CONNECTIONS and PG_*) returns `status: "skipped"`. **Server picks values from a fresh recompute — never accepts arbitrary values from the client.** Returns `{ ok, results: [{ key, status, oldValue, newValue, reason? }], restartRequired }`. Writes one `capacity_advisor.staged` Event (info) listing applied keys + one `capacity_advisor.stage_failed` Event (warning) when any entry errored.
- `GET    /server-settings/sample-retention` — Returns `{ retention: SampleRetention }` from `getSampleRetention()`. Shape is `{stream: {tier: {class: days}}}` — 3 streams (sample / telemetry / systemInfo) × 3 tiers (detail / hourly / daily) × 3 classes (default / switch / accessPoint). Defaults 7/30/365 across the board on a fresh install.
- `PUT    /server-settings/sample-retention` — Body is a partial `SampleRetention` shape; missing keys inherit from the existing stored value (so the UI can PUT a single cell or the full grid). Validates each numeric to a non-negative integer; out-of-range or non-numeric values fall back to the existing stored value. Writes one `sample_retention.updated` Event. The cache is invalidated immediately; chart endpoints see the new values on the next request, the prune layer on the next daily tick.
- `GET    /server-settings/agent-event-log` — Returns `{ config: AgentEventLogConfig }` (`{enabled, minLevel, windowsChannels, linuxMinPriority, maxPerPush, perAssetHourlyCap}`) from `getAgentEventLogConfig()`. Default disabled. Drives the **Agent OS Event Log** card on the Retention tab.
- `PUT    /server-settings/agent-event-log` — Body is a partial config; `updateAgentEventLogConfig` clamps ranges + merges with the stored value. Writes one `agent_event_log.updated` Event. Delivered to agents on their next `GET /agents/config` poll (the filter is part of the config ETag) and applied server-side at `/samples` ingest.
- `POST   /server-settings/security-tokens/generate` — Body `{ which: "metrics" | "health" }`. Generates a 32-byte hex token, writes `METRICS_TOKEN` / `HEALTH_TOKEN` into the runtime `.env` via `setEnvVar` (in `src/utils/envFile.ts`), and stamps `process.env[KEY]` so the bearer-token gate on `/metrics` or `/health` takes effect immediately without a restart (both endpoints read the env var per-request). Driven by the [Generate token] button on the `metrics_token_unset` / `health_token_unset` capacity reasons. The raw token is never returned to the caller — operators read the value from `.env` if their monitoring system needs it. Writes one `server.security_token.generated` Event.
- `POST   /server-settings/restart` — Operator-triggered process restart. Responds `{ ok: true }` before calling `restartService()` from `updateService.ts` so the client sees a clean 200 and can switch to its restart-polling overlay. On Linux exits with code 1 so systemd's `Restart=on-failure` brings the process back; on Windows shells out to NSSM. Driven by the **Restart Polaris to apply** button on the Capacity Advisor card after the staging flow flips `_advisorJustStaged=true` and the recommendation list reaches zero outstanding levers. The frontend gates the click with `warnIfDiscoveryRunning("restart")` + a confirm dialog before posting. Writes one `server.restart.requested` Event (warning) with the actor's username.

Additional `/server-settings` sub-surfaces (all `requireAdmin` except branding GET which is public; see `src/api/routes/serverSettings.ts` for bodies):
- **Branding** — `PUT /branding`, `POST /branding/logo`, `DELETE /branding/logo` (alongside the public `GET /branding`).
- **HTTPS / certificates** — `GET|PUT /https`, `POST /https/apply`; `GET|POST /certificates`, `DELETE /certificates/:id`, `POST /certificates/generate`.
- **DNS** — `GET|PUT /dns`, `POST /dns/test`. **NTP** — `GET|PUT /ntp`, `POST /ntp/test`.
- **OUI** — `GET /oui`, `POST /oui/refresh`, `GET|POST /oui/overrides`, `DELETE /oui/overrides/:prefix`.
- **Tags** — `GET|POST /tags`, `PUT|DELETE /tags/:id`, `GET|PUT /tags/settings`.
- **Database backups** — `GET /database`, `GET /database/backups`, `DELETE /database/backups/:id`, `GET /database/backups/:id/download` (streamed, not buffered), `GET|PUT /database/backup-schedule` (the automatic-backup cadence — read carries the blanket `serverSettingsSystem` floor, PUT is `serverSettingsData=fullwrite` since it can schedule gigabytes of writes and holds a passphrase; the passphrase is masked on read and a masked echo preserves the stored value), alongside `POST /database/backup` + `/restore`. All of them are thin wrappers over `services/backupService.ts` / `services/backupScheduleService.ts`.
- **Software updates** — `GET /updates/check`, `GET /updates/status`, `POST /updates/apply`, `POST /updates/dismiss`, `GET|PUT /updates/settings`, `GET /updates/history`. `GET /updates/status` is polled from two places: the Application Updates card (every 2 s while an apply is in flight) AND the sidebar (every 5 s, admin-only) — the latter drives the `#update-status` in-progress panel in [public/js/app.js](public/js/app.js) (`renderUpdateStatus`), which mirrors the discovery indicator and shows just the currently-running step while `state ∈ {applying, restarting}` (the full per-step checklist stays on the Maintenance card). The sidebar poll keeps the last-known status on a failed fetch during the restart window so the panel doesn't flicker out. **Update train** (`update.train` Setting, default `nightly`, surfaced on `GET|PUT /updates/settings` alongside `skipBackup` and via the Maintenance-card dropdown): `nightly` tracks the update-branch tip (`origin/HEAD → main → master`, the historical behavior — `git pull --ff-only`); `release` tracks the highest release tag by version sort (`git tag --sort=-v:refname "v[0-9]*" "[0-9]*"`) and applies it via `git checkout --detach <tag>`. With no release tags published, `checkForUpdates` on the release train returns `up-to-date` + a `note`. Switching back to nightly from a detached release checkout returns HEAD to the default branch before pulling. Version/change computation is shared by `computeTargetInfo(ref)` for both trains.
- **Polaris Agent build/management** — `GET /agents/inventory`, `POST /agents/build`, `GET /agents/build/current`, `GET /agents/build/:buildId`, `DELETE /agents/build/:buildId`, `GET /agents/installed-summary`, `GET /agents/installed` (full per-host list — one row per ManagedAgent joined with a thin Asset slice: host/IP, os+arch, agentVersion, installStatus, lastSeenAt, `privilegeTier`, `caps` (decoded reportedCapEff; null = not reported), `outOfDate`, `hasInstallCredential`; backs the "Installed agents" slide-in on the Polaris Agents tab, whose per-host Reinstall/Upgrade/Remove buttons call the `/assets/:id/agent/*` routes, whose host cell is click-through to the asset details slide-in (in place when `openViewModal` is on the page, else the `#view=asset:<id>` deep link — the credential-usage slide-in's hand-off, which is why integrations.html needn't pull in assets.js), and whose **Privilege** column renders the VERIFIED state for ptrace-tier rows — "PTRACE + DAC_READ ✓" amber when the reported caps hold the pair, "stale, reinstall" red when the mask lacks CAP_DAC_READ_SEARCH (pre-DAC-fix unit, collects nothing), "unverified" amber when caps is null; legacy `root` danger, `unprivileged` plain, fixed LocalSystem / root-daemon text on Windows / macOS — alongside header counts of elevated + stale Linux agents), `POST /agents/upgrade-all`, `GET|PUT /agents/auto-build-setting`, `POST /agents/prune`, `GET|PUT /agents/server-url`. See `agentBuildService` + ARCHITECTURE.md → Monitoring Architecture (Polaris Agent in-app build).
- **Agent code signing (Azure Trusted Signing)** — `GET /agents/signing` (masked config + live availability probe), `PUT /agents/signing` (`serverSettingsSystem=fullwrite`; `clientSecret` follows the mask-echo-preserves-stored convention), `POST /agents/signing/test` (fullwrite; probes Java/jsign and mints a REAL Entra ID token — no jsign run). The sidebar-alert feed lives OUTSIDE this router at `GET /api/v1/assets/agent-signing-alert`, gated `assets:write` (the agent-deploy permission) so assetsadmin-style roles without `serverSettingsSystem` can see it. See `agentSigningService` + TOUCHES.md → cross-cutting/polaris-agent-build.

### Agents — runtime + install (mixed scoping)
Inbound agent-runtime routes mounted at `/agents` (see `src/api/routes/agents.ts`; full semantics in ARCHITECTURE.md → Monitoring Architecture):
- `POST /agents/enroll` *(public; one-shot enrollment token + cert-pin check)*, `POST /agents/samples` / `GET /agents/config` / `POST /agents/heartbeat` / `POST /agents/system-info` *(bearer via `requireAgentBearer`)*, `GET /agents/binary/:filename` *(public, cert-pinned download)*.
- Outbound WebSocket channel handled by `src/api/routes/agentsWs.ts` (bearer via `Sec-WebSocket-Protocol`).
- Operator-facing per-asset routes on `/assets/:id/agent`: `GET` *(any auth)*, `POST /install` / `POST /retry` / `POST /reinstall` / `POST /upgrade` *(assets-admin)*, `DELETE` *(admin; `?force=true` hard-deletes)*. `POST /reinstall` starts over from ANY status (vs `/retry`, which only resets a `failed` row): revokes the old bearer, resets to `pending`, and re-runs `startInstall` with the stored install credential (re-pushes binary + agent.conf, re-enrolls). Emits `agent.reinstall_kickoff`.
- `POST /assets/bulk-agent-install` *(assets ≥ write)* — bulk agent deploy from the assets-page bulk bar. Body `{ ids[] (≤200), sshCredentialId?, winrmCredentialId?, arch?, scriptIds? }` (at least one credential required; `scriptIds` = per-OS `{linux?,darwin?,windows?}` install-method variant, OS-locked + validated up front, applied per an asset's inferred platform). Delegates to `agentInstallService.bulkInstallAgents`: per-asset OS/transport resolved via `inferAgentPlatform` + `pickTransportAndCredential` (Windows → WinRM, SSH fallback; else SSH), run-level preconditions (TLS pin, callback URL, built binaries, credential types) checked once, ineligible assets (existing agent / hypervisor / Fortinet source / unreachable / no matching cred / no binary) returned as `skipped[]` with reasons. Creates `ManagedAgent` rows synchronously (immediate "pending"), then drains the remote installs through a bounded background pool. Returns `{ requested, kicked, skipped[] }`.
- `GET    /assets/agent-install-scripts` *(assets ≥ read)* — the curated install-method catalog (`agentInstallScripts.AGENT_INSTALL_SCRIPTS`) backing the deploy modal's OS-locked "Install method" picker. Returns `{ scripts: [{ id, osPlatform, label, description, isDefault }] }`. Registered BEFORE `GET /:id` so the literal path isn't captured as an asset id.

### MIB Database — mixed scoping
Reads (`list`, `get`, `download`, `facets`, `profile-status`, `structure`, and the MIB-aware `walk`) are open to **admin OR assets-admin** so the team that owns asset onboarding can use the MIB-aware browse + walk surface. Writes (`upload`, `delete`) stay **admin-only**.
