Routes live in `src/api/routes/mibs.ts` mounted at `/server-settings/mibs` *before* the rest of `/server-settings` so its per-route guards take precedence over the blanket `serverSettingsSystem` read gate on the rest of /server-settings. The same router carries three additional routes under `/std/` (`GET /std`, `GET /std/:key/structure`, `POST /std/:key/walk`) that expose the eleven bundled standard MIBs (System / IF-MIB / IF-MIB Extended / HOST-RESOURCES-MIB / ENTITY-MIB / ENTITY-SENSOR-MIB / LLDP-MIB / POWER-ETHERNET-MIB / BRIDGE-MIB / Q-BRIDGE-MIB / RSTP-MIB) via the same structure + walk shape as uploaded MIBs — see "Standard MIBs" below.
- `GET    /server-settings/mibs?manufacturer=&model=&scope=all|device|generic` *(admin OR assets-admin)* — List uploaded MIBs (filters: manufacturer + model exact match, scope filters generic vs device-specific).
- `GET    /server-settings/mibs/facets`         *(admin OR assets-admin)* — `{ manufacturers: [], modelsByManufacturer: { mfr: [models] } }` — distinct values from already-uploaded MIBs **plus** the asset inventory, so the upload-form datalists aren't empty before the first vendor MIB is uploaded.
- `GET    /server-settings/mibs/:id`            *(admin OR assets-admin)* — Full record including raw `contents`.
- `GET    /server-settings/mibs/:id/download`   *(admin OR assets-admin)* — `text/plain` download with the original filename.
- `GET    /server-settings/mibs/:id/structure`  *(admin OR assets-admin)* — Parsed object tree for the Browse modal. Returns `{ moduleName, imports[], symbols: MibSymbol[], tables: MibTable[], mibId, manufacturer, model, unresolvedCount, unresolvedRoots[] }`. `unresolvedRoots` (from `oidRegistry.findUnresolvedRootSymbols`, empty when `unresolvedCount` is 0) names the distinct EXTERNAL symbols the file references but nothing defines — the actionable cause behind the count, since a module anchored on an IMPORTed symbol fails at its root and takes every symbol chained off it down too (an operator sees "nothing resolved", not "a few gaps"). The Browse modal's warning banner names them and tells the operator to upload the MIB that defines them. Each `MibSymbol` carries `name`, `parentName`, `oidIndex`, `fullOid` (resolved at the MIB's natural scope; null when a dependency is missing), `kind`, `syntax`, `baseType` (`INTEGER` / `Counter32` / `Gauge32` / `TimeTicks` / `OCTET STRING` / `IpAddress` / `OBJECT IDENTIFIER` / `BITS` / `SEQUENCE` / `SEQUENCE OF` / `OTHER`), `enumValues` (`{label, value}[]` for INTEGER types with named values, e.g. `up(1)/down(2)`), `access`, `status`, `description`, `isTableRow`, `indexNames`. Each `MibTable` carries `name`, `rowSymbol`, `columns` (children of the row in OID arc order), `indexNames`, `description`. Parser lives in `src/services/mibService.ts:parseMibStructured` (peer of `parseMib` so a regression in the heavier parser cannot break uploads); OID resolution is provided by `oidRegistry.resolveSymbolsForMib`. Per-symbol parse failures degrade to "name + parentName known, everything else null" rather than dropping the symbol — operators can still walk it, they just don't get decoding.
- `POST   /server-settings/mibs/:id/walk`       *(admin OR assets-admin)* — MIB-aware SNMP walk. Body: `{ assetId, credentialId, objectName, maxRows? }`. Resolves `objectName` against the MIB's structured parse, walks the asset's IP using the supplied SNMP credential via the same `snmpWalkRaw()` primitive the numeric `/assets/:id/snmp-walk` uses, then post-processes results: each row's OID is matched back against the MIB's symbol map (longest-prefix wins, so a table cell's OID resolves to the column symbol rather than the row), `INTEGER` values whose symbol has `enumValues` are decoded into `up(1)`-style labels, `TimeTicks` are rendered as human duration. Response shape: `{ kind: "table" | "scalars", ... , truncated, durationMs, rowCount, decodedCount, host, oid, objectName }`. When every result row's parent matches a single declared `MibTable.rowSymbol`, returns `kind: "table"` with `table: { name, rowSymbol, columns, indexNames, rows: [{ index, cells: { col → {raw, decoded} | null } }] }` so the UI can render a 2D row-per-INDEX grid; otherwise returns `kind: "scalars"` with `entries: [{ oid, symbol, suffix, syntax, baseType, raw, decoded }]`. Each call writes one `asset.snmp_walk` Event with `{ mibId, mibModuleName, objectName, kind, rowCount, decodedCount, truncated, durationMs }` in the details (info on success, warning on probe failure). `decodedCount < rowCount/2` is the operator's hint that the chosen MIB doesn't match the asset's manufacturer — the UI surfaces a yellow banner.
- `POST   /server-settings/mibs`                *(admin)* — `multipart/form-data` upload. Fields: `file` (required), `manufacturer?`, `model?`, `notes?`. The body is parsed by a minimal SMI validator (`mibService.parseMib`) before insert: rejects empty files, files containing NUL/control bytes, anything missing the `<NAME> DEFINITIONS ::= BEGIN ... END` envelope, or files exceeding 1 MB. `moduleName` and `imports` are extracted from the parse and stored on the row. Duplicate `(manufacturer, model, moduleName)` returns 409. Setting `model` without `manufacturer` is a 400 (generic MIBs can't be model-scoped).
- `DELETE /server-settings/mibs/:id`            *(admin)* — Remove a stored MIB.
- `GET    /server-settings/mibs/profile-status` *(admin OR assets-admin)* — Returns one entry per built-in vendor telemetry profile (`{ vendor, matchPattern, example, symbols: [{metric, symbol, resolved, fromModuleName, fromScope}], ready, partial, modelOverrides: [{model, mibCount}] }`). The MIB Database card uses this to render the **Vendor Profile Status** pill. `fromScope` is `"device" | "vendor" | "generic" | "seed"` and reflects which layer of `oidRegistry`'s scoped resolver provided the symbol.

#### Standard MIBs (bundled — RFC/IEEE) — mixed scoping
The eleven canonical SMI/IEEE MIBs the SNMP Walk tab pre-populates in its dropdown (`std:system`, `std:interfaces`, `std:if-ext`, `std:host-resources`, `std:entity`, `std:entity-sensor`, `std:lldp`, `std:poe`, `std:bridge`, `std:q-bridge`, `std:rstp`) ship as text files under [src/services/stdMibs/](src/services/stdMibs/) and load through `stdMibLibrary.ts`. The last four back the switch physical-layer surfaces: `std:poe` is POWER-ETHERNET-MIB (RFC 3621 — per-port PoE detection status + power class; note it defines NO per-port wattage object, only per-PSE consumption), `std:bridge` is BRIDGE-MIB (RFC 4188 — `dot1dTpFdbTable` MAC forwarding, the `dot1dBasePortIfIndex` basePort→ifIndex join every FDB/STP row needs, and `dot1dStp`), `std:q-bridge` is Q-BRIDGE-MIB (RFC 4363 — the VLAN-aware `dot1qTpFdbTable` a VLAN-aware switch populates instead), and `std:rstp` is RSTP-MIB (RFC 4318). Wire shape matches the uploaded variants so the frontend renders the browse tree + MIB-aware walk identically — see [public/js/assets.js](public/js/assets.js) `_loadAndRenderMibTree` + walk dispatch. Routes are static-segment paths declared before the `/:id/*` catchall in `mibs.ts` so `GET /std` doesn't get eaten by `GET /:id`. Read permission requires `mibDatabase` `read` (admin OR assets-admin); the std bundle is read-only (operators upload custom MIBs through the existing uploaded-MIB routes).
- `GET    /server-settings/mibs/std` *(admin OR assets-admin)* — `[{ key, label, moduleName, rootOid }]` for every bundled MIB. Frontend uses this for the dropdown; the existing hardcoded `_SNMP_STANDARD_MIBS` table in `assets.js` is the primary source today, the endpoint exists for tooling that wants a server-authoritative list.
- `GET    /server-settings/mibs/std/:key/structure` *(admin OR assets-admin)* — Same shape as the uploaded `:id/structure` endpoint, plus `mibId: "std:<key>"`, `moduleName`, `manufacturer: null`, `model: null`, `isStandard: true`. `:key` is the std key without the `std:` prefix (e.g. `lldp` not `std:lldp`); the API client `serverSettings.getStdMibStructure(key)` strips the prefix transparently. Returns 404 for unknown keys.
- `POST   /server-settings/mibs/std/:key/walk` *(admin OR assets-admin)* — Same Zod body (`{ assetId, credentialId, objectName, maxRows? }`) and response shape as the uploaded walk endpoint. Looks the operator's `objectName` up in the std MIB's symbol table, resolves to a numeric OID via `BUILT_IN_OIDS` + the std MIB's own resolved-symbol map, and dispatches `snmpWalkRaw` exactly like the uploaded path. Writes the standard `asset.snmp_walk` Event with `details.mibId = "std:<key>"` (audit logs treat the field as opaque — no UUID FK). LLDP-MIB walks are correctness-validated by the named-number resolver fix in `oidRegistry.tryResolveParts` — `lldpRemTable` resolves to `1.0.8802.1.1.2.1.4.1` through ASN.1 `name(value)` syntax in the root anchor.

### Manufacturer Profiles — mixed scoping
Reads (`list`, `get`) open to **admin OR assets-admin**; writes admin-only. Mounted at `/server-settings/manufacturer-profiles` *before* the blanket `serverSettingsSystem` read gate on the rest of `/server-settings`, same precedent as the MIB Database routes. The monitoring path does NOT consume these rows yet — the resolver swap from the hardcoded `VENDOR_TELEMETRY_PROFILES` constant to DB-backed lookup lands in a follow-up commit. This surface owns the operator-editable persistence: list profiles, get one profile in full, create profiles, edit per-metric defaults, manage per-model overrides, manage custom widgets that Slice 7's Custom MIB tab will render.
- `GET    /server-settings/manufacturer-profiles`                  *(admin OR assets-admin)* — `{ profiles: ProfileSummary[], transforms: [{kind, label}], combiners: [{kind, label}] }`. Each summary carries counts of metric rows / overrides / widgets / manufacturer-scoped uploaded MIBs. `transforms` is the unary `TransformKind` registry (paired with `type="scalar"` rows); `combiners` is the binary `CombinerKind` registry (paired with `type="double_scalar"` rows) — the frontend's Transform dropdown swaps option list based on the row's current Type.
- `GET    /server-settings/manufacturer-profiles/suggestions`      *(admin OR assets-admin)* — `{ suggestions: [{ value, sources: ("asset"|"alias"|"oui")[], assetCount }] }` for the card's "+ Add Manufacturer" typeahead. Merges distinct `Asset.manufacturer` (with a device count), `ManufacturerAlias.canonical`, and the `manufacturer` on each static OUI override; every value is alias-canonicalized so the box offers exactly what `POST` would store, values already carrying a profile are dropped, and ordering is device-count desc then alphabetical. The raw IEEE OUI database is deliberately not a contributor. Declared **before `/:id`** so the literal path isn't captured. The box itself stays free text — any custom manufacturer is still accepted.
- `GET    /server-settings/manufacturer-profiles/:id`              *(admin OR assets-admin)* — `{ profile: ProfileFull }` with metric rows, overrides, and custom widgets fully populated.
- `POST   /server-settings/manufacturer-profiles`                  *(admin)* — `{ manufacturer }`. Manufacturer is alias-canonicalized on insert; pre-populates the seven empty metric rows so the modal opens with the full canvas. 409 if a profile for the canonical form already exists.
- `PUT    /server-settings/manufacturer-profiles/:id/metrics/:metricKey`                              *(admin)* — Set this metric row's defaults. Body: `{ defaultSymbol?, defaultSymbolB?, defaultMibId?, defaultMibStdKey?, defaultType?, defaultTransform? }`. The service validates the post-write shape via `validateMetricRowShape` (scalar → symbolB null; double_scalar → both symbols required; table → symbolB+transform null; empty-row state allowed). `defaultTransform` is validated against the matching registry based on `defaultType` — a `CombinerKind` on a `scalar` row (or a `TransformKind` on `double_scalar`) is 400. `defaultMibId` and `defaultMibStdKey` are mutually exclusive — the service rejects requests that try to set both as non-null. `defaultMibStdKey` is validated against the `STD_MIB_KEYS` set; unknown keys are 400'd.
- `POST   /server-settings/manufacturer-profiles/:id/metrics/:metricKey/overrides`                    *(admin)* — Add a per-model override. Body: `{ modelPattern, symbol, symbolB?, mibId?, type?, transform?, order? }`. Same shape validation as the metric row (override rows always require `symbol`; `symbolB` required when `type="double_scalar"`). `modelPattern` is validated as a real regex.
- `PUT    /server-settings/manufacturer-profiles/:id/metrics/:metricKey/overrides/:overrideId`        *(admin)* — Edit.
- `DELETE /server-settings/manufacturer-profiles/:id/metrics/:metricKey/overrides/:overrideId`        *(admin)*.
- `POST   /server-settings/manufacturer-profiles/:id/widgets`     *(admin)* — Add a custom widget. Body: `{ name, symbol, mibId, type?, widgetType, transform?, displayOptions?, order?, modelPattern? }`. `mibId` is REQUIRED — custom widgets always reference an uploaded MIB.
- `PUT    /server-settings/manufacturer-profiles/:id/widgets/:widgetId`  *(admin)* — Edit.
- `DELETE /server-settings/manufacturer-profiles/:id/widgets/:widgetId`  *(admin)*.
- `DELETE /server-settings/manufacturer-profiles/:id`             *(admin)* — Remove the profile (cascades to metric rows, overrides, and widgets). No usage-count refusal yet — the resolver swap is the commit that introduces dependency, today the profile rows are purely additive.

### Device Icons — mixed scoping
Operator-uploaded images that overlay vendor logos on each Device Map topology node's colored status circle. **SVG uploads are transparently rasterized to 512×512 PNG on the way in** via `@resvg/resvg-js` (see `deviceIconService.rasterizeSvgToPng`) and stored as PNG bytes — Cytoscape's `background-image` pipeline can't scale a viewBox-only SVG past the browser's tiny default natural size, so rendering through it leaves the icon stuck at a fixed pixel size and visually anchored upper-left at every zoom. Pre-rasterizing on the server bypasses the whole class of bug, and the `rasterizeStoredSvgIcons` startup job migrates any legacy `image/svg+xml` rows already in the DeviceIcon table. Every icon is keyed to a **manufacturer plus either an asset type or a specific model** — there is no standalone "type-only" / "model-only" / "manufacturer-only" scope, because a "firewall" logo across every vendor would be meaningless. Resolution priority at render time, most-specific-wins: `manufacturer-model: <mfr>/<model>` (specific chassis) → `manufacturer-type: <mfr>/<assetType>` (vendor + role). Both scopes' manufacturer half is canonicalized through the `manufacturerAlias` map so "Fortinet, Inc." and "Fortinet" don't create two rows; the asset's `manufacturer` is canonicalized the same way at resolution time. Type values lowercased; model values preserved as typed. Topology renderer overlays the resolved icon at ~68% of the node so the colored status ring (Up green / Warning amber / Recovering blue / Down red / Unmonitored grey — per the existing five-state machine) stays visible around the logo at a glance. Storage is bytes-in-DB (`DeviceIcon` model). Allowed formats: PNG / JPEG / WebP (256 KB cap) plus SVG (32 KB cap, strict validation). Magic-byte check at upload validates declared mimeType matches actual content for raster formats. **SVG validation is reject-on-pattern, not sanitize** — refusal beats silent rewriting of operator content: the upload must start with `<?xml` or `<svg` (after optional BOM/whitespace) and is rejected outright if any of these patterns is present: `<script>`, `<foreignObject>`, `<iframe>`, `<object>`, `<embed>`, `<!DOCTYPE>`, `<!ENTITY>` (XXE), `<?xml-stylesheet>`, `on*=` event handlers, `javascript:` URLs (entity-escape-aware regex), any external `href`/`xlink:href`/`src` (only in-document `#fragment` refs allowed), `@import` in styles, external `url()` references. Defense-in-depth on the image-serve endpoint: SVG responses get `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` and a strict `Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; style-src 'unsafe-inline'; img-src data:; sandbox` so direct-URL access can't execute anything even if a validator bypass slipped through.
- `GET    /device-icons`                         *(admin)* — List uploaded icons. Each row carries `{ id, scope, key, filename, mimeType, size, uploadedBy, uploadedAt, url }` where `key` is the canonical `"<canonicalManufacturer>/<typeOrModel>"` form and `url` points at the image-serve endpoint below for thumbnail previews.
- `POST   /device-icons`                         *(admin)* — `multipart/form-data` upload. Fields: `file` (required), `scope` ("manufacturer-type"|"manufacturer-model"), `manufacturer` (required; canonicalized via alias map), `typeOrModel` (required; assetType enum value when `scope=manufacturer-type`, free text when `scope=manufacturer-model`). Re-uploading the same canonical key replaces the existing image atomically.
- `DELETE /device-icons/:id`                     *(admin)* — Remove an uploaded icon.
- `GET    /device-icons/:id/image`               *(auth)* — Serves raw bytes with the stored `Content-Type` and `Cache-Control: private, max-age=3600`. SVG responses additionally carry `X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff` + a strict CSP so direct-URL access is locked down. Topology endpoint embeds this URL in each node's `iconUrl` so Cytoscape's `background-image` renders the logo inset over the status-colored node fill (icon at 68% size, centered). Browser HTTP cache deduplicates fetches across re-renders.

## Multi-process architecture

Polaris can run as one process (default) or split across specialized processes
that coordinate through the shared PostgreSQL + pg-boss queue (the SolarWinds
Orion model: many supervised services + a grouping wrapper). The role is chosen
by `POLARIS_ROLE`; capability gating lives in `src/utils/role.ts` (`roleConfig`),
and `src/app.ts` branches on the capability flags at boot.

| Role | Boots | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `all` (default, unset) | everything | Local dev (`npm run dev`) — runs everything in one process for fast iteration. Not a production deployment target since Phase 3 (no `polaris.service` unit is shipped). |
| `web` | Express/HTTPS/agent-WS, **all singleton schedulers**, one-shot migrations, pg-boss **producer** connection, **sample/probe write buffers** (the Polaris Agent `/samples` + `/probe-now` endpoints ingest here, so the web role must run the flush tick or agent-sourced rows never persist) | Single instance — the control plane. Owns the in-app updater (restarts the whole group). |
| `monitor` | pg-boss **monitor-queue consumers** + floating pool, sample/probe write buffers | Run **N replicas** — pg-boss hands each job to exactly one worker, so replicas never double-execute. |
| `discovery` | pg-boss **discovery-queue consumer** (`runDiscovery`) | Executes discovery runs off the `polaris-discovery-run` queue. |

**Discovery is queue-backed.** `triggerDiscovery` (route + scheduler) validates,
upserts a `queued` `DiscoveryRun`, and `publishDiscoveryJob`s to the
`polaris-discovery-run` queue (singletonKey = integrationId → one active run per
integration). The discovery worker runs `runDiscovery`, transitioning the
`DiscoveryRun` row (queued → running → completed/aborted/error) and flushing a
progress accumulator to it; the web process reads that row for the
`/discoveries` endpoint, `isDiscoveryRunning`, the slow-run check, and renders
cancel by setting `cancelRequested` (the worker polls it → aborts its local
AbortController). When pg-boss is off (cursor mode), `triggerDiscovery` runs
`runDiscovery` in-process — the single code path across topologies. See
`src/services/discoveryRunState.ts` and `DiscoveryRun` in the domain model.

**Cancel has two tiers.** The abort signal is observed natively by every HTTP
transport under discovery (fgRequest 15s cap, FMG rpc 10s cap + bounded
retries, geocoder 8s) and cooperatively by `syncDhcpSubnets`, which throws
`DiscoveryAbortError` at each `phaseMark` boundary (`utils/errors.ts` —
`name="AbortError"` so the terminal handler counts the run as aborted, not
errored; the `__end__` mark is exempt so a fully-committed sync isn't
discarded). For wedges the signal cannot reach — a Prisma query blocked on a
Postgres lock has no statement timeout, ignores the signal, and keeps the 60s
heartbeat ticking so the reaper never fires either (prod incident 2026-07-20:
one FortiGate held a run "running" 5+ hours through a cancel) —
`discoveryCancelWatchdog` is armed on abort and disarmed in runDiscovery's
finally: if the run hasn't unwound 2 minutes after abort, it logs the stuck
devices, finalizes the row `aborted`, writes `integration.discover.force_exit`,
and exits 1 so systemd/NSSM restarts the process (same exit-and-restart pattern
as the operator /restart endpoint). Under `all`/cursor-mode-fallback the exit
takes the whole process — matching /restart semantics. If pg-boss redelivers
the interrupted job, runDiscovery sees `cancelRequested` still set at startup
and aborts cleanly.

**Singletons** (monitor producer ticks, discovery scheduler, reconcilers,
rollups, prune, one-shot migrations) are pinned to `web`/`all` so they run in
exactly one process; monitor/discovery stay pure consumers.

**Connection budgeting.** Each process opens its own Prisma + pg-boss pool, so
the group footprint ≈ `(monitor replicas + 2) × per-process pool`. Size so it
stays under Postgres `max_connections` (PgBouncer absorbs the Prisma pools but
pg-boss pools always hit Postgres directly). Each process emits
`polaris_db_pool_role_capacity{role}`; the Capacity Advisor's max_connections
model multiplies by `POLARIS_MONITOR_REPLICAS` (and `peakObserved` is already
group-wide via `pg_stat_activity`).

**Deployment.** systemd: `polaris-migrate.service` (oneshot, sole migrator) →
`polaris-web.service` / `polaris-monitor@.service` (templated, N) /
`polaris-discovery.service`, grouped by `polaris.target` (`systemctl start
polaris.target`). Docker: one image, per-service `POLARIS_ROLE`, a one-shot
`migrate` compose service the app services gate on, plus an `nginx` service
fronting the stack. The single-process `polaris.service` unit was removed
in Phase 3 — every fresh install via `deploy/setup-*.sh` lands the split-role
+ nginx layout. The `all` role still exists in `src/utils/role.ts` so
`npm run dev` keeps working; it's a runtime mode, not a production
deployment target. See [docs/INSTALL.md](docs/INSTALL.md).

**Per-role metrics endpoint.** prom-client registries are per-process. The
web role exposes `/metrics` on its main HTTPS listener; monitor and discovery
boot a standalone HTTP listener via [src/utils/metricsServer.ts](src/utils/metricsServer.ts)
when `POLARIS_METRICS_PORT` is set. The shipped unit files pin the monitor
template to `910N` (instance N → 9101/9102/…) and discovery to `9110`, both
on `127.0.0.1`. Prometheus must scrape every role endpoint or panels that
depend on consumer-stamped metrics (`polaris_probe_*`, `polaris_monitor_work_duration_seconds`,
`polaris_sample_write_duration_seconds`, `polaris_discovery_*`,
`polaris_fmg_worker_queue_depth` / `_inflight`) silently show no data on the
Grafana dashboard. Dashboard queries already `sum()` across instances, so
panels populate as soon as the scrape job is complete. See
[docs/grafana/README.md](docs/grafana/README.md) for an example scrape job.

**nginx-front HTTPS (only mode post-Phase-4).** nginx terminates TLS for the lifetime of the install. Polaris listens HTTP-only on `127.0.0.1:${PORT:-3000}` and reads nginx's cert at `POLARIS_PROXY_CERT_PATH` to surface the fingerprint each Polaris Agent pins. `POLARIS_PUBLIC_URL` is required — [src/utils/runtimeConfig.ts](src/utils/runtimeConfig.ts) fails fast at boot if it's missing. [src/utils/proxyMode.ts](src/utils/proxyMode.ts) is the single lazy check (no module-load caching, so Vitest tests + runtime config reloads see fresh state). [src/utils/trustProxy.ts](src/utils/trustProxy.ts) resolves the Express `trust proxy` setting — operator override > default `"1"` (first-hop trust) — without mutating `process.env`. [src/services/certInfo.ts](src/services/certInfo.ts) reads the PEM from disk with a layered cache keyed on file-content hash and last-known-good fallback that survives certbot-style atomic-rename windows; public API (`getServerCertFingerprint`, `getServerCertHostnames`, `getServerCertExpiry`) is consumed by the agent-install path and `GET /server-settings/https`. [src/utils/publicUrl.ts](src/utils/publicUrl.ts) parses `POLARIS_PUBLIC_URL` to derive the public-facing port stamped into agent.conf. The nginx reference config at [deploy/nginx/polaris.conf](deploy/nginx/polaris.conf) ships HTTP/2 + HTTP/3 listeners (TCP/443 + UDP/443) on the same vhost with `Alt-Svc` advertising HTTP/3 to browsers; requires nginx ≥ 1.25 (setup scripts pull from nginx.org's mainline repo if RHEL AppStream is older). Fresh installs land split-role + nginx + a self-signed cert via [deploy/setup-rhel.sh](deploy/setup-rhel.sh) / [setup-ubuntu.sh](deploy/setup-ubuntu.sh); existing installs use [deploy/migrate-to-nginx.sh](deploy/migrate-to-nginx.sh).

**Phase 2 dual-pin** lifts the "fleet-wide re-install on every cert rotation" caveat. Each `ManagedAgent` row carries `serverCertFingerprint` (canonical) + `additionalServerCertFingerprints String[]` (staged). The union is the agent's trust set; rotation is operator-driven via the Maintenance card's "Cert pin rotation" pane (`POST /server-settings/agents/cert-pins/bulk-add` and `/bulk-remove`). The agent.conf format gained `cert_fingerprints = pin1,pin2,...` (Go agent parses the union; pre-Phase-2 binaries still read the legacy `cert_fingerprint` line for downgrade safety). When the operator stages a new pin, the server pushes via WS `refresh-config` and online agents apply within seconds (offline agents pick it up on next /config poll); agents Save() the new pin set + exit via `os.Exit(0)` so systemd cycles the process with the new pin set live. See cross-cutting/polaris-agent → "Cert pin rotation" in [TOUCHES.md](TOUCHES.md) for the full lockstep checklist.

**In-app nginx GUI (Server Settings → Certificates).** Operator-facing GUI for six nginx directives (HTTPS listen port, HTTP/3 toggle, TLS protocols, HSTS, Prometheus allow-list — plus cert rotation via the dual-pin stage→swap→retire workflow). Trust model: the polaris OS user has narrow sudo via `/etc/sudoers.d/polaris-nginx` granting only `/usr/local/sbin/polaris-nginx-apply` (shipped as [deploy/scripts/polaris-nginx-apply.sh](deploy/scripts/polaris-nginx-apply.sh)). Subcommands take NO user-supplied paths — staged files live at hardcoded `/run/polaris-nginx-stage/` locations set up by `/etc/tmpfiles.d/polaris-nginx.conf`, and the wrapper holds `flock /run/polaris-nginx-apply.lock` + `timeout 30` for every op. Setup scripts (setup-rhel.sh + setup-rhel-nodb.sh + setup-ubuntu.sh + setup-ubuntu-nodb.sh + migrate-to-nginx.sh) install the wrapper/sudoers/tmpfiles and add the polaris user to the nginx group (or Ubuntu's `www-data` group) so the existing fingerprint pane reads the `0640 root:nginx` cert file directly; existing installs pick the same helpers up through [src/services/updateService.ts](src/services/updateService.ts)'s sync block on every in-app update.

The shipped reference config at [deploy/nginx/polaris.conf](deploy/nginx/polaris.conf) is mirrored by a template at [deploy/nginx/polaris.conf.template](deploy/nginx/polaris.conf.template) that Polaris renders from an operator-settable `proxyConfig` Setting row plus env-derived server_name / upstream port. [src/services/nginxRenderer.ts](src/services/nginxRenderer.ts) substitutes the placeholder tokens and emits the rendered file + sha256 (used downstream for drift detection). [src/services/nginxConfigParser.ts](src/services/nginxConfigParser.ts) is the bootstrap-only counterpart: regex-based extraction of the same six directives out of a live `/etc/nginx/conf.d/polaris.conf` so first boot of this feature seeds the `proxyConfig` row from whatever the operator already has on disk (rather than auto-clobbering). `ProxyConfig` shape lives in [src/types/proxyConfig.ts](src/types/proxyConfig.ts). [src/services/proxyConfigService.ts](src/services/proxyConfigService.ts) is the Setting-table accessor (cached, validated; rejects HTTP/3-with-TLS-1.2-only, port out of 1..65535, etc.). [src/services/privilegedSysadmin.ts](src/services/privilegedSysadmin.ts) wraps the sudo call with output capture + timeout. [src/services/nginxApplyService.ts](src/services/nginxApplyService.ts) is the orchestrator: `applyProxyConfig` renders + stages + sudoes the wrapper + records sha256; `rotateCertAndKey` does libcrypto SPKI cert+key pair validation, atomic-renames, invalidates [src/services/certInfo.ts](src/services/certInfo.ts)'s cache via the new `invalidateCache()` export; `preflightCertRotation` returns the new cert metadata + the current canonical fingerprint (so the GUI knows which old pin to retire via the existing `/agents/cert-pins/bulk-remove` after rotation); `bootstrapProxyConfig` runs once at boot via [src/jobs/bootstrapProxyConfig.ts](src/jobs/bootstrapProxyConfig.ts) (no-op outside proxy mode or when the row already exists); `getDriftStatus` compares the live file hash to `lastAppliedHash` for the refuse-and-banner UX. Beyond the six operator-settable directives the shipped config also carries request-body limits that are NOT operator-settable: `client_max_body_size 8m` at the server level (nginx's 1m default sat below the app's own per-route ceilings and 413'd them at the edge) plus a dedicated `location` for `/api/v1/server-settings/database/restore` that lifts the limit (`0`) and sets `proxy_request_buffering off`, since a restore is a whole-database `pg_dump` streamed to disk with no `fileSize` of its own. That block is why `nginxConfigParser` expects **8** location blocks — see TOUCHES.md → cross-cutting/deployment for the lockstep rule.

Routes live in [src/api/routes/proxySettings.ts](src/api/routes/proxySettings.ts), mounted at `/api/v1/server-settings/proxy/*` ABOVE the blanket `serverSettingsSystem:read` gate so each route declares its own permission level (read on GET, fullwrite on PUT / `/apply` / `/adopt-managed-mode` / `/cert/preflight` / `/cert/rotate`). The cert rotation flow is orchestrated by the frontend modal in [public/js/server-settings.js](public/js/server-settings.js)'s `openRotateCertModal`: it calls `/cert/preflight` (libcrypto validate + return new metadata) → `/agents/cert-pins/bulk-add` (stage the new pin on every active agent so they accept both old + new while reconnecting) → `/cert/rotate` (sudo wrapper atomic-renames the cert files + reloads nginx) → `/agents/cert-pins/bulk-remove` (retire the old pin once uptake is verified). Adopt-managed-mode gate: `proxyConfig.managedMode` starts at `false` on every install; the GUI shows a yellow drift banner (with drift markers from the regex parser) and disables the controls until the operator clicks "Adopt managed mode." In-app updates render the template only when `managedMode=true` and refuse-to-clobber on sha256-drift.
